synergy.reason: Alessio's smoke hides allies too, so Lian Po can close the distance before anyone sees him coming.
Arli can keep hitting whatever Lian Po launches, so her Maple stacks reach the detonation easily.

counters.reason: Diaochan blinks away again and again, so Lian Po's dashes never manage to catch her.
Marco Polo's Destroyed Defense lets his shots deal true damage, so Lian Po's armor counts for nothing.

passive.description:
Lian Po has crowd control immunity while using his skills.
When in combat, Lian Po gains Battle Spirit continuously, and his Basic Attacks and skills grant more Battle Spirit on hit. Battle Spirit provides 0-20% damage reduction (based on the value of Battle Spirit). At max Battle Spirit, his Attack Speed is increased by 30%.
When out of combat, Battle Spirit diminishes over time, and is converted to 70 (70 + 1.5% extra Health) Health recovery each time it diminishes, for up to 10 times in total.
passive.name: Warrior's Soul

skill1.description:
Lian Po dashes in the target direction, dealing 55 (55 + 15% extra physical attack) physical damage to enemies in his path and launching them for 0.5s. He also deals 5% of the target's Health as physical damage to heroes and 183 (5% of his Health) as physical damage to non-hero units.
Passive: Lian Po's every third Basic Attack is a heavy strike that deals 250 (250 + 100% extra physical attack) extra physical damage.
skill1.name: Burst Ram

skill2.description:
Lian Po charges up and slams the ground, gaining a shield that negates 360 (360 + 8.5% extra Health) damage for 5s. While charging, he slows enemies within range by 15% and pulls non-hero enemies toward him.
After 1s, the ground splits, dealing 325 (325 + 85% extra physical attack) physical damage to enemies. Enemies closer to the epicenter take more damage, up to an extra 100%. If any enemies are within range when charging begins, Skill 1's Cooldown is reset.
He can use other skills while using Skill 2.
skill2.name: Magma Slam

skill3.description:
Lian Po leaps to the target location and hammers the ground 3 times. The direction of each strike can be adjusted using the movement wheel.
Strike 1: He deals 200 (200 + 50% extra physical attack) physical damage to enemies within range and slows them by 15% for 1s. Enemies in the center take an extra (60% extra physical attack) physical damage.
Strike 2: He deals 400 (400 + 100% extra physical attack) physical damage to enemies within range and slows them by 30% for 1s. Enemies in the center take an extra (90% extra physical attack) physical damage.
Strike 3: He deals 600 (600 + 150% extra physical attack) physical damage to enemies within range and launches them for 1s. He also deals 10% of the target's Health as physical damage to heroes and 10% of his Health as physical damage to non-hero units. Enemies in the center take an extra (150% extra physical attack) physical damage.
He can use Skill 1 while his Ultimate is in effect.
skill3.name: Tremor Smash

strategy.earlyGame: Lian Po's Battle Spirit only starts building once a fight begins. His damage reduction is small at the start, so early trades should be short ones built from the Burst Ram dash and the heavy strike on every third Basic Attack, not long brawls. Magma Slam pulls minions toward its center, and enemies closer to the center take more damage, so it clears waves in one go. When you get chipped, step out of combat for a moment: Battle Spirit turns into Health and you recover without leaving the lane.
strategy.midGame: Once he learns Tremor Smash, Lian Po can start fights himself. He leaps to a spot and strikes three times, steering each strike, so the first two slows can close escape routes before the third-strike launch goes onto the real target. He has crowd control immunity while his skills are active, so enemies waiting for his landing cannot stop him with CC. Burst Ram is still usable during the ultimate, which lets him chase anyone who steps out of range. Win or lose, leave combat afterward. Battle Spirit turns back into Health, so you don't head to the next objective already worn down. The 21 October update lowered the damage of both Magma Slam and Tremor Smash a little.
strategy.teamfight: Use Tremor Smash to clear the enemy front line and land where you can catch two or more of them. Start charging Magma Slam the moment you land. If enemies are in range, Burst Ram comes back, and the slow during the charge delays their scatter. Magma Slam only pulls non-hero units, so putting heroes at the center of the blast means stepping in yourself. Dash, charge, dash again: draw their attacks onto yourself while splitting their formation. When your Health runs low, back off, let Battle Spirit turn into Health, then return.

combos.title: Three-Slam Pin
combos.sequence: Skill 3 (Tremor Smash: first and second strikes slow) → Skill 1 (Burst Ram: dash back in during the strikes) → Skill 3 (third strike launches) → Skill 2 (Magma Slam)
combos.description: Each strike of Tremor Smash can be steered, so place the first two slows where the target wants to run. Burst Ram stays usable during the ultimate, so if they slip out, dash back in and land the third-strike launch on them. Start Magma Slam's charge while they are in the air, and with an enemy in range Burst Ram comes back once more.

combos.title: Cooldown Reset Loop
combos.sequence: Skill 2 (Magma Slam: charge next to enemies, gain a shield) → Skill 1 (Burst Ram: dash and launch) → Basic Attack (third hit is the heavy strike)
combos.description: Starting Magma Slam's charge with an enemy nearby refreshes Burst Ram on the spot. Other skills stay usable during the charge, so he can dash in for another launch while waiting for the blast. Every third Basic Attack is a heavy strike, which is the reason to keep hitting after the blast.

strengths: Crowd control immunity during skills lets him engage without being interrupted
Battle Spirit builds as a fight drags on, steadily cutting the damage he takes
Charging Magma Slam next to enemies refreshes Burst Ram, so he can dash in again
Leaving combat converts Battle Spirit into Health, so he gets back into the next fight quickly
weaknesses: Battle Spirit is low when a fight begins, so his damage reduction is small at first
Magma Slam's blast comes after the charge, giving mobile enemies time to step out
Magma Slam only pulls non-hero units; enemy heroes have to be caught by his own positioning
Tremor Smash saves its launch and biggest hit for the third strike, so stopping short wastes most of it

playstyle.style: A tank who has crowd control immunity while using his skills, so enemy CC cannot stop him mid-cast. Battle Spirit builds up the longer a fight lasts and reduces the damage he takes. Out of combat it turns into Health recovery, which lets him leave and rejoin the front line again and again.
playstyle.suited: Lian Po shows his strength the longer he keeps a fight going. The key routine is starting Magma Slam's charge next to enemies to refresh Burst Ram, then dashing in again, all in the middle of a brawl. Players who don't mind re-entering over and over will find him easier than those who want to settle things in one short exchange.

synergy.reason: Guiguzi drags enemies into a clump and stuns them, so Xiao Qiao's meteors keep raining on stationary targets.
Donghuang suppresses a hero in place, so Xiao Qiao's Blossoming Fan lands its full first hit.

counters.reason: Han Xin is immune to crowd control during his ultimate, so Honeysweet Breeze's knockup does nothing.
Mozi stacks a shield with every skill he casts, so Blossoming Fan's first hit is absorbed outright.

passive.description: Xiao Qiao gains 25% Movement Speed for 2s on skill hit.
passive.name: Encouraging Thoughts

skill1.description: Xiao Qiao tosses a spinning fan in the target direction that returns to her after reaching its max range, dealing damage to enemies in its path and again on its way back. The first enemy hit takes 585 (585 + 80% magical attack) magical damage. Damage is reduced by 20% with each subsequent hit, down to 50% of the initial damage.
skill1.name: Blossoming Fan

skill2.description: Xiao Qiao summons a whirlwind in the target location, dealing 300 (300 +50% magical attack) magical damage to enemies within range and launching them for 1.5s.
skill2.name: Honeysweet Breeze

skill3.description:
Xiao Qiao calls down meteors for 6s. Meteors randomly target a nearby enemy, dealing 400 (400 + 100% magical attack) magical damage. The meteors prioritize enemy heroes.
Her passive skill effect is activated during the skill's duration. Each enemy can be hit by up to 4 meteors, but subsequent hits deal 50% less damage.
skill3.name: Meteor Storm

strategy.earlyGame: Early on, the line you throw Blossoming Fan along decides both your wave clear and your poke. The fan flies to max range, comes back, and hits on both trips. Each enemy it hits first lowers the damage to the next, so when aiming at your opponent, throw the moment they step out of the minion line. Honeysweet Breeze can poke too, but for a hero without a movement skill it is also her defense when the enemy jungler closes in.
strategy.midGame: Once she learns her Ultimate, there is one more skill to stack after Honeysweet Breeze lands. If the whirlwind misses, go back to poking with the fan and wait for the next one. Meteors fall on nearby enemies and prioritize heroes, so as long as you are in range you don't need to aim them. Her passive speed stays on while the meteors fall, letting her move and adjust distance as she casts. After pushing the wave, use the speed from landed skills to head to fights in another lane.
strategy.teamfight: Xiao Qiao's teamfight starts with Blossoming Fan thrown from behind her allies. The first enemy the fan hits takes the most damage, so pick a line where your priority target is in front. Meet anyone who dives you with Honeysweet Breeze, cast Meteor Storm while they are airborne, and fall back toward your team. If you are the one attacking, drop the whirlwind where enemies have stopped against your frontline, then stack the meteors and the fan on top.

combos.title: Stack Everything on the Knock-Up
combos.sequence: Skill 2 (Honeysweet Breeze: knock-up) → Skill 3 (Meteor Storm: meteors) → Skill 1 (Blossoming Fan: out and back)
combos.description: This order spends the rest only after confirming the whirlwind landed. Enemies can't move while airborne, so both passes of the fan land on the same target while the meteors fall.

combos.title: Chip With the Returning Fan
combos.sequence: Skill 1 (Blossoming Fan: hit on the way out) → use the speed to sidestep → the fan's return hits the same enemy
combos.description: Repositioning with the speed boost right after the hit puts your target back on the fan's return path.

combos.title: Answer a Dive
combos.sequence: Skill 2 (Honeysweet Breeze: launch the diver) → Skill 1 (Blossoming Fan) → Skill 3 (Meteor Storm: cast it and fall back)
combos.description: With no movement skill, the whirlwind is also her way out. Launch the diver, hit them with the fan, then retreat toward your team while the meteors fall. Her passive speed stays on during Meteor Storm, so she can open distance even while backing off.

strengths: Blossoming Fan hits on the way out and on the way back, chipping twice per throw
Each skill hit raises her Movement Speed, keeping her quick while she keeps landing them
Honeysweet Breeze's knock-up works both to start a fight and to defend herself
Meteor Storm prioritizes nearby enemy heroes, so it lands without precise aiming
weaknesses: No blink or dash; her defense is limited to Honeysweet Breeze and her speed boost
Blossoming Fan loses damage with each enemy it hits, so anyone after the first takes less
Using Honeysweet Breeze on offense leaves her thin on self-defense until it returns
Meteor Storm can't choose its target and falls on nearby enemies at random

playstyle.style: Xiao Qiao has no movement skill, so she protects herself with two things: Honeysweet Breeze's knock-up and the speed she gains from landing skills. Her main damage comes from Blossoming Fan, a fan that flies out and back and hits enemies both ways. Her Ultimate, Meteor Storm, keeps dropping meteors on nearby enemies, and her passive speed boost stays on the whole time.
playstyle.suited: Her speed rises the more skills she lands, so she suits players who can keep up the rhythm of hit, move, hit again. Each fight asks whether to spend Honeysweet Breeze on offense or save it for self-defense.

synergy.reason: Mai Shiranui launches enemies into the air, so Zilong's Skysplitter lands on targets that cannot move.
Zhang Fei leaps in after Zilong's dive and shields him deep in the enemy line.

counters.reason: Liang lines Zilong's dash paths with barriers, and touching any of them stuns him on the spot.
Mozi's barrier keeps stunning whatever touches it, and Zilong has to stand in melee to finish his jabs.

passive.description:
Zilong gets stronger the more he fights. As his Health declines, his potential is triggered: he enjoys greater damage reduction, and his basic skills are enhanced.
Hidden Dragon: When his Health is more than 70% and less than or equal to 100%, he gains 5% damage reduction.
Dragon Portent: When his Health is more than 40% and less than or equal to 70%, he gains 10% damage reduction.
Dragon in Flight: When his Health is more than 0% and less than or equal to 40%, he gains 20% damage reduction.
Any Health in excess of the current bracket will be converted into a permanent shield. When a shield Health bracket is full, excess shield value will be converted into Health instead.
passive.name: Dragon's Roar

skill1.description:
Zilong charges forward with his spear, dealing 350 (350 + 120% extra physical attack) physical damage.
The next Basic Attack is enhanced and deals an extra 120 (120 + 40% extra physical attack) physical damage and slows the enemy by 25% for 2s.
This skill's cooldown is reset each time his Health enters a new bracket.
Dash distance increases with skill level.
skill1.name: Thunderbreaker

skill2.description: Zilong jabs 5 times, with each jab dealing 180 (180 + 65% extra physical attack) physical damage to enemies hit and restoring 65 (65 + 2.5% extra Health) Health. The effect of each subsequent jab is reduced by 8%.
skill2.name: Stormpiercer

skill3.description:
Zilong leaps into the air and unleashes a lightning strike, dealing 480 (480 + 145% extra physical attack) physical damage to enemies within range and applying an induction mark. Skill hits within 5s on marked targets deal 30 (30 + 10% extra physical attack) magical damage, and launch enemies in the center of the area for 1s.
50% of the cooldown is returned if no enemy heroes are hit.
skill3.name: Skysplitter

strategy.earlyGame: Zilong keeps his Health up with Stormpiercer's healing as he clears the jungle. Dragon's Roar raises his damage reduction as his Health falls, and every bracket change lets him use Thunderbreaker again, so a wounded Zilong actually fights better. At full Health, though, his damage reduction stays small. When he meets the enemy jungler while healthy, pick a fight where he does not take the big hits first. Healing beyond his current bracket becomes a shield, so using Stormpiercer near full Health never wastes the healing.
strategy.midGame: Skysplitter returns half its cooldown if it hits no enemy hero. A miss costs little, so once he has his ultimate he can gank more often. The 21 October update lowered the base damage of both Stormpiercer and Skysplitter, so finishing a target now takes more hits than before.
strategy.teamfight: Zilong leaps in after your front line has gone first. Once the enemy has spent stuns and knock-ups on your team, leap onto a soft target with Skysplitter and layer Stormpiercer and Thunderbreaker on the marked enemy. Damage reduction rises as his Health falls and Stormpiercer's healing and shields stack on top, so the longer the brawl lasts, the harder Zilong is to take down. Only against a team with healing reduction should you stop counting on that staying power.

combos.title: Layering the Induction Mark
combos.sequence: Skill 3 (Skysplitter: leap in and apply the induction mark) → Skill 1 (Thunderbreaker: dash for bonus magic damage) → Basic Attack (empowered, with a slow) → Skill 2 (Stormpiercer: heal on each jab)
combos.description: For a short time after Skysplitter marks a target, every skill that hits them adds bonus magical damage. Follow the leap straight away with Thunderbreaker and Stormpiercer, and use the enhanced attack's slow to keep them from getting away.

combos.title: Bracket-Break Trade
combos.sequence: Skill 1 (Thunderbreaker: dash) → Basic Attack (empowered, with a slow) → Skill 2 (Stormpiercer: heal on each jab) → Skill 1 (Thunderbreaker: exit or re-engage once the bracket changes)
combos.description: Dash in, blunt their reply with the enhanced attack's slow, then drive in the jabs. When his Health crosses into a new bracket mid-trade, Thunderbreaker becomes available again, so right after getting chunked he can choose to chase or leave. While healing reduction is on him, use it to leave rather than to stay.

strengths: Damage reduction rises as his Health falls, so he holds on from low Health
Skysplitter returns half its cooldown if it hits no enemy hero
Stormpiercer's healing, plus overheal turning into shields, wins long trades
Entering a new Health bracket lets him use Thunderbreaker again, for a chase or an exit
weaknesses: Damage reduction is small at full Health, leaving him exposed to opening burst
His approach relies on Thunderbreaker and Skysplitter; slows and stuns that stop him keep him from fighting
Healing reduction cuts into Stormpiercer's healing and the shields it feeds

playstyle.style: Zilong is a jungle fighter whose damage reduction rises as his Health falls. Stormpiercer heals him with every jab, and healing past his current bracket stays as a permanent shield, so the longer a trade runs, the harder he is to put down.
playstyle.suited: As his Health drops, you have to decide whether to back off or hold your ground by watching Dragon's Roar's brackets. Players who can stay calm in low-Health exchanges get the most out of that resilience. You also need the judgment to avoid being burst down from full Health.

synergy.reason: Guiguzi drags enemies into one spot, so Mozi's self-centered barrier keeps stunning all of them.
Dyadia's snares pin the target in place, so Mozi's Cannon Blast is easy to land.

counters.reason: Standing in the river, Dolia heals nonstop and her Ode shoves Mozi away.
Nezha's Universe Ring reveals Mozi anywhere, letting Skyfall dive on him from across the map.

passive.description:
Every 4th Basic Attack is enhanced, dealing 450 (450 + 70% magical attack) magical damage to enemies within range and knocking them back for 0.75s.
Whenever he uses a skill, he gains 1 stack of shield for 3s, for up to 3 stacks. Each stack negates 300 (300 + 35% magical attack) damage.
passive.name: Fight for Peace

skill1.description: Mozi dashes in the target direction, dealing 250 (250 +38% magical attack) magical damage to enemies in his path and enhancing his next Basic Attack.
skill1.name: Peacebringer

skill2.description:
Mozi fires a shell in the target direction. The shell explodes upon hitting an enemy or reaching its max range, leaving behind an electrified crater.
The explosion deals 525 (525 +45% magical attack) magical damage to enemies within range and stuns them for 1s.
The electrified crater lasts for 4s and deals 50 (50 +5% magical attack) magical damage to enemies within range every 0.5s.
skill2.name: Cannon Blast

skill3.description: Mozi creates an energy barrier around himself that lasts for up to 3.3s. Every 0.5s, it deals 200 (200 +45% magical attack) magical damage and stuns enemies it touches.
skill3.name: Think Inside the Box

strategy.earlyGame: Whether Mozi lands Cannon Blast decides who controls the mid lane. The shell explodes on the first enemy it hits, so aim for moments when the opponent steps up for a last hit with nothing between you. If the stun lands, dash in with Peacebringer and follow with the enhanced Basic Attack. Peacebringer and the fourth-hit enhanced attack handle the wave, and every skill cast stacks a shield, so he can stay in small trades without backing off.
strategy.midGame: Away from lane, Cannon Blast becomes the signal for your team to start a fight. When your jungler is close and the shell lands, the stun gives them time to arrive while the crater keeps chipping the target. Think Inside the Box puts a barrier around him that stuns anyone touching it again and again, which suits narrow corridors and bush exits where enemies come to him. Shields stack with each cast but do not last long. In standoffs before Tyrant or Overlord, wait while looking for an angle that lets the shell through.
strategy.teamfight: Fire Cannon Blast from a distance and let your team focus whoever it stuns. If it misses, don't step forward; chip the front line with Peacebringer and the enhanced Basic Attacks while you wait for the next shell. When enemies head for your back line, put up Think Inside the Box in their path. Enemies touching the barrier stay stunned, so the tighter the space, the harder it is for them to get through. Casting skills back to back also stacks the shields, so he can hold out for a moment when enemies reach him.

combos.title: Shell, Dash, Then Barrier
combos.sequence: Skill 2 (Cannon Blast: explosion stuns) → Skill 1 (Peacebringer: dash and enhance the next Basic Attack) → Basic Attack (enhanced hit) → Skill 3 (Think Inside the Box: stun on touch)
combos.description: Dashing in with Peacebringer while the shell's stun lasts lets the enhanced Basic Attack reach the target. Putting up Think Inside the Box there keeps stunning anyone touching the barrier. Three skills have been cast by this point, so the shields have stacked up as well.

combos.title: Answering a Dive
combos.sequence: Basic Attack (fourth hit knocks back) → Skill 3 (Think Inside the Box: barrier stuns) → Skill 1 (Peacebringer: dash away)
combos.description: The fourth, enhanced Basic Attack knocks back nearby enemies, opening a gap between Mozi and whoever reached him. With Think Inside the Box up next, anyone who comes back and touches the barrier is stunned. Dashing away with Peacebringer during that time puts distance between him and the chasers.

strengths: A landed Cannon Blast shell stuns enemies from a distance
Every skill cast adds a shield stack, so casting more keeps him alive longer
Enemies touching the Think Inside the Box barrier keep getting stunned
The electrified crater left by Cannon Blast keeps damaging enemies for a while
weaknesses: Cannon Blast explodes on the first enemy it hits, so someone standing in front of your target sets it off early
Peacebringer's dash is his only movement skill, so he struggles to get away once caught
Think Inside the Box forms only around him and cannot reach distant enemies
The shields do not last long and fade when he goes a while without casting

playstyle.style: Mozi stops enemies with two kinds of stun: the shell from Cannon Blast and the barrier from Think Inside the Box. He gains a shield stack every time he uses a skill, so the more he casts, the harder he is to bring down. Every fourth Basic Attack turns into an area hit with a knockback, which also pushes away anyone who walks up to him.
playstyle.suited: Cannon Blast explodes on the first enemy it hits, so you need to wait for moments when no one else stands in front of your target. If checking the line before every shot doesn't bother you, a single shell from range can start the fight. Think Inside the Box only forms around him, so each time you choose between waiting for enemies to come to you and stepping in yourself.

synergy.reason: Wukong's enhanced Basic Attack is hard to land, but Daji's stun holds the target still for it.
Arke only crits from behind, and Daji's stun freezes the target long enough for her to get there.

counters.reason: Mulan stacks Balance until it detonates and silences Daji, cutting off her skills entirely.
Gao Changgong strikes out of stealth, and Daji has nothing but her stun to answer with.

passive.description: Every time Daji's skills deal damage, she places 1 stack of Captivated on the target, for up to 3 stacks. Each stack reduces the enemy's Magical Defense for 3s by 36-72, depending on her level.
passive.name: Captivate

skill1.description: Daji unleashes a soul blast in the target direction, dealing 570 (570 +120% magical attack) magical damage to enemies in its path.
skill1.name: Soul Impact

skill2.description: Daji casts a love spell on an enemy, dealing 285 (285 +66% magical attack) magical damage and stunning them for 1.5s.
skill2.name: Strike a Pose

skill3.description:
Daji releases 5 hearts that attack enemies within range at random, each heart dealing 325 (325 +75% magical attack) magical damage.
When multiple hearts hit the same target, subsequent hearts only deal 50% magical damage.
skill3.name: Heartbreaker

strategy.earlyGame: Until your opponent walks into Strike a Pose range, clear minions with Soul Impact and wait. Before she learns her ultimate, she attacks with the pair of Strike a Pose followed by Soul Impact. The May 28 update gave Soul Impact a cooldown that shortens as the skill levels up. The more points it has, the more casts she gets for both clearing and poking. Once Strike a Pose is used she has nothing left to stop anyone, so the less you know about where the enemy jungler is, the closer to your tower she should fight.
strategy.midGame: Only once she learns her ultimate, Heartbreaker, can all three skills land on a target held by Strike a Pose. Captivate lowers Magical Defense every time a skill deals damage, so the later a skill comes in the sequence, the harder it hits. After pushing the wave, slide to a side lane, wait in a bush, and catch whoever steps forward. The hearts fly at random enemies in range, so choosing moments with few other enemies around your target sends more of the damage where you want it. With her skills spent, she has no way to stop anyone until Strike a Pose comes back. Take the kill and leave rather than lingering.
strategy.teamfight: In a head-on teamfight, Heartbreaker's hearts scatter onto frontliners too, so her damage struggles to gather on the target you want. Daji does her best work against an enemy who dives into your backline or one who stands apart from their team. Using Strike a Pose at the start leaves her without protection, so hold it until you have decided who it is for. Stop the diver and finish them, and you protect your backline while bringing their numbers down.

combos.title: Stun, Then Layer All Three
combos.sequence: Skill 2 (Strike a Pose: stuns one enemy) → Skill 3 (Heartbreaker: hearts) → Skill 1 (Soul Impact: saved for last)
combos.description: Captivate lowers Magical Defense every time a skill deals damage, so the heavy single hit of Soul Impact goes last.

combos.title: Catch the Last-Hit
combos.sequence: Skill 2 (Strike a Pose) → Skill 1 (Soul Impact) → back off
combos.description: When your opponent stops to take a last hit, throw Strike a Pose. Land Soul Impact while they are stunned, then stay out of reach of their skills until Strike a Pose is ready again.

strengths: Strike a Pose is cast on a chosen enemy and stuns them
Each skill hit lowers the target's Magical Defense, so later skills hit harder
Stun first, then layer the other skills: the sequence is easy to follow
Soul Impact damages every enemy along its path
weaknesses: Heartbreaker's hearts pick random enemies in range, so crowds pull damage off the target
No mobility skill and no escape beyond Flash
Once her skills are spent, nothing protects her until Strike a Pose returns

playstyle.style: Daji's job starts with stopping one enemy with Strike a Pose. She then layers Heartbreaker and Soul Impact on that target, using the Magical Defense her skills strip away with every hit to finish them off.
playstyle.suited: Her inputs are few; the real decision is who gets Strike a Pose, and when. With no way to escape, how long she survives depends on picking the target before she moves and backing off once her skills are spent.

synergy.reason: Zhang Fei shields his teammates, so Garuda can stand through the whole of Wings of Judgment.
Lian Po's slow and launch pin enemies down, so the arrows of Wings of Judgment keep landing.

counters.reason: Gao Changgong opens from stealth, and his charge hits Garuda before Garuda can shield or reposition.
Han Xin leaps in twice in quick succession, and Garuda's single shield can only cover one of those arrivals.

passive.description: Garuda's Basic Attacks pierce targets and deal 287 (120 + 100% physical attack + 35% magical attack) magical damage. His Basic Attacks deal 50% less damage to structures.
passive.name: Keen Feathers

skill1.description: Garuda conjures an arrow formation that deals 150 (150 + 30% magical attack) magical damage to enemies within it every 0.5s for 2.5s and slows them by 15% for 1s.
skill1.name: Arrows of Gold

skill2.description:
Garuda unleashes the power of wishes, gaining 100 Movement Speed that diminishes over 3s, as well as a shield that negates 300 (300 + 55% magical attack) damage. He also deals 200 (200 + 40% magical attack) magical damage to nearby enemies.
Passive: Gains 15 Movement Speed.
skill2.name: Golden Winged Blessing

skill3.description:
Garuda sends 90 golden arrows of judgment surging forward over 5s, each of which deals 54 (54 + 10% magical attack) magical damage and grants him 20% Movement Speed. He can use other skills at the same time as this skill.
If the skill is used again, Garuda immediately shoots all remaining arrows in every direction, dealing an equal amount of magical damage and inflicting Dread on nearby enemies. He also removes all Physical Attack bonuses granted by their equipment for 2s.
skill3.name: Wings of Judgment

strategy.earlyGame: Garuda's piercing basic attacks are the core of his mid-lane play. Standing where the opponent lines up behind the minions lets him clear and poke at the same time. Placing the Arrows of Gold formation on the opponent's escape route rather than at their feet makes better use of the slow. Keep Golden Winged Blessing as insurance for when he is about to take hits. Until he has his ultimate, prioritize last hits and Health over chasing kills.
strategy.midGame: Once he learns Wings of Judgment, he gains real area control. Fired during tight contests at Tyrant or in front of a tower, the long barrage pushes the whole enemy team back. The core pattern is to slow with the formation, pour in the barrage, and keep firing while Golden Winged Blessing's speed keeps the distance. Don't recast Wings of Judgment casually; Dread and the removal of Physical Attack bonuses are his answer to assassins, so keep it while divers are still around. Stand diagonally behind your front line and look for angles where his piercing attacks reach their back line through their frontliners.
strategy.teamfight: Garuda's value comes down to how long he can keep the barrage going. Once the fight starts, layer Arrows of Gold over the front line and pour Wings of Judgment's arrows into the enemy cluster. Mixing in piercing basic attacks carries the damage through to their back line. If enemies close in, back off with Golden Winged Blessing's speed, and if they still stick to him, recast Wings of Judgment to reset with Dread. Leave fleeing enemies to your team and focus on keeping the arrows flying.

combos.title: Slow Them, Then Barrage
combos.sequence: Skill 1 (Arrows of Gold: slowing formation) → Skill 3 (Wings of Judgment: keep firing arrows) → Basic Attack (piercing attack) → Skill 2 (Golden Winged Blessing: speed and shield to keep distance)
combos.description: The arrow formation keeps damaging and slowing where it is placed. The Wings of Judgment barrage lasts longer, so once the formation fades he has to re-aim himself. He can use other skills while firing, so slotting in Golden Winged Blessing's speed lets him finish the barrage while keeping his distance.

combos.title: Recast When Someone Gets On Him
combos.sequence: Skill 3 (Wings of Judgment: barrage) → Skill 3 (recast the moment someone gets close: Dread) → Skill 2 (Golden Winged Blessing: shield and speed to get away) → Basic Attack
combos.description: The recast fires all remaining arrows around him at once. In exchange for the rest of the barrage, nearby enemies are inflicted with Dread and lose the Physical Attack bonuses from their equipment. It works best when pressed after a physical assassin is already on him.

strengths: His basic attacks pierce, so he keeps damaging grouped enemies
Recasting Wings of Judgment inflicts Dread on nearby enemies and removes their equipment's Physical Attack bonuses
Golden Winged Blessing's shield and speed let him keep his distance while firing
Arrows of Gold and the barrage from Wings of Judgment lock down narrow spaces before objectives
weaknesses: No reliable hard crowd control of his own, so fleeing enemies are hard to catch
Using Dread means discarding the remaining arrows of Wings of Judgment
No blink, so chained crowd control can keep him from escaping

playstyle.style: Garuda is a mage who damages both lines and wide areas with piercing basic attacks and barrages of golden arrows. His ultimate, Wings of Judgment, lets him move and use other skills while firing, so he can keep pressure on the whole fight while backing away. Using it again releases all remaining arrows around him, inflicting Dread on nearby enemies and removing the Physical Attack bonuses from their equipment.
playstyle.suited: He suits players who enjoy firing nonstop. The central decision is the recast of Wings of Judgment: whether to throw away the remaining arrows to reset with Dread, or to fire them all. The more he can hold off on pressing it, the longer he stays alive in fights.

synergy.reason: Lian Po's Tremor Smash launches the whole pile, giving Lady Sun a free window to fire into it.
Lu Bu's Tremble, Mortals launches the group and its edge slows escapes, so Ultimate Shell lands cleanly.

counters.reason: Donghuang's Forsaken Contract suppresses Lady Sun outright, shutting down her rolls and her attacks alike.
Mozi's barrier stuns anything that touches it, so Lady Sun has no safe line to roll in on.

passive.description: Each Basic Attack that hits reduces Skill 1's cooldown by 10%.
passive.name: Energy Burst

skill1.description:
Lady Sun rolls in the target direction and enhances her next Basic Attack, which will deal 454 (285 + 100% physical attack) physical damage to enemies in its path. Using the enhanced Basic Attack will reset the following Basic Attack and increase its range.
If there is an enemy hero nearby after she rolls, her Movement Speed will increase by 80%. This effect diminishes over 2s.
skill1.name: Rolling Raid

skill2.description:
Lady Sun tosses a grenade at the target location, dealing 380 (380 + 120% extra physical attack) physical damage to enemies within range and applying extreme slow for 1s. Reduces enemies' physical defense by 10% and marks enemy heroes and minions for 5s.
Her Basic Attacks deal 120 (120 + 36% extra physical attack) extra physical damage to marked enemy heroes, and 240 (240 + 72% extra physical attack) physical damage to marked minions.
skill2.name: Frag Grenade

skill3.description: Lady Sun fires a powerful shot in the target direction, dealing 840 (840 + 250% extra physical attack) physical damage to the first enemy it hits. Upon hitting an enemy or reaching its maximum range, it detonates, dealing 75% damage to enemies in a cone-shaped area beyond the point of explosion.
skill3.name: Ultimate Shell

strategy.earlyGame: Early on, simply farming without stopping her basic attacks is how Lady Sun prepares to defend herself. The roll, enhanced Basic Attack and extended-range Basic Attack chain works for trading too. Still, while you don't know where the enemy jungler is, it is safer to keep one roll in reserve. Frag Grenade marks minions as well, and basic attacks on marked minions deal heavy extra damage, which helps when you want the wave gone quickly.
strategy.midGame: Once she is fighting away from lane, apply the mark and defense shred with Frag Grenade, then cash it in with basic attacks. Roll forward only when you judge the kill is there; otherwise roll sideways or back while shooting and let the cooldown return. Ultimate Shell explodes in a cone beyond the first enemy it hits, so firing it while enemies bunch up before Tyrant or Overlord reaches the ones in the back. Whether to use it to chip before a fight or save it to finish a fleeing target depends on the situation. The July 2 update raised how much extra physical attack Ultimate Shell and Frag Grenade use, so their damage climbs more as her items come together.
strategy.teamfight: Keeping basic attacks going from a distance nobody can reach is her main job in teamfights. Land Ultimate Shell on the enemy frontline before the fight and the explosion carries into the enemies lined up behind. After that, keep cutting Rolling Raid's cooldown with basic attacks and roll sideways to keep divers at a distance. If someone gets close, drop Frag Grenade at your feet and roll away while the heavy slow holds them.

combos.title: Keep the Roll Coming
combos.sequence: Skill 1 (Rolling Raid: roll and enhance the next Basic Attack) → Basic Attack (enhanced) → Basic Attack (extended range) → Basic Attack (landing hits to cut the cooldown) → Skill 1 (Rolling Raid)
combos.description: Rolling near an enemy hero also gives her a burst of speed, letting her choose each time whether to close in or pull away.

combos.title: Mark, Then Punch Through
combos.sequence: Skill 2 (Frag Grenade: slow, mark and physical defense shred) → Skill 1 (Rolling Raid: find the angle) → Basic Attack (mark bonus) → Skill 3 (Ultimate Shell)
combos.description: With physical defense lowered by Frag Grenade, the enhanced Basic Attack and Ultimate Shell that follow hit harder. Ultimate Shell's explosion spreads in a cone beyond the first enemy hit, so roll to an angle where enemies line up behind your target and catch them together.

strengths: Basic attacks shorten Rolling Raid's cooldown, so she rolls while she shoots
Right after the enhanced Basic Attack, she can fire a longer-range one
Frag Grenade's defense shred and mark let her damage reach tough targets
Ultimate Shell's explosion carries past the first enemy hit to those behind
weaknesses: After an aggressive roll, she has no escape left
Rolling Raid is her only mobility, so stacked crowd control is hard to escape
Her skill damage leans on extra physical attack, so it stays low when her items are late

playstyle.style: The more Lady Sun shoots, the more she rolls. Every Basic Attack that lands shortens Rolling Raid's cooldown, so as long as she keeps attacking, rolls for closing in and rolls for getting out keep coming back.
playstyle.suited: You have to decide, roll by roll, whether you are attacking or escaping. A forward roll leaves her with no exit right after, so players who judge whether a kill is there before rolling live much longer. Having only one escape is a weakness she covers by landing basic attacks without pause.

synergy.reason: Agudo's Gorge Mobilization stuns a cluster, so Air Support's untargeted bombs keep finding someone.
Lian Po's Tremor Smash launches the whole group, so Air Support keeps bombing them where they stand.

counters.reason: Li Bai clears every debuff as Stroke of Genius forms, so the Blowfish Grenade slow vanishes.
Consort Yu is immune to physical attacks during Protecting Winds, and the scattershot is just an enhanced Basic Attack.

passive.description: After using 4 Basic Attacks or a skill, Luban No.7's next Basic Attack is enhanced to a scattershot that deals damage 3 times in a straight line ahead. Each shot deals physical damage equal to 65 (+4% of the target's max Health, increases by 1% for every 100 extra physical attack), or 207 (120 + 50% physical attack) physical damage to non-hero enemy units.
passive.name: Suppressive Fire

skill1.description: Luban No.7 hurls a blowfish grenade at the target location, dealing 520 (520 + 120% extra physical attack) physical damage to enemies within range and reducing their Movement Speed by 25% for 2s. He also gains vision of targets hit by the grenade.
skill1.name: Blowfish Grenade

skill2.description: Luban No.7 launches a rocket in the target direction. The rocket knocks back enemies directly in front of him and explodes upon hitting the first enemy hero. The explosion deals 450 (450 + 100% extra physical attack) physical damage and magical damage equal to 5% of the target's lost Health to enemies within range.
skill2.name: Shark Cannon

skill3.description:
Luban No.7 summons a blowfish airship in the target direction for 14s, which drops bombs on a random enemy within range. The bombs explode where they landed after a short delay, dealing 520 (520 + 120% extra physical attack) physical damage to nearby enemies and reducing their Movement Speed by 25% for 1s.
The airship grants him vision of the area it is bombarding.
skill3.name: Air Support

strategy.earlyGame: In lane, put last hits first and stay close to your tower. He has no mobility skill, so while the enemy jungler or support is out of sight, don't step forward. The scattershot damages non-hero units too, and Blowfish Grenade hits an area, so he can clear waves even from a cautious position. Blowfish Grenade grants vision of whatever it hits, so when a bush looks suspicious, throw one in. If it hits, the enemy inside is revealed. To trade, slip a Basic Attack in after a skill so the scattershot lands on the opponent.
strategy.midGame: Even after he leaves lane and moves with the team, Luban No.7's place stays behind the frontline. The Air Support airship also grants vision of the area it bombs, so in standoffs before objectives, send it ahead to where the enemy is likely waiting. Its bombs pick enemies in range at random, so it is not the tool for finishing one particular target. Against enemies defending a tower, weave skills to land scattershots and wear them down with max-Health damage before moving on the tower with your team. Shark Cannon is how he pushes enemies away, so before using it offensively, check where the enemy divers are. Its explosion also deals magic damage based on the target's missing Health, so wounded enemies take it harder.
strategy.teamfight: Luban No.7 stands a little behind his frontline and shoots whichever enemies the scattershot can reach. The scattershot travels in a straight line, so aiming down a line of enemies hits several of them in one shot. When they spread out, aiming at a high-Health frontliner still is not wasted, thanks to the max-Health damage. Once the fight opens, slow the enemy cluster with Blowfish Grenade and keep stacking scattershots after each skill. If an enemy assassin comes from behind, push them off with Shark Cannon, leave a Blowfish Grenade slow on the chaser, and back off toward your team.

combos.title: Weave Skills for More Scattershots
combos.sequence: Skill 3 (Air Support: over the enemy cluster) → Skill 1 (Blowfish Grenade: slow) → Basic Attack (scattershot) → Skill 2 (Shark Cannon) → Basic Attack (scattershot)
combos.description: The Basic Attack right after a skill becomes a scattershot, so slipping one in after each skill gets scattershots out faster than waiting through a string of normal attacks. Air Support keeps bombing for a long time, so casting it first keeps bombs and slows coming throughout the rest of the sequence. Once Blowfish Grenade slows the enemies, the straight-line scattershot is easier to land.

combos.title: Push Back and Retreat to the Team
combos.sequence: Skill 2 (Shark Cannon: knock back enemies in front) → Basic Attack (scattershot) → Skill 1 (Blowfish Grenade: slow the chaser) → back off
combos.description: Shark Cannon is the only thing that moves an enemy off him, so when he uses it to defend, it goes first. The Basic Attack after it is a scattershot, so if the enemy he pushed back is still in the line ahead, it hits them too. When retreating, land Blowfish Grenade on whoever follows and walk back to your team while they are slowed.

strengths: The scattershot deals damage based on enemy heroes' max Health, so it still works on bulky frontliners
Every skill turns his next Basic Attack into a scattershot, so he fires them more often
Blowfish Grenade and Air Support let him get his own vision
The scattershot and Blowfish Grenade also hit minions, so waves go down quickly
weaknesses: No mobility skill; once someone reaches him, Shark Cannon's knockback is his only defense
The scattershot only hits a straight line ahead, so spread-out enemies take fewer hits
Air Support's bombs pick their targets at random and cannot be focused on the enemy he wants dead
Using Shark Cannon to attack leaves him nothing to answer a dive until it returns

playstyle.style: Luban No.7 has no mobility skill at all; instead, his scattershot Basic Attack deals damage based on enemy heroes' max Health. After a set number of Basic Attacks, or right after he uses a skill, his next shot becomes a scattershot that hits three times down a straight line ahead. Blowfish Grenade and Air Support give him his own vision, so he is a marksman who holds a fixed spot behind his frontline and keeps shooting whatever he can see.
playstyle.suited: When someone reaches him, Shark Cannon's knockback is about all he can rely on. Whether he survives is decided almost entirely by where he stands. If you can stay behind your frontline and calmly push divers away only when they come, he gets to keep shooting for much longer. Players who want to step forward and chase kills will find him cramped.

synergy.reason: Lady Sun only speeds up when she rolls beside an enemy, while Zhuangzi's marks keep her quick everywhere else.
Marco Polo fires from inside the enemy line, and Zhuangzi's Butterfly Effect keeps crowd control from cutting it short.

counters.reason: Pei's Guarding Stance burns everyone around him, so Zhuangzi cannot stay close enough to protect his carry.

passive.description:
Enters a Dreamscape every 6s for 2s and recovers 40 (40 + 0.6% extra Health) Health.
Dreamscape: Removes all crowd control effects and grants crowd control immunity, 15% damage reduction, and 15% Movement Speed for 2s.
passive.name: Nature's Will

skill1.description: Zhuangzi sends out dream butterflies in a cone-shaped area, gaining the enhancement from his passive skill for 2s. The butterflies deal 400 (400 +72% magical attack) magical damage to enemies within range and slow them by 30% for 2s.
skill1.name: Kaleidoscope

skill2.description:
Zhuangzi deals 250 (250 + 40% magical attack) magical damage to nearby enemies and places 1 mark on them for 5s, for up to 5 stacks. Each mark deals 125 (125 + 20% magical attack) magical damage to enemies.
He also places 1 mark on himself and nearby teammates for 5s, for up to 5 stacks. Each mark increases Movement Speed by 3%.
Passive: Zhuangzi uses Skill 2 every 7s.
skill2.name: Sleep Starts

skill3.description: Zhuangzi conjures up a dreamscape, removing all crowd control effects from himself and nearby teammates while granting a shield that grants crowd control immunity and negates 600 (600 + 12% extra Health) damage to himself and all teammates for 1.5s.
skill3.name: Butterfly Effect

strategy.earlyGame: Zhuangzi's first spot as a roamer is next to his marksman. In lane, land Kaleidoscope on the opponent to slow them and make your team's attacks easier to land. Thanks to his passive, he can stand a step forward without fearing enemy lockdown. Sleep Starts also casts itself at regular intervals, so staying near the enemy keeps marks and team speed flowing. Before the fight over Tyrant, step into the river bushes first so your jungler can start safely.
strategy.midGame: From the mid game on, what Zhuangzi contributes comes down to when and for whom he uses Butterfly Effect. On the front line of objective fights, spread Kaleidoscope's slow while counting how many enemy heroes have crowd control and who their engager is. Decide in advance whom to save Butterfly Effect for, and you can layer it on without hesitation when a teammate gets caught. The July 30 update shortened Butterfly Effect's crowd control immunity and shield duration.
strategy.teamfight: Zhuangzi's place is half a step in front of his back line. His passive regularly removes his own crowd control, so absorbing some hits and drawing as many enemy skills onto himself as possible is part of the job. Kaleidoscope's slow works both for running down fleeing enemies and for buying teammates time to escape. The longer the brawl lasts, the more Sleep Starts' mark damage and speed boosts add up.

combos.title: Erase the Engage After It Lands
combos.sequence: watch enemy crowd control land on a teammate → Skill 3 (Butterfly Effect: area cleanse, shield and crowd control immunity) → Skill 1 (Kaleidoscope: slow in a cone) → Skill 2 (Sleep Starts: stack marks)
combos.description: Butterfly Effect hands out cleansing and immunity at once, but the immunity ends quickly. Pressing it early just lets the enemy wait, so layer it on the moment a teammate gets caught. Once they are free, slow the enemy with Kaleidoscope and turn straight into a counterattack.

combos.title: Sticking Close to Stack Marks
combos.sequence: Skill 1 (Kaleidoscope: slow and passive enhancement) → Skill 2 (Sleep Starts: marks up close) → Basic Attack → Skill 2 (Sleep Starts: layer it when the cooldown is back)
combos.description: Casting Kaleidoscope grants his passive enhancement for a moment, making him immune to crowd control. Step in and layer Sleep Starts, and enemies get marks that deal damage over time while he and nearby teammates get speed marks.

strengths: Butterfly Effect removes crowd control from teammates and briefly makes them immune to it
His passive regularly removes his own crowd control, so lockdown rarely holds him for long
Kaleidoscope's slow works both for chasing and for buying teammates time to escape
Passive healing and damage reduction let him stay on the front line for a long time
weaknesses: No hard crowd control, so his own kill pressure is small
Against heavy burst, he has few defenses beyond his shield
Against teams with little crowd control, Butterfly Effect's cleanse has fewer chances to matter

playstyle.style: Zhuangzi is a support who regularly sheds his own crowd control and removes it from teammates too with his ultimate, Butterfly Effect. His passive puts him in a Dreamscape at regular intervals, removing crowd control and briefly granting crowd control immunity and damage reduction. Kaleidoscope sends butterflies out in a cone that slow enemies and also calls up his passive enhancement.
playstyle.suited: He suits players who would rather make enemy engages whiff than take kills. Butterfly Effect works very differently depending on when it is pressed, so he needs the judgment to hold back and wait for the enemy's key crowd control. He has few ways to get kills himself, so he spends the game moving near his back line.

synergy.reason: Garo's Silent Arrow detonates on a delay, so Robo Smash's stun holds the target in place for it.
Hou Yi's enhanced Arrow Volley also damages structures, pairing with Liu Shan, whose skills hit towers just as hard.

counters.reason: Marco Polo's Destroyed Defense adds true damage to every hit, so Liu Shan's armor does nothing against it.
Sun Bin's Time Flux speeds up his whole team, so Liu Shan's charge lands on empty ground.

passive.description: Liu Shan's skills deal equal damage to structures, and his crowd control skills disrupt them for 1.2s. He pillages parts of structures to recover 280 Health when dealing damage to them with his skills.
passive.name: Magnetic Barrier

skill1.description: Liu Shan activates his shield and initiates an assault, gaining 50% Movement Speed that diminishes over time and a shield that negates 650 (650 + 16% extra Health) damage for 3s. Also enhances Liu Shan's next Basic Attack, in which he leaps up and slams into the ground, dealing 569 (350 + 122% physical attack) physical damage to enemies within range and launching them for 1s.
skill1.name: Overcharge!

skill2.description: Liu Shan commands his mechcraft to claw at enemies in a cone-shaped area, dealing 580 (400 + 100% physical attack) physical damage to them and stunning them for 1s.
skill2.name: Robo Smash

skill3.description:
Liu Shan commands his mechcraft to spin its arms, dealing 380 (380 + 110% extra physical attack) physical damage to nearby enemies every 0.5s for 3s and slowing them by 15% for 0.5s every second.
Other skills can be used while spinning.
skill3.name: Take It for a Spin

strategy.earlyGame: While roaming, Liu Shan moves with his teammates and keeps an eye on the next structure he can hit. His early star is Robo Smash's stun; landing the tip of the cone during your jungler's gank stops the target and sets up the kill. Every skill is short range, so approach after gaining the shield and speed from Overcharge!. At Tyrant, stand in front and stop anyone who comes to interfere with a stun.
strategy.midGame: Liu Shan shines right after a teamfight win. Once the enemy backs off, head to the nearest tower and hit it while Robo Smash stops its attacks. Each skill hit on a structure restores Health, so he can often take one more tower at a Health level where he would normally back off. Decide which structure to take after a win before the fight even starts.
strategy.teamfight: Liu Shan's role is to keep enemies stopped where your team's damage can reach. Step into the enemy back line with Overcharge! and open with the enhanced attack's launch. Follow with Robo Smash's stun on the key target, then spin with Take It for a Spin to damage and slow everything around him. He can use other skills while spinning, so his crowd control never has to stop. Enemies who keep their distance are out of his reach, so meeting divers who jump onto your back line is steadier than chasing and getting isolated.

combos.title: An Engage Without Gaps
combos.sequence: Skill 1 (Overcharge!: shield and speed) → Basic Attack (enhanced attack launches) → Skill 2 (Robo Smash: stun) → Skill 3 (Take It for a Spin: spin and slow)
combos.description: Overcharge!'s speed boost is strongest right after casting and fades from there, so start moving in immediately. When the launch from the enhanced attack and Robo Smash's stun land back to back, your team has time to pile on. Other skills can be used while spinning, so he can keep slowing and holding enemies.

combos.title: Take a Tower Right After Winning
combos.sequence: Skill 1 (Overcharge!: step forward) → Skill 2 (Robo Smash: stop the tower's attacks) → Skill 3 (Take It for a Spin: keep hitting) → Skill 2 (stop it again when ready)
combos.description: His skills deal the same damage to structures and restore Health with each hit. Stopping the tower's attacks is the job of his crowd control skills, so pace the hits around Robo Smash. After winning a teamfight, go straight on to take a tower.

strengths: His skills deal the same damage to towers and crystals, and his crowd control skills stop their attacks
Each skill hit on a structure restores his Health, so he can hold on during a push
He can chain a launch, a stun and a slow by himself
Overcharge!'s shield and speed boost carry him into the first step of a fight
weaknesses: Every skill is short range, so enemies who keep their distance are out of reach
Overcharge!'s speed boost is his only way to close distance, and fast enemies can escape
His own damage is modest, so if his team cannot follow up, the time he buys is wasted

playstyle.style: Liu Shan is a support whose skills deal the same damage to towers and crystals, and whose crowd control skills shut down a tower's attacks. Each skill hit on a structure pillages parts and restores his Health, so he can hold on deep in a push. He chains Overcharge!'s launch, Robo Smash's stun, and Take It for a Spin's spinning slow all by himself.
playstyle.suited: He suits players who think ahead to which tower to take, and when, after a teamfight win. Every skill needs him up close, so committing to the step forward with Overcharge! is what decides how he plays. His own damage is modest, so the job is stopping enemies where your team can follow up.

synergy.reason: Bai Qi's pull and taunt hold enemies in one clump, so Rock Out! and Wild Chord's ricochets keep landing.
Sun Bin's speed boost carries Gao into the enemy line, where Rock Out! grows tougher with each enemy hero nearby.

counters.reason: Liang can suppress Gao outright, cutting off Rock Out! long before the drawn-out performance finishes.
Donghuang's suppression shares all damage taken, so allies rushing in to free Gao end up hurting him instead.

passive.description: After using 3 Basic Attacks or skills, the next Basic Attack is enhanced to an energized chord that deals 290 (290 + 80% magical attack) magical damage to enemies in its path.
passive.name: Guitar Solo

skill1.description:
Gao plays wild notes, dealing 340 (340 + 47% magical attack) magical damage to up to 2 enemies within range. When these notes hit an enemy, they ricochet into nearby enemies up to 2 times.
When multiple notes hit the same hero, subsequent hits only deal 30% damage.
skill1.name: Wild Chord

skill2.description:
Gao dashes in the target direction while strumming wildly, dealing 450 (450 + 60% magical attack) magical damage to nearby enemies and slowing them by 15% for 2s. Each hero hit recovers 100 (100 + 15% magical attack) Health, while non-hero units recover half this amount. During the dash, he gains 10% damage reduction and immunity to slow.
Using Wild Chord during the dash allows for another dash.
skill2.name: String Bender

skill3.description: Gao performs passionately, dealing 200 (200 + 20% magical attack) magical damage every 0.5s for 5s. While performing, he gains 50% Movement Speed which diminishes over 3s. He also gains 10% damage reduction if there is an enemy hero nearby, plus an extra 5% for every additional enemy hero nearby.
skill3.name: Rock Out!

strategy.earlyGame: Until he learns his ultimate, Gao has only String Bender to protect himself in mid lane, so he avoids forcing things. Wild Chord's notes ricochet into nearby enemies, so hitting minions and bouncing the notes into the opposing hero chips them safely. String Bender heals only half as much off non-hero units, so outside of escapes, use it at an angle that hits the opponent.
strategy.midGame: Once he learns Rock Out!, his playstyle changes. In fights over Tyrant, wait behind your front line, then dive in with String Bender the moment enemies bunch up and play Rock Out!. While Rock Out! is down, stay off the front line. Before engaging, check who the enemy's stunners are, and going in after seeing those skills used on your front line makes it easier to finish the performance. The tight terrain before Shadow Tyrant and Shadow Overlord suits ricocheting notes, so he can also contribute by chipping before the fight.
strategy.teamfight: Open by keeping distance and chipping with Wild Chord; the real play is diving in the moment enemies bunch up. Right after casting Rock Out! he moves faster, but the speed fades, so settle his position early. If he is about to die mid-performance, simply walking back toward his team instead of finishing can bait the enemy's chase and buy time.

combos.title: Double Dash Into the Brawl
combos.sequence: Skill 2 (String Bender: dash and deal damage) → Skill 1 (Wild Chord: cast mid-dash to dash again) → Skill 3 (Rock Out!: perform)
combos.description: Casting Wild Chord during String Bender's dash allows another dash. Use the two steps to reach the middle of a clumped enemy team. The middle of a brawl gives Rock Out! more damage reduction than chasing an isolated target, making it easier to play the whole performance.

combos.title: The Piercing Third Chord
combos.sequence: Skill 1 (Wild Chord) → Skill 2 (String Bender) → Basic Attack → Basic Attack (energized chord)
combos.description: Basic Attacks and skills each count as one play. After three, the next Basic Attack becomes an energized chord that pierces enemies in its path, so it can reach the opponent through minions.

strengths: Rock Out! grants more damage reduction the more enemy heroes are nearby, so he holds up at the center of brawls
String Bender's healing and the extra dash from Wild Chord let him both dive in and get out
The piercing energized chord clears waves and pokes at the same time
weaknesses: While Rock Out! is down, he has little power to start fights himself
His peak damage comes up close, so stuns that stop his performance leave him fragile
Wild Chord deals less damage on repeated hits to the same hero, so his single-target burst is low

playstyle.style: Gao is a mage who wears enemies down together with ricocheting notes and the fierce performance of his ultimate. After three Basic Attacks or skills, his next Basic Attack becomes an energized chord that pierces enemies in its path. His ultimate, Rock Out!, keeps dealing damage while he plays, and he takes less damage the more enemy heroes are nearby.
playstyle.suited: He suits players who want a mage that steps into the enemy instead of only firing from the back. Rock Out! holds up better the more enemies are nearby, so he needs both the nerve to enter the middle of a brawl and the caution to check the enemy's stunners first.

synergy.reason: Bai Qi's taunt turns the target toward him, leaving their back open for Arke's guaranteed crit.
Guiguzi's camouflage covers Arke too, so she reaches a target's back without ever being seen coming.

counters.reason: Arthur's enhanced attack dashes in and silences Arke, cutting her combo off partway through.
Lu Bu's ring of slaughter spikes his defenses, and its edge slows Arke as she tries to leave.

passive.description: All attacks Arke launches from behind her target are guaranteed to crit, while attacks launched from the front are guaranteed not to crit. Her initial Critical Damage is 125%, and every 1% Critical Rate grants an extra 0.5% Critical Damage. Arke's damage when attacking non-hero units from the front is increased by 20%, and her damage to non-hero units is capped at 2,000.
passive.name: Kiss of Death

skill1.description: Arke wields her twin blades and attacks 2 times, each dealing 150 (150 + 65% extra physical attack) physical damage.
skill1.name: Arclight

skill2.description:
Arke dashes forward quickly and attacks a nearby enemy at her destination, dealing 270 (270 + 85% extra physical attack) physical damage and marking the enemy for 10s. She also gains 40% Attack Speed for 3s.
Her attacks on marked the enemy inflict 25% slow for 1s and reduce Untouchable's cooldown by 1s. She takes 30% less damage from marked enemies.
Only 1 enemy can be marked by her at a time.
skill2.name: Untouchable

skill3.description:
Arke goes into stealth mode after a short delay. While in stealth mode, her Movement Speed increases by 40% and she recovers 150 (150 + 25% extra physical attack + 5% extra Health) Health every 0.5s for 4s.
Attacking an enemy will cancel stealth mode and increase her Physical Attack by 120 for 3s.
When an enemy is hit, her Movement Speed increases by 30% for 1s.
Passive: Defeating a hero or assisting refreshes the cooldown of all skills.
skill3.name: Phantom Dance

strategy.earlyGame: Arke struggles until her first kill, so she focuses on clearing the jungle. Her passive increases damage when hitting monsters from the front, so there is no need to get behind them while clearing. Before she has Phantom Dance, her ganks rely only on Untouchable's dash and cannot chase far, and a failed one costs a lot of growth, so only go for targets she can finish.
strategy.midGame: Once she learns Phantom Dance, her main job becomes approaching invisibly from bushes. She moves faster while invisible, so circle around from places without vision and only start attacking from behind. She never crits from the front, so that extra step turns straight into extra damage. As her critical rate items come together, she can take down back-liners alone, and cooldowns refreshing on kills become the starting point for chain plays. Before Shadow Tyrant or Shadow Overlord, lurk in bushes and only circle behind once the enemy's stuns or lockdowns have been used on your team. Enemies standing against walls are hard to get behind, so choose back-liners in open ground.
strategy.teamfight: Arke goes in last. Once the enemy's attention and skills are on your front line, wait a little more, circle behind them with Phantom Dance, close in from behind with Untouchable to mark the target, and pour in basic attacks and Arclight. She takes less damage from the marked target, so staying on one target until it falls keeps her alive longer. Once the target is down, keep moving and use her refreshed skills to get behind the next one.

combos.title: Get Behind Them, Then Strike
combos.sequence: Skill 3 (Phantom Dance: vanish and speed up) → circle behind the enemy → Skill 2 (Untouchable: dash and mark) → Basic Attack → Skill 1 (Arclight)
combos.description: Attacking breaks her stealth, so walk around to the target's back before doing anything. Her passive makes every attack from behind a critical hit and none from the front. After revealing herself, her Physical Attack rises for a while, stacking with Untouchable's attack speed boost.

combos.title: Chase Without Losing the Mark
combos.sequence: Skill 2 (Untouchable: mark the target) → Basic Attack → Skill 1 (Arclight: two strikes) → Basic Attack
combos.description: Each attack on the marked target shortens Untouchable's cooldown and slows them a little. Keep hitting and the dash will be ready again in time to chase.

strengths: Attacks from behind always crit, letting her take down back-liners quickly
Kills and assists refresh all her cooldowns, so she can chain fights
Phantom Dance heals her while invisible, making resets and escapes easier
She takes less damage from the target marked by Untouchable, so she holds up in one-on-one brawls
weaknesses: She never crits from the front, so her damage drops in face-to-face trades
No hard crowd control, and a single stun can stop and kill her
She struggles to make an impact until her first kill, especially in losing games

playstyle.style: Arke is a jungler whose attacks from behind are always critical hits, while attacks from the front never crit. Her ultimate, Phantom Dance, lets her vanish and heal while circling around to strike the target's back. Defeating or assisting on a hero refreshes all her skill cooldowns, so taking down the first target lets her move straight on to the next.
playstyle.suited: She suits players with the patience to pick an isolated target and wait until they can get behind it. She never crits from the front, so what decides how she plays is treating the time spent circling around as preparation rather than a chore. With no hard crowd control and a fragile body, sticking to the right order of engagement is essential.

synergy.reason: Daji's stun pins a target in place, letting Wuyan land her hammer's center, where it hits hardest.
Luban No.7's slows leave enemies struggling to escape the area Wuyan covers while spinning her hammer.

counters.reason: Marco Polo blinks away on a short cooldown, so Wuyan's dash can never stay on him.
Mozi's cannon stuns and leaves a burning crater, so Wuyan is chipped down the entire walk in.

passive.description:
Whenever Wuyan deals damage with a Basic Attack or skill, there is a 50% chance to petrify enemies for 0.75s.
The same target can only be petrified once every 8s.
Every 3s, she summons the power of the earth to gain a shield that negates 300 (300 + 8% extra Health) damage.
passive.name: Petrifying Strike

skill1.description:
Wuyan dashes in the target direction while enhancing her next Basic Attack for 4s. Her enhanced Basic Attack deals 250 (250 + 50% extra physical attack) extra physical damage to enemies within range and slows them by 25% for 2s.
Using Skill 1 while the Ultimate is active slightly reduces the speed of her dash.
skill1.name: Storm and Stress

skill2.description: Wuyan slams the target area with her hammer, dealing 700 (700 + 200% extra physical attack) physical damage to enemies within range and an extra 50% damage to enemies in the center.
skill2.name: Shock and Awe

skill3.description:
Wuyan spins her hammer, increasing her Movement Speed by 10% for 3.2s. Every 0.4s, she deals 300 (300 + 100% extra physical attack) physical damage to nearby enemies and an extra 50% damage to enemies at the edge of her attack range.
While spinning, she gains 5% Movement Speed and a shield that negates 80 (80 + 3% extra Health) damage every 0.4s, for up to 4 stacks.
skill3.name: Hurricane Hammer

strategy.earlyGame: Wuyan holds the clash lane while honing her aim with Shock and Awe. It also clears waves, and she can aim it at the opponent's feet the moment they step up to last-hit. In trades, touch the opponent with Storm and Stress's dash and the enhanced Basic Attack, and when petrification triggers, layer Shock and Awe onto the stuck target to build a lead. Her passive shield refreshes over time, so the more short exchanges she slips in, the better.
strategy.midGame: Once she learns Hurricane Hammer, make sure she can show up for fights over Tyrant. The spin hits many times and each hit rolls petrification, so simply placing it in a brawl freezes several enemies in turn. During the spin her Movement Speed builds and shields stack, so she can chase fleeing enemies too. Keeping Shock and Awe for right after the spin ends helps her finish a petrified back-liner.
strategy.teamfight: Wuyan's job is spinning in the middle of the enemy to break their formation. Each enemy can only be petrified once in a while, so walking the spin toward enemies she has not stopped yet holds the whole team longer than chasing one who was already petrified. Right after the spin ends she is exposed, so decide on the spot whether to spend Shock and Awe on a back-liner or keep it to protect herself. Petrification is chance-based, so don't rely on it too much when there is someone she really needs to stop.

combos.title: Petrify, Then Center Hit
combos.sequence: Skill 1 (Storm and Stress: dash and enhance the next Basic Attack) → Basic Attack (enhanced: area damage and slow) → Skill 2 (Shock and Awe: aim for the center)
combos.description: The enhanced Basic Attack's damage also rolls her passive's petrify chance. Petrification ends quickly, though, so reacting after it lands is too late. Predict where the slowed target will be and place Shock and Awe's center there.

combos.title: Spin Through Their Formation
combos.sequence: Skill 1 (Storm and Stress: dash) → Skill 3 (Hurricane Hammer: spin) → Skill 2 (Shock and Awe)
combos.description: Storm and Stress's dash slows down during Hurricane Hammer, so dash in close before starting to spin. Enemies at the outer edge of the spin take extra damage, so keeping them at the rim by shifting half a step increases her damage.

strengths: Both Basic Attacks and skills can petrify, so the more she hits, the more chances she has to stop enemies
Shock and Awe deals heavy damage when it lands with the center of its area
Shields from her passive and Hurricane Hammer help her hold up in brawls
weaknesses: Petrification is chance-based and may not trigger when she needs it
Shock and Awe is a placed area skill, so landing the center on moving targets is hard
Storm and Stress's short dash is her only movement, so kiting enemies are hard to reach

playstyle.style: Wuyan is a front-line fighter whose Basic Attacks and skills have a chance to petrify enemies whenever they deal damage. Her passive also grants a shield at regular intervals. While she spins her hammer with her ultimate, Hurricane Hammer, she chips nearby enemies while stacking shields.
playstyle.suited: She suits players who prefer pressing with constant attacks over fine control. Petrification is chance-based, so she has to keep attacking with a plan for when it does not trigger. Shock and Awe hits much harder at the center of its area, so predicting the target's footing takes practice.

synergy.reason: Lady Sun's rotation speeds up with every Basic Attack that lands, and Sun Bin's slow keeps enemies in range.
Luban No.7's scattershot only lands on enemies lined up ahead, and Sun Bin's slow holds them there.

counters.reason: Mulan ignores crowd control while casting in heavy sword form, so Time Lapse never interrupts or silences her.
Diaochan keeps blinking to new positions, so Sun Bin's skill shots rarely find her at all.

passive.description: Whenever Sun Bin uses a skill, he gains 65-130 Movement Speed for 2s.
passive.name: Hourglass of Time

skill1.description:
Sun Bin throws a bomb in the target direction that deals 200 (200 + 20% magical attack) magical damage to the first enemy it hits and latches onto them.
The bomb explodes 3s later or when the target dies, dealing 575 (575 + 60% magical attack) magical damage to enemies within range and slowing them by 15% for 2s.
Cleansing the bomb will cause it to detonate immediately.
skill1.name: Time Bomb

skill2.description:
Sun Bin manipulates time, increasing the Movement Speed of himself and nearby teammates by 130 for 2s. After the 2s, he recovers Health equal to 25% of the damage taken during this period.
Passive: He gains 7.5% Cooldown Reduction.
skill2.name: Time Flux

skill3.description:
Sun Bin throws an enhanced bomb in the target direction. Upon hitting an enemy or reaching its max range, the bomb unfurls an energy field, dealing 500 (500 + 45% magical attack) magical damage to enemies within range and slowing them immensely for 1s. The field interrupts the enemy's skill and silences them for 1s.
The energy field explodes 5s later, dealing 1,500 (1,500 + 135% magical attack) magical damage to enemies within range.
skill3.name: Time Lapse

strategy.earlyGame: Sun Bin first follows his marksman and holds the farm lane bushes. When the enemy engages, back off together with his teammates using Time Flux's speed. Part of the damage he takes during the boost comes back afterward, so using it just before enemy skills land returns more Health. Time Bomb's payoff is the explosion after it attaches, so in skirmishes, sandwich the bombed target with a teammate and chase until it blows.
strategy.midGame: Once he learns Time Lapse, he can cut off enemy escape routes during ganks. In fights over Tyrant and mid-game rotations, Time Flux moves his whole team together. Keep arriving at objectives as a full team a step before the enemy. The July 2 update changed the speed from his passive and Time Flux from a percentage to a flat value.
strategy.teamfight: His first move is placing Time Lapse on the enemy's retreat path rather than at their feet. The immense slow helps his team's chase land, and the explosion a little later catches enemies backing off. Following up by attaching Time Bomb to a frontliner sets up the explosion and area slow for a follow-up. Time Flux can also speed up an engage, but its main use is timing it to big incoming enemy damage to recover more Health afterward. His own damage is modest, so keep moving from behind his team where enemies cannot reach him.

combos.title: Close the Gap Until It Blows
combos.sequence: Skill 1 (Time Bomb: attach the bomb) → Skill 2 (Time Flux: speed up himself and teammates) → chase with teammates
combos.description: Time Bomb's real payoff is the explosion a little after it attaches. Time Flux is not only for running away; it also works as speed to stay on the target until the bomb goes off. The bomb explodes even if the target dies first, so attach it early to enemies you can finish.

combos.title: Interrupt and Slow
combos.sequence: Skill 3 (Time Lapse: unfurl the field and slow immensely) → Skill 1 (Time Bomb) → Skill 2 (Time Flux: speed up)
combos.description: Time Lapse's field deals damage and an immense slow the moment it unfurls, then explodes heavily a little later. It interrupts the enemy's skill and silences them, so aim it at enemies holding an escape skill or mages with long casts.

strengths: Time Flux speeds up nearby teammates together, quickening rotations and chases
Time Lapse's field slows enemies immensely, and a big explosion follows a little later
Every skill he uses speeds him up too, making it easy to reposition
weaknesses: No hard crowd control like a stun, so he is weak at catching enemies on his own
Both Time Bomb and Time Lapse take time to explode, so he lacks instant lockdown
His own durability and damage are modest, and a badly timed speed boost leaves little behind

playstyle.style: Sun Bin is a support who speeds up himself and nearby teammates together, quickening his whole team. When Time Flux's speed boost ends, he recovers part of the damage he took during it. His ultimate, Time Lapse, unfurls a field where it lands that slows enemies immensely, then explodes heavily a while later.
playstyle.suited: He suits players who want to control the tempo of a match. His speed boost does very different work depending on when he hands it out, so he needs to judge the moments his team engages and retreats. He has limited ways to stop enemies, so he moves in step with his team's attacks.

synergy.reason: Bai Qi taunts and pulls enemies into one clump, so Dr Bian's detonated marks hit the whole group.
Xiang Yu cannot be defeated during his ultimate, so Dr Bian's healing has time to land and hold the line.

counters.reason: Yang Jian's damage scales with the Health Dr Bian has already lost, so every trade makes the next one worse.
Mai Shiranui strips magical defense before she dashes in, leaving Dr Bian no room to reset the distance.

passive.description:
Dr Bian's Basic Attacks and skills place a poison mark on enemies for 7s (up to 5 stacks), dealing 20 (20 + 5% magical attack) magical damage per second.
Healing skills place a healing mark on teammates and himself for 7s (up to 5 stacks), restoring 3 (3 + 2% magical attack) Health per second to teammates, and 3 (3 + 2% magical attack + 0.15% extra Health) Health per second to himself.
passive.name: Malicious Practice

skill1.description:
Dr Bian throws a vial of lethal poison that shatters upon impact, releasing a pool of poison for 4s. Every second, it deals 65 (65 + 14% magical attack) magical damage to enemies within the area and slows them by 30% for 2s.
Dr Bian stocks 1 vial every 12.5s. Up to 3 vials can be stocked.
skill1.name: Deadly Panacea

skill2.description: Dr Bian throws a concoction, dealing 130 (130 +30% magical attack) magical damage to enemies hit and restoring 65 (65 +15% magical attack) Health to nearby teammates.
skill2.name: Fatal Diagnosis

skill3.description:
Dr Bian detonates all nearby marks, dealing 150 (150 + 40% magical attack) magical damage to enemies while restoring 70 (70 + 20% magical attack) Health to teammates. Each stack of mark increases damage and healing by 50%.
He also recovers 400 (400 + 30% magical attack + 5% extra Health) extra Health.
skill3.name: Master of Life

strategy.earlyGame: Dr Bian lacks the burst to finish enemies quickly, so he doesn't force early trades in mid lane. He clears waves with Deadly Panacea's poison pools and prioritizes keeping his Health up. Vials recharge over time and he can stock several, so keeping one in reserve for self-defense is safer.
