The fourth Basic Attack's launch and lifesteal help him keep his Health through repeated fights
Crowd control immunity and damage reduction during The Unrivaled Spear let him finish swinging under crowd control
Ruthless Assault can cross walls, making it easy to move in and out of the enemy jungle
weaknesses: He is fragile, and crowd control after he has spent his movement skills often kills him
Fight or Die!'s reversed input is unusual, and mistakes put him in danger
His damage centers on the fourth Basic Attack, so it is low in short trades
He spends a lot of time alone and struggles in games without vision

playstyle.style: Han Xin is a jungle assassin who leaps around with a double jump and a backward dash. Every fourth Basic Attack launches the enemy and adds extra damage and lifesteal, and landing skills or enhanced Basic Attacks raises his attack speed. His ultimate, The Unrivaled Spear, sweeps a cone four times, granting crowd control immunity and damage reduction while he swings.
playstyle.suited: He suits players who enjoy movement for its own sake. Fight or Die! dashes in the opposite direction from where you aim, so it takes practice until your fingers learn it. Spending every movement skill on offense leaves him with no way out, so judging which one to save for the way back is essential.

synergy.reason: Zhang Fei's stun pins the target down, so Frigid Prison's delayed freeze lands every time.
Zhou Yu's fire domain only burns those who stay in it, and Frigid Prison's freeze holds them there.

counters.reason: Mai Shiranui keeps dashing to new ground, so Frigid Prison's delayed detonation catches nothing.
Zhuangzi's passive cycles into crowd control immunity, so Frigid Prison's freeze slides off him while that immunity is up.

passive.description:
Upon leaving combat, Wang Zhaojun gains a shield that negates 450 (450 + 58% magical attack) damage. Enemies that deal physical damage to the shield will be chilled. When the shield disappears, it deals 400 (400 + 75% magical attack) magical damage to nearby enemies and chills them.
Her every third Basic Attack will be enhanced, firing 3 icicles that deal a total of 180 (180 + 36% magical attack) magical damage. Each icicle applies 100% of the Basic Attack's on-hit effects.
Hits from her active skills and enhanced Basic Attacks will chill enemies, reducing their Movement Speed by 25-50% and Attack Speed by 25-50% for 2s. These effects diminish over time.
passive.name: Frozen Heart

skill1.description: Wang Zhaojun conjures a burst of exploding ice in the target location, dealing 350 (350 + 50% magical attack) magical damage and inflicting chill to enemies within range. She also gains vision of the area and any enemies hit for 2s.
skill1.name: Shattered Ice

skill2.description:
Wang Zhaojun summons a freezing circle in the target location. After a short delay, she deals 250 (250 +50% magical attack) magical damage to enemies within range and freezes them for 2.5s.
She deals an extra 150 (150 + 20% magical attack) magical damage to frozen enemies.
skill2.name: Frigid Prison

skill3.description:
Wang Zhaojun summons a snowstorm in the target location for 5s. The snowstorm deals 200 (200 + 35% magical attack) magical damage and inflicts chill to enemies within range every 0.5s.
Summoning a snowstorm grants her the shield from her passive.
skill3.name: Winter Is Here

strategy.earlyGame: Casting Shattered Ice gives her brief vision of the blast area and any enemy it hits. Fire it into the river brush while clearing waves and you can check whether the enemy jungler is waiting there. Leaving combat gives her the Frozen Heart shield, and enemies who chip it with physical damage get chilled. While the shield is up, she can take trades more readily; once it breaks, step back and wait for it to return. Frigid Prison takes time to go off, so in this phase place it where your opponent stops to take a last hit.
strategy.midGame: Once she learns her Ultimate, she can drop Winter Is Here's snowstorm on the enemy's path and keep chilling anyone who walks through. Enemies inside the snowstorm are chilled again and again, slowing their Movement Speed and Attack Speed. Casting it also grants her shield again, so she can hold her ground in the trade right after placing it. When joining a gank, place Frigid Prison ahead of time where the enemy will flee. Enemies it freezes take Frigid Prison's extra damage, and allies get to hit a target that cannot move. Winter Is Here has a long cooldown, so save it for contested moments such as the fights before Shadow Tyrant or Overlord.
strategy.teamfight: Who Wang Zhaojun chills decides what she contributes to a teamfight. Chill lowers Attack Speed as well as Movement Speed, so stacking it on enemies who fight with Basic Attacks cuts their damage output. Before the fight starts, place Winter Is Here on the enemy backline and line Frigid Prison up with their escape route. Frozen enemies cannot move, so ask your team to focus them. With no movement skill, stand behind your allies, and if someone reaches you, freeze them before backing away.

combos.title: Slow, Then Freeze
combos.sequence: Skill 3 (Winter Is Here: snowstorm) → Skill 2 (Frigid Prison: freeze) → Skill 1 (Shattered Ice) → Basic Attack (third hit, icicles)
combos.description: Enemies slowed by the snowstorm's chill have a harder time walking out of Frigid Prison before it goes off. A landed freeze also brings Frigid Prison's extra damage, and the target cannot move, so stack Shattered Ice and the icicles before it ends.

combos.title: Freeze the Retreat
combos.sequence: Skill 2 (Frigid Prison: where they will fall back) → Skill 1 (Shattered Ice: chill and vision) → Basic Attack (enhanced)
combos.description: Frigid Prison takes a moment to go off, so placing it behind a moving target tends to come too late. Aim at where they are heading; a landed freeze lets your allies catch up. Shattered Ice also reveals enemies it hits, so ducking into brush won't hide them.

combos.title: Look Before You Commit
combos.sequence: Skill 1 (Shattered Ice: into brush) → check the vision → Skill 2 (Frigid Prison: at whoever shows up)
combos.description: Shattered Ice gives vision of its blast area, so a cast into brush tells you whether someone is hiding there. Its cooldown is short, so using it to scout costs little. If an enemy shows up, go place Frigid Prison; if not, return to the wave.

strengths: Chill lowers both Movement Speed and Attack Speed, cutting down how often basic attackers can hit
Casting Winter Is Here grants her Frozen Heart shield again
Shattered Ice reveals the blast area and any enemy it hits
Frozen enemies take Frigid Prison's extra damage, which lines up well with allied follow-up
weaknesses: Frigid Prison has a delay before it goes off, making moving enemies hard to hit
No movement skill; once someone reaches her, chill and freeze are all she has to defend herself
Enemies who step out of the snowstorm stop taking its damage and chill
Winter Is Here has a long cooldown, so a wasted cast is hard to make up for

playstyle.style: Wang Zhaojun is a mage who slows enemies' feet and attacks with chill, then stops them with the freeze of Frigid Prison. Leaving combat gives her the Frozen Heart shield, and casting Winter Is Here grants it again. She has no movement skill, so chill and freeze also have to protect her.
playstyle.suited: Frigid Prison goes off some time after it is placed, so she suits players who can read where an enemy will move and place it there first. Winter Is Here has a long cooldown, and where you spend it shapes the teamfight. She also fits players who would rather set a trap where the enemy will walk than dive in themselves.

synergy.reason: Guiguzi strips their armor and pulls them into a stun, so Gao Changgong's dive lands on a helpless target.
Zhang Fei shields the dive and stuns enemies at the edge of his wind, so Gao Changgong lands on a frozen target.

counters.reason: Shouyue builds Ambush stacks while out of combat, so his pierce-boosted shots chip Gao Changgong down as he approaches.
Ata heals back from the damage he deals, so trading blows with him gets Gao Changgong nowhere.

passive.description: Gao Changgong's Movement Speed is increased by 15-30% when moving toward enemy heroes.
passive.name: Secret Skill - Rush

skill1.description:
Gao Changgong slashes enemies within range, dealing 400 (400 + 135% extra physical attack) physical damage. He also summons a shadow copy of himself to attack a random nearby enemy, which deals the same physical damage he does.
The shadow copy prioritizes attacking heroes with low Health.
skill1.name: Secret Skill - Split

skill2.description: Gao Changgong throws a shadow dagger in the target direction, dealing 200 (200 + 90% extra physical attack) physical damage to the first enemy it hits and slowing them immensely for 2s, which diminishes over time. Dagger hits place marks on enemies for 3s. His attacks on marked targets will stun them for 1s and restore 350 (350 + 10% extra Health) Health to him. When marks disappear, the enemy takes physical damage equal to 152 (140 + 12% lost Health) (plus an extra 1% for every 50 extra physical attack). The dagger is destroyed upon hitting an enemy hero.
skill2.name: Secret Skill - Sling

skill3.description: Gao Changgong immediately exits stealth, charging toward the target direction and dealing 750 (750 + 255% extra physical attack) physical damage to enemies in his path.
skill3.name: Secret Skill - Strike

skill4.description: After a 1.5s delay, Gao Changgong enters stealth for 30s while gaining 15%-30% Movement Speed for 5s. Upon leaving stealth, he gains 30%-60% Attack Speed for 5s. Staying near an enemy while in stealth for over 3s will remove stealth automatically. Movement Speed and Attack Speed boosts scale with hero level.
skill4.name: Secret Skill - Shadow

strategy.earlyGame: Until he has his ultimate and the full sequence, Gao Changgong focuses on clearing the jungle. Only with Secret Skill - Strike's charge does the chain from dagger to marked stun come together. His passive speeds him up only while moving toward enemy heroes, so ganks work best approaching through bushes rather than head-on.
strategy.midGame: As his physical attack and pierce items come together, his ability to finish targets rises. The mark from Secret Skill - Sling deals damage based on lost Health when it fades, so chipping the target first and then letting the mark expire makes it hit harder. Attacking a marked target stuns them and heals him, so he can make it back from fairly aggressive dives. Go for enemies pushing side lanes alone or supports coming out to take vision; once the dagger lands, the stun and mark damage often finish them. Removing one enemy right before Overlord or Shadow Tyrant becomes a numbers advantage on its own.
strategy.teamfight: Avoid diving in first. He is fragile and dies to a single crowd control effect, so wait until the enemy's lockdown has been spent on your front line before circling behind. Open with Secret Skill - Sling; a hit slows the target heavily, but the slow fades over time, so close in during the first moment. Closing the distance with Secret Skill - Strike and following with the stun from attacking the mark is the main pattern. Secret Skill - Split's shadow copy prioritizes low-Health heroes on its own, so it picks up wounded enemies he cannot reach.

combos.title: Strike From Stealth
combos.sequence: Skill 4 (Secret Skill - Shadow: vanish and speed up) → Skill 3 (Secret Skill - Strike: appear and charge) → Skill 2 (Secret Skill - Sling: slow and mark) → Basic Attack (attack the mark to stun and heal) → Skill 1 (Secret Skill - Split)
combos.description: Get behind the target while invisible, close in with the charge, then land the dagger. Leaving stealth raises his attack speed for a while, so his hits keep coming through to the attack on the mark. A missed dagger means no stun and no healing, so get within range before throwing it.

combos.title: Mark, Hit, and Leave
combos.sequence: Skill 2 (Secret Skill - Sling: slow and mark) → Basic Attack (stun and heal) → Skill 1 (Secret Skill - Split) → back off (the mark fades for extra damage)
combos.description: This is for moments when he cannot chase. The mark fades after a short time and deals damage based on the target's lost Health as it does. The shadow copy prioritizes low-Health heroes, so it keeps chipping even after he backs off.

strengths: Attacking a Secret Skill - Sling mark stuns the target, and the fading mark deals damage based on lost Health
His passive speeds him up toward enemy heroes, making chases and ganks easier
Attacking marked targets heals him, so he survives aggressive dives
Secret Skill - Split's shadow copy automatically targets low-Health enemies and picks off stragglers
weaknesses: He is fragile and can die to a single crowd control effect
Missing Secret Skill - Sling means no stun and no mark damage
Few ways to fight head-on, so he struggles in the middle of a teamfight
Secret Skill - Strike is his only movement skill, so retreating after chasing is hard

playstyle.style: Gao Changgong is a jungler who vanishes with Secret Skill - Shadow, closes in unseen, marks his target and finishes them. A target hit by Secret Skill - Sling's dagger is marked; attacking them stuns them and heals him, and when the mark fades they take extra damage based on their lost Health. His passive speeds him up while moving toward enemy heroes, which also makes him strong at chasing.
playstyle.suited: Most of his game is time spent invisible while closing in. He suits players who enjoy planning many ways to enter a fight, from which bush to who to target. Whether he lands the dagger the moment he appears changes the outcome a lot, so he needs the composure to wait until he is in range.

synergy.reason: Zhuangzi's Butterfly Effect strips crowd control and grants immunity, so Mulan can dive in without hesitation.

counters.reason: Liang's barriers stun the first enemy to touch them, so Mulan's dashes only lock her down.
Mi Yue vanishes with Umbral Moon and wipes the debuffs, so Balance rarely builds to its detonation.

passive.name: Great Wall Guardian
passive.description:
While her dual swords are drawn, Mulan gains 40 Movement Speed, and each time her Basic Attacks or skills deal damage, she places 1 stack of Balance on enemy heroes for 5s. At 5 stacks, the marks detonate, dealing 225 (140% physical attack) physical damage to the target, silencing them and slowing them immensely for 1s, and restoring 80 (80 + 1% extra Health) Health to Mulan. Effect is halved against non-hero units.
While her heavy sword is drawn, her Attack Speed is reduced, but Basic Attacks deal an extra (50% physical attack) damage. She also gains crowd control immunity and 45% damage reduction while using skills.

skill1.name: Snaking Strike / Sundering Slash

forms.description:
Mulan dashes in the target direction. During the dash, she can dash again by using the movement wheel. Each dash deals 134 (70 + 40% physical attack) physical damage to enemies in her path.
If she hits an enemy during the dash, she can use this skill again within 5s.

Mulan charges up and swings her sword in the target direction, dealing 216 (120 + 60% physical attack) −1,083 (600 + 300% physical attack) physical damage to enemies within range. Damage dealt depends on the duration of the charge.
If she charges up for 0.75s, hit enemies are slowed by 25% for 2s.
If she charges up for 1.5s or more, hit enemies are launched for 0.5s.
If she hits an enemy with this skill, she can use it again within 5s.

skill1.description:
Mulan dashes in the target direction. During the dash, she can dash again by using the movement wheel. Each dash deals 134 (70 + 40% physical attack) physical damage to enemies in her path.
If she hits an enemy during the dash, she can use this skill again within 5s.

skill2.name: Dagger Waltz / Blade Flurry

forms.description:
Mulan throws a sword in the target direction, dealing 400 (400 + 110% extra physical attack) physical damage to enemies in its path. When the sword reaches its max range, it spins in place for 3s, dealing 160 (160 + 50% extra physical attack) physical damage to enemies within range every 0.5s and reducing their Movement Speed by 25% for 1s.
She can retrieve the sword by walking next to it. Doing so reduces the skill's Cooldown by 5s.

Mulan advances in the target direction while slashing 4 times with her sword. Each slash deals 320 (320 + 85% extra physical attack) physical damage and knocks back enemies within range while reducing their Movement Speed by 25% for 2s.

skill2.description:
Mulan throws a sword in the target direction, dealing 400 (400 + 110% extra physical attack) physical damage to enemies in its path. When the sword reaches its max range, it spins in place for 3s, dealing 160 (160 + 50% extra physical attack) physical damage to enemies within range every 0.5s and reducing their Movement Speed by 25% for 1s.
She can retrieve the sword by walking next to it. Doing so reduces the skill's Cooldown by 5s.

skill3.name: Blooming Blade

forms.description:
Mulan draws her heavy sword, gaining 45% damage reduction while doing so and dealing 377 (200 + 110% physical attack) physical damage to nearby enemies. She also gains 90 physical attack for 5s.
She gains access to her heavy sword skills while her heavy sword is drawn.

Mulan draws her dual swords and makes a sweeping slash, dealing 377 (200 + 110% physical attack) physical damage to nearby enemies and gaining 60% Attack Speed for 5s.
She gains 40 Movement Speed and can use her dual sword skills while her dual swords are drawn.

skill3.description:
Mulan draws her heavy sword, gaining 45% damage reduction while doing so and dealing 377 (200 + 110% physical attack) physical damage to nearby enemies. She also gains 90 physical attack for 5s.
She gains access to her heavy sword skills while her heavy sword is drawn.

strategy.earlyGame: Early on, Mulan faces her clash-lane opponent with dual swords. Stack Balance to five through short trades and build a lead with the detonation's silence and healing. Until she can switch to her heavy sword with Blooming Blade, don't chase kills; treat it as time to drill managing marks and retrieving her sword.
strategy.midGame: The basic flow is stacking five marks with dual swords, detonating them, switching to the heavy sword with Blooming Blade and following with Sundering Slash's charged swing. Her physical attack rises for a while right after switching, so finish the swing within that window. Silence only stops skills; the target can still walk, slowly. The September 10 update made the detonation restore Health and let marks be applied to minions.
strategy.teamfight: Mulan's job is silencing the action the enemy most needs to make. Move around the edge with dual swords placing marks, and time the fifth for the target she wants to stop. Landing the silence as a mage winds up a skill stops that cast. Then switch to the heavy sword and swing charged slashes in the brawl, relying on crowd control immunity. Coming in from the front gets her surrounded, so choose an entry from the side.

combos.title: Stack Five Balance to Silence
combos.sequence: Skill 1 (Snaking Strike: dash, recast if it hits) → Basic Attack → Skill 2 (Dagger Waltz: throw a sword that spins) → Basic Attack → Skill 1 (Snaking Strike: recast dash)
combos.description: A Balance stack is added each time her Basic Attacks or skills deal damage. The spinning sword deals damage repeatedly, so keeping the target in its spin builds stacks quickly. She can retrieve the thrown sword by walking over it, which shortens Dagger Waltz's cooldown, so throw it toward her escape route.

combos.title: Heavy Sword Charge After the Silence
combos.sequence: detonate five Balance stacks (silence and heavy slow) → Skill 3 (Blooming Blade: switch to the heavy sword) → Skill 1 (Sundering Slash: charge and swing) → Skill 2 (Blade Flurry: four slashes that knock back)
combos.description: The silence ends quickly, so what carries her through the charge is the heavy slow that remains and the crowd control immunity during heavy sword skills. A long charge adds a launch; if the target looks like escaping, swing early to take just the slow.

strengths: Detonating five Balance stacks silences the target and slows them heavily
Crowd control immunity and damage reduction during heavy sword skills let her swing without fear of crowd control
She can switch between dual-sword mobility and heavy-sword damage as the situation calls for
weaknesses: Sundering Slash misses easily if the target gets out of range while she charges
Snaking Strike's dash with her dual swords is her main way to close in, so she struggles against kiting
Misjudging when to switch leaves both her damage and mobility half-done

playstyle.style: Mulan is a fighter who switches between her dual swords and her heavy sword. With dual swords drawn she moves faster, stacks Balance on enemy heroes with Basic Attacks and skills, and at five stacks detonates them to silence the target and restore her Health. Drawing her heavy sword with Blooming Blade grants crowd control immunity and damage reduction while using skills, and her charged Sundering Slash hits hard.
playstyle.suited: She suits players who want to switch between two weapons within one match. She keeps deciding on the spot when to stack marks with her dual swords and when to charge swings with her heavy sword.

synergy.reason: Dun's stun and launch pin enemies in place, letting Erin fire freely from the back line.
Xiang Yu peels divers off Erin and cuts enemy damage output, so she survives being focused.

counters.reason: Lam's pull drags Erin in regardless of her slow immunity, so she cannot hold her distance.
Mai Shiranui's low-cooldown KACHOUSEN strips Erin's magical defense and keeps chipping her down.

passive.description:
Erin's Basic Attacks deal 166 (100% physical attack + 20% magical attack) physical damage and grant Energy. When Energy is at max, Erin speeds up, gains 1 stack of Laurel, and enhances her next Basic Attack.
Speed Up: Erin spends Energy to fly, increasing 30 Movement Speed per 100 magical attack, up to a maximum increase of 450 Movement Speed.
Enhanced Basic Attack: Erin's enhanced Basic Attack deals 269 (70 + 120% physical attack + 30% magical attack) physical damage to enemies in its path.
Her Pierce and Lifesteal stats are linked. Physical Pierce/Lifesteal and Magical Pierce/Lifesteal each use the higher of the two stats.
passive.name: Elf Dance

skill1.description:
Erin shoots a laurel leaf, dealing 510 (510 + 115% extra physical attack + 100% magical attack) magical damage to enemies hit and gaining a stack of Laurel. Upon hitting an enemy hero or flying to its maximum range, the leaf starts flying in a circle, and enemies that come into contact with the circle take 170 (170 + 38% extra physical attack + 33% magical attack) magical damage and are slowed by 15% for 1s.
The skill's cooldown is reduced by 0.1s for every 100 Magical Attack, for a reduction of up to 1.5s.
skill1.name: Dance - Leaf Greeting

skill2.description:
Blessed by the Luminescent Forest, Erin immediately recovers full Energy, gains her Passive effect (including Speed Up, 1 Laurel stack, and an enhanced Basic Attack) and obtains another stack of Laurel.
Erin also becomes immune to slow and gains 20% Attack Speed for 3s.
skill2.name: Twirl - Forest Whisper

skill3.description:
At max Energy, Erin gains a stack of Laurel. When the skill is activated, she gains 10% Movement Speed and continuously consumes Laurel stacks to shoot leaves. Each leaf shot deals 130 (72 + 35% physical attack + 25% magical attack) magical damage to the enemy within range with the lowest Health. Each shot also reduces the cooldown of Twirl - Forest Whisper by 0.2s.
Waltz - Laurel Bloom is only unlocked at 6 Laurels. Laurel can be stacked up to 12 times.
Every 3 leaves counts as 1 Basic Attack.
skill3.name: Waltz - Laurel Bloom

strategy.earlyGame: In lane, Erin fights by deciding what each bar of Energy is for. Her enhanced Basic Attack also hits enemies in its path, so firing from a spot where the minion wave and the opponent line up clears and pokes in a single shot. Flying spends Energy, so every bit used for movement delays the next enhanced attack and Laurel stack. When you want to trade, stay grounded and keep attacking, and when Dance - Leaf Greeting hits a hero, add the slow from the ring it spreads.
strategy.midGame: She moves faster while Waltz - Laurel Bloom runs, and the leaves it spends her stacks on pick out the lowest-Health enemy in range by themselves. Each leaf shortens Twirl - Forest Whisper's cooldown, so after the ultimate she can rebuild Energy and stacks quickly. Magical attack makes her flight faster and cuts the cooldown of Dance - Leaf Greeting. Her physical and magical Pierce each use the higher value, so if the magical pierce from Boots of the Arcane or Void Staff is larger, her physical damage uses it as well. If someone chases her, holding Twirl - Forest Whisper means she can back off without worrying about slows.
strategy.teamfight: Erin keeps attacking from behind her front line and opens Waltz - Laurel Bloom once the stacks are there. The leaves choose the lowest-Health enemy in range on their own, so she can focus on keeping her distance. When someone dives her, refill Energy with Twirl - Forest Whisper and fly back toward her team while slows cannot stop her. Hit the chaser with Dance - Leaf Greeting so the ring slows them down. Twirl only blocks slows, so while an enemy with a stun is nearby, stand a step further back.

combos.title: Stack Laurels, Then Open the Ultimate
combos.sequence: Skill 1 (Dance - Leaf Greeting: hit for one Laurel) → Basic Attack (fill Energy for another Laurel) → Skill 2 (Twirl - Forest Whisper: two Laurels at once) → Skill 3 (Waltz - Laurel Bloom)
combos.description: This sequence starts once her Laurel stacks are close to the number needed for the ultimate. Twirl - Forest Whisper adds two Laurel stacks in one go, so it saves the most time when you are just short of unlocking the ultimate. Build stacks first with Dance - Leaf Greeting and Basic Attacks, and the ultimate is ready right after Twirl. Every leaf the ultimate fires shortens Twirl's cooldown, so the next round of stacking starts sooner.

combos.title: Dodge the Dive and Shoot Back
combos.sequence: Skill 2 (Twirl - Forest Whisper: full Energy and slow immunity) → fly to open the gap → Skill 1 (Dance - Leaf Greeting: slowing ring) → Enhanced Basic Attack
combos.description: Twirl - Forest Whisper fills Energy even from empty, so she can fly again right after running dry. Open the distance while slows cannot touch her, then catch the chaser in the ring from Dance - Leaf Greeting. Her enhanced Basic Attack also hits enemies in its path, so a chaser lined up behind someone else can be hit together.

strengths: Twirl - Forest Whisper refills Energy at once and makes her immune to slows
Waltz - Laurel Bloom's leaves aim for the lowest-Health enemy in range on their own
Her physical and magical Pierce and Lifesteal each use the higher of the two values
Magical attack makes her flight faster and Dance - Leaf Greeting come back sooner
weaknesses: Waltz - Laurel Bloom stays locked until enough Laurel stacks build up
The more Energy she spends flying, the later her enhanced Basic Attack and Laurel stacks arrive
Spending Twirl - Forest Whisper just to move leaves her nothing to answer a dive
Twirl - Forest Whisper only stops slows; stuns and other crowd control still land

playstyle.style: Every time her Energy fills, Erin gains a Laurel stack and her next Basic Attack is enhanced. Once she has enough Laurel stacks, her ultimate, Waltz - Laurel Bloom, unlocks. Her damage holds up as long as Basic Attacks and Twirl - Forest Whisper keep feeding Laurel stacks into the ultimate.
playstyle.suited: Erin is a constant choice between shooting and flying, made by watching her Energy. Flying spends Energy, which pushes back her next enhanced Basic Attack and Laurel stack. If reading that gauge before every move feels like a chore, she will run short of Energy both for attacking and for escaping.

synergy.reason: Ming can land his defense-shredding instrument for certain on a hero pinned by Liang's suppression.
Yaria's attached shield soaks the incoming damage, so Liang can hold the full suppression instead of dying mid-channel.

counters.reason: Zhang Fei is immune to crowd control and invincible while roaring, so Liang's suppression is wasted entirely.
Li Bai's sword formation clears his debuffs and turns him untargetable, so Liang's suppression never lands.

passive.description: After Liang's Basic Attacks or skills deal damage to a target twice within 1.5s, he enters a state of continuous attack, during which he deals 120 (120 +70% magical attack) true damage to the target every 1.2s.
passive.name: Power Word - Trance

skill1.description:
Liang summons 4 magical barriers at the target location. When touched by an enemy, barriers disappear and deal 360 (360 +75% magical attack) magical damage while stunning the target for 0.75s. After the stun wears off, the enemy is slowed by 25% for 0.5s.
If the same enemy touches multiple barriers within a short period, subsequent barriers only deal half of the damage without the stun, and the enemy's is slowed by 25% for 1.25s.
skill1.name: Power Word - Barrier

skill2.description:
Liang conjures a circle of attrition at the target location for 5.5s. The circle deals 110 (110 + 24% magical attack) magical damage to 1 enemy within range every 0.5s and provides vision of the area. Non-hero enemy units take 50% more damage. He gains 60 Movement Speed while inside a circle of his.
He can have at most 2 circles up at the same time. He stocks 1 charge of the skill every 12s (affected by Cooldown Reduction), for up to 3 charges.
skill2.name: Power Word - Fate

skill3.description:
Liang uses a Power Word to suppress an enemy hero for 2.2s and deal 100 (100 +18% magical attack) magical damage to them every 0.5s.
If he finishes using this skill without being interrupted, a magic field is summoned at the target hero's location for 0.5s. Enemies that step into the field take 240 (240 +30% magical attack) magical damage and are stunned for 0.75s.
skill3.name: Power Word - Control

strategy.earlyGame: Liang opens by clearing mid waves with Power Word - Fate's circles. The circles are strong against minions and monsters, and he can keep two up at once, so placing one in a river bush doubles as vision. Once the wave is pushed, use that vision to join your jungler. Once he learns Power Word - Control, he constantly threatens to catch someone from mid.
strategy.midGame: After leaving lane, his main job is teaming up with the jungler to catch isolated enemies. Catching an enemy who comes to take vision before Tyrant or Shadow Tyrant can win the objective without a fight. He cannot move during the suppression either, so only use it within your team's reach; otherwise he is left alone once it ends. When moving around, walking through Power Word - Fate's circles speeds him up, which is worth making a habit.
strategy.teamfight: Stand behind your front line at the edge of Power Word - Control's range. Open by placing Power Word - Barrier on the enemy's path to blunt their approach with stuns, and lay Power Word - Fate at your feet to claim ground. Don't rush Power Word - Control; time it for the most dangerous enemy, such as a mobile assassin making their move. A stunning field is left at the target's feet when it ends, so coordinate with your team to finish them right as the suppression lifts.

combos.title: Pick Off With the Suppression
combos.sequence: Skill 2 (Power Word - Fate: circle for vision) → Skill 3 (Power Word - Control: suppress an enemy hero) → Skill 1 (Power Word - Barrier: barriers at their feet) → Basic Attack (keep damaging to sustain the true damage)
combos.description: The suppression is exactly the time your team needs to arrive. Only if he finishes the cast does a short field appear at the target's feet, stunning enemies who step in. If he is interrupted, the field does not appear, so cast from where enemies cannot reach him.

combos.title: Answer a Dive With Barriers
combos.sequence: Skill 1 (Power Word - Barrier: barriers on your escape path) → Skill 2 (Power Word - Fate: circle at your feet) → Basic Attack (back off with the speed from the circle)
combos.description: Barriers stun enemies who touch them and leave a slow afterward. Once the chaser stumbles, stand on his own circle for the speed boost and move away. The same enemy will not be stunned twice in a row, so treat the later barriers as slows.

strengths: Power Word - Control suppresses one enemy hero and gives his team time to focus them
Repeated hits add true damage, so his damage gets through tough targets
Power Word - Fate's circles clear waves while providing vision
Power Word - Barrier's barriers guard or block narrow paths
weaknesses: He cannot move while Power Word - Control is active, which makes it hard to use in a scramble
No movement skill, so ganks and assassin ambushes are dangerous
Barrier stuns do not land twice in a row on the same target
Low burst damage, so he rarely finishes kills on his own

playstyle.style: Liang is a mage whose ultimate, Power Word - Control, suppresses one enemy hero and buys time for his team to pile on. Power Word - Barrier's barriers stun enemies who touch them, and Power Word - Fate's circles damage enemies inside while granting vision. Dealing damage repeatedly in a short window keeps his passive true damage ticking.
playstyle.suited: He suits players who want to be the one their team asks to lock down a threat. He cannot move while Power Word - Control is active either, so how well he does depends on using it where his team's damage can reach. His own finishing damage is modest; his strength is setting up the stop that lets his team take the kill.

synergy.reason: Donghuang's suppression pins a hero in place, so Mai Shiranui can land her dash on a target that cannot move.
Sun Bin's Time Flux buffs nearby allies, so Mai Shiranui gets in and back out faster.

counters.reason: Liang can suppress a lone diver outright, so Mai Shiranui gets picked off the moment she goes in.
Mozi stacks a shield with every skill he casts, so Mai Shiranui's opening burst is absorbed before it lands.

passive.description:
Every 5s, Mai Shiranui enhances her next Basic Attack. The enhanced Basic Attack deals 100 (100 + 100% magical attack) magical damage to the target and knocks them back. Also restores 10 Energy to Mai Shiranui.
When Mai Shiranui is performing an enhanced Basic Attack or casting a skill, moving the movement wheel causes her to dash again and gain 50% Movement Speed that diminishes over 0.5s.
passive.name: HISSATSU SHINOBI-BACHI

skill1.description:
Mai Shiranui dashes in the target direction. At the end of the dash, she launches a flying kick, dealing 600 (600 + 80% magical attack) magical damage to enemies within range and launching them for 0.75s.
She recovers 25 Energy if an enemy is hit.
skill1.name: HISHOU RYUUENJIN

skill2.description: Mai Shiranui throws her fan in the target direction, dealing 470 (470 + 90% magical attack) magical damage to the first enemy hit, slowing them immensely for 0.5s, and reducing their magical defense by 50 for 3s. She recovers 10 Energy if she hits an enemy. After landing a hit, the fan deals an equal amount of magical damage (halved against heroes) to the closest unit behind the target.
skill2.name: KACHOUSEN

skill3.description:
Mai Shiranui dashes in the target direction, dealing 800 (800 + 110% magical attack) magical damage to all enemies in her path and knocking them back while reducing their physical attack by 20% for 2.5s.
She recovers 25 Energy for each enemy hit.
skill3.name: CHOU HISSATSU SHINOBI-BACHI

strategy.earlyGame: Early on, Mai Shiranui plays it safe in mid lane. Energy only comes back properly when skills land, so missing repeatedly leaves her unable to do anything in lane. KACHOUSEN does most of her wave clearing; it also reaches the unit behind the first target, so throwing it through minions at the opponent clears and pokes at once.
strategy.midGame: Once she learns CHOU HISSATSU SHINOBI-BACHI, push mid quickly and move to the side lanes. Start every engage with KACHOUSEN; its magical defense reduction lasts a while, so the same sequence deals different damage depending on whether the fan lands first. Moving the stick right after an enhanced attack or skill rolls her into a new position, letting her slip around walls to cut off escapes or roll out of the path of a counterattack. Her durability is low, so in head-on teamfights she pressures from the edges, flashing her rolls, and dives with KACHOUSEN into HISHOU RYUUENJIN the moment the enemy's crowd control is spent. CHOU HISSATSU SHINOBI-BACHI lowers the physical attack of those it hits, so landing it on the enemy marksman also protects her.
strategy.teamfight: Wait a little after the brawl starts and come in late. Stack HISHOU RYUUENJIN's launch on enemies whose magical defense KACHOUSEN has lowered, push them along with enhanced attacks, and finish with CHOU HISSATSU SHINOBI-BACHI. In case it does not work out, decide where you will roll to escape before diving in. Her attacking rolls and escaping rolls use the same input, so keeping an escape route in mind is what keeps her alive. Don't forget to pull back when her Energy runs low.

combos.title: Break Their Magical Defense, Then Go In
combos.sequence: Skill 2 (KACHOUSEN: lower magical defense and heavily slow) → Skill 1 (HISHOU RYUUENJIN: dash and launch) → Basic Attack (enhanced attack knocks back) → Skill 3 (CHOU HISSATSU SHINOBI-BACHI: dash, knock back, lower physical attack)
combos.description: Whether the fan's debuff lands first changes how much the same sequence takes off. The enhanced basic attack knocks the target back, so send CHOU HISSATSU SHINOBI-BACHI to where they land. This sequence uses a lot of Energy, so start it with a full gauge.

combos.title: Poke With the Fan Through Minions
combos.sequence: Skill 2 (KACHOUSEN: throw through minions to hit the enemy behind) → roll (move the stick during the skill) → Basic Attack (enhanced attack knocks back and restores Energy)
combos.description: The fan also hits the closest unit behind the first enemy it strikes. Damage to heroes is reduced, but it is one of her few ways to reach opponents hiding behind minions. She gets back less Energy than she spends, so only throw it while keeping enough for HISHOU RYUUENJIN.

strengths: Going in after KACHOUSEN lowers magical defense makes her follow-up skills hit harder
Two dashes and her rolls let her move in and out quickly
Launches, knockbacks and a physical attack reduction give her some self-defense
As long as her skills land, Energy keeps returning and she can keep fighting
weaknesses: Missed skills drain her Energy and leave stretches where she can do nothing
No skills raise her durability, so a single crowd control effect can kill her
Rolling in the wrong direction can carry her into danger
Her inputs are demanding, so differences in practice turn directly into differences in damage

playstyle.style: Mai Shiranui is a mage who spends Energy on her skills and earns it back by landing them, fighting at close range. Her periodically enhanced basic attack knocks enemies back, and moving the stick during an enhanced attack or a skill lets her dash again to reposition. KACHOUSEN lowers the magical defense of the target it hits, which makes the HISHOU RYUUENJIN and CHOU HISSATSU SHINOBI-BACHI that follow hit harder.
playstyle.suited: She suits players who enjoy chaining dashes and rolls without stopping. She has no skills that raise her durability, so deciding when to go in and where to roll out ahead of time matters.

synergy.reason: Lu Bu's ultimate has a long cooldown, and Celestial Melody hands it right back after he leaps.
Shangguan's Finishing Stroke sits at its longest cooldown right after a full dash chain, exactly what Celestial Melody resets.

counters.reason: Dharma slams Dolia into a wall for a stun, and that wall powers up his follow-up kick.
Mozi stacks stuns from his shell and barrier, and they keep interrupting Dolia's Celestial Melody channel.

passive.description:
Dolia takes the form of a mermaid while in water, reducing slow effects by 50% and recovering 60 (60 + 1% extra Health) Health and 5 Mana every second. Her Basic Attacks become splashes of water that deal area damage.
Her Recovery skill becomes Mermaid's Gift, which can be used to form a covenant with a selected teammate. This teammate becomes the priority target for Celestial Melody.
passive.name: Mermaid's Gift

skill1.description:
Dolia sings, unleashing 4 soundwaves that spread out around her. The first 3 deal 135 (135 + 20% magical attack) magical damage and inflict a 7.5% slow.
The 4th soundwave deals 270 (270 + 40% magical attack) magical damage and inflicts a 30% slow for 1s. This soundwave triggers echoes when hitting enemies, dealing 150 (150 + 24% magical attack) magical damage. While in water, it stirs up a wave that knocks back nearby enemies and stuns enemies next to her.
Echoes triggered by non-hero units have a shorter range and only deal 50% damage.
skill1.name: Ode

skill2.description:
Dolia leaps forward and transforms into a mermaid. If she lands on solid ground, she creates a pool of water and restores 320 (320 + 40% magical attack) Health to her and her nearby teammates. While in the pool, teammates recover Health and Mana at the same rate as Dolia's.
Cooldown is reduced by 25% if used while in water.
The pool disappears if she leaves it for 4s.
skill2.name: Wavemaker

skill3.description:
Dolia channels for a short time, resetting the cooldown of a skill for a teammate within range. The skill that gets reset is the one with the longest remaining cooldown. In return, Dolia takes on a Cooldown of 10 (+120% of the current skill Cooldown) seconds herself.
If the teammate does not use the reset skill, the cooldown of Celestial Melody is reduced by 20%. If the teammate uses the reset skill within 5s, it does not consume Energy, and any earnings from defeating enemies with that skill are shared evenly with Dolia.
This skill prioritizes the teammate with whom she has formed a covenant. If no teammates are nearby, she resets one of her own skills. If the reset fails, the cooldown of Celestial Melody is significantly reduced.
skill3.name: Celestial Melody

strategy.earlyGame: The first decision is which ally to bond with through Mermaid's Gift. That ally gets priority for Celestial Melody, so pick someone with a big, long-cooldown skill whose second cast would swing a fight. Early on, stay near your partner and look for fights in the river. In the river she takes her mermaid form, recovering Health and Mana, and Ode gains a knockback against nearby enemies.
strategy.midGame: Cast Celestial Melody right after an ally's big skill, and the enemy faces a move they thought they had already dodged. If the ally uses the reset skill right away and gets a kill with it, the rewards are split evenly with Dolia. Wavemaker's cooldown is shorter when cast from water, so she can leap more often while the fight stays on the water. The August 27 update raised Ode's fourth soundwave the most, so standing where she can finish all four waves without backing off pays off more than before. If she dies, the resets stop, so stand behind your covenant partner.
strategy.teamfight: Put a pool under your team with Wavemaker before the fight starts. Allies on the water fight while recovering, and divers who reach them get pushed back by Ode. On top of that, follow an ally's big skill with Celestial Melody. The pool vanishes shortly after Dolia leaves it, so place it where she will not need to move far. When retreating, the water also lightens the slows she takes, making her harder to catch.

combos.title: Bring the Water, Push Them Back
combos.sequence: Skill 2 (Wavemaker: leap and create a pool on landing) → Skill 1 (Ode: in water, knocks back nearby enemies) → Basic Attack (area splash)
combos.description: Even far from the river, landing Wavemaker on solid ground creates a pool, and Ode gains its knockback. That makes it her tool for prying an enemy off an ally, so leap toward the teammate you want to protect.

combos.title: Your Ally's Big Skill, Twice
combos.sequence: Ally casts a major skill → Skill 3 (Celestial Melody: resets the skill with the longest remaining cooldown) → Skill 2 (Wavemaker: pool for sustain)
combos.description: Celestial Melody resets whichever skill has the longest remaining cooldown. Cast it right after an ally's big skill and that is the one that comes back.

strengths: Celestial Melody lets an ally cast a skill again
In water she recovers Health and Mana and takes lighter slows
Wavemaker brings a pool of water anywhere, not just the river
The covenant lets her choose in advance who Celestial Melody serves
weaknesses: Celestial Melody puts a long cooldown on her, based on the skill she reset
With no ally nearby, Celestial Melody can only reset one of her own skills
Out of the water, Ode loses its knockback
Her only movement is Wavemaker's leap, so once it is used she struggles to escape

playstyle.style: While standing in the river or any pool of water, Dolia changes into her mermaid form. She keeps recovering Health and Mana, and Ode gains a wave that knocks back nearby enemies, so the water itself becomes her battlefield. Her other pillar is her ultimate, Celestial Melody, which resets one ally's skill so they can cast the same move again.
playstyle.suited: Celestial Melody resets an ally's skill; it does not damage enemies. The faster you can see which skill an ally just used and decide who to reset and when, the more that ultimate is worth. You also need to plan where the water goes, so the question is whether you enjoy setting up the ground your team fights on.

synergy.reason: Lady Zhen's Destructive Deluge slows enemies down, leaving them easy targets for Nakoruru's AMUBE YATORO.
Guiguzi's The Animist clumps enemies together and stuns them, so KAMUI MUTSUBE's charge hits the whole group.

counters.reason: Zhang Fei's spear sweep knocks enemy heroes away, so Nakoruru gets shoved back when she dives him head-on.
Wukong's Protective Shroud eats one of Nakoruru's skills outright and hands him a shield in return.

passive.description: When Nakoruru hits an enemy with a skill, her next Basic Attack is enhanced, for up to 3 stacks. Her next Basic Attack summons Mamahaha, who deals damage to nearby enemies based on the number of stacks, with each stack dealing 120 (120 + 37% extra physical attack) physical damage.
passive.name: DANCING SWORD ARTS

skill1.description:
Nakoruru summons Mamahaha to attack the enemy, dealing 400 (400 + 125% extra physical attack) physical damage and marking them with an Eagle Eye Mark.
Further damage dealt by her will activate the marks, dealing physical damage equal to 6% of the target's Health (max damage to monsters from the mark capped at 300).
Every 40 additional Physical Attack increases max Health by 1%. Activating the mark will reduce the cooldown of AMUBE YATORO by 2.5s and recover 35 Mana.
skill1.name: AMUBE YATORO

skill2.description:
Nakoruru dashes forward, dealing 400 (400 + 130% extra physical attack) physical damage to enemies in her path. For every enemy hero hit, she recovers 400 (400 + 5% extra Health) Health.
When this skill hits a monster, it deals 50% more damage. Hitting non-hero units restores 50% of the Health restored when hitting heroes.
skill2.name: RERA MUTSUBE

skill3.description:
Nakoruru summons Mamahaha, gaining 50% Movement Speed for 6s which diminishes over time. She can ignore terrain once while flying.
Using this skill again causes her to charge toward the target area, dealing 700 (700 + 195% extra physical attack) physical damage to enemies within range. Enemies hit by her are slowed by 25% and deal 30% less damage for 3s.
Passive: Nakoruru summons Mamahaha to fly with her after staying out of combat for 4s, increasing her Movement Speed by 10%. She loses the Movement Speed increase upon re-entering combat.
skill3.name: KAMUI MUTSUBE

strategy.earlyGame: Nakoruru's jungle clear starts with RERA MUTSUBE. It deals extra damage to monsters and heals on hit, so she keeps both clear speed and Health. The thing to watch is Mana: triggering AMUBE YATORO's mark with other damage restores it. Make a habit of following up to trigger every mark you apply. Once she learns KAMUI MUTSUBE, its speed boost and terrain hop let her gank from directions the enemy is not watching.
strategy.midGame: From the mid game on, ganks from outside vision using the wall hop are her main weapon. Fly in along paths the enemy cannot see, mark with AMUBE YATORO, and trigger it with the charge to add damage based on the target's Health. In fights over Tyrant or Shadow Tyrant, land KAMUI MUTSUBE's charge on the enemy jungler. Enemies hit by the charge deal less damage for a while, giving her the edge in trades over objectives. Her marks still get through as enemy frontliners grow tougher. She has few ways out after diving, so avoid opening fights and instead wait in bushes for worn-down or isolated enemies. After staying out of combat for a while she flies with Mamahaha for extra speed, so pause in a bush after a fight before heading to the next spot. The November 5 update raised the damage of AMUBE YATORO and KAMUI MUTSUBE.
strategy.teamfight: Nakoruru enters from the side or behind. Her first job is not damage but landing KAMUI MUTSUBE's charge on the enemy's main damage dealer to cut their damage output. After that, chase down worn-down enemies around AMUBE YATORO's mark and trigger, weaving in enhanced basic attacks. Each activation shortens AMUBE YATORO's cooldown, so as long as she keeps landing it her damage rarely breaks off.

combos.title: Over the Wall to Trigger the Mark
combos.sequence: Skill 3 (KAMUI MUTSUBE: speed up and hop terrain once) → Skill 1 (AMUBE YATORO: Eagle Eye Mark) → Skill 3 (use again to charge and trigger the mark) → Skill 2 (RERA MUTSUBE: dash and heal) → Basic Attack (enhanced)
combos.description: Hop the wall with KAMUI MUTSUBE's speed, apply the mark, then trigger it with the recast charge. RERA MUTSUBE to finish also restores Health when it hits an enemy hero.

combos.title: Clearing Without Running Out of Mana
combos.sequence: Skill 2 (RERA MUTSUBE: dash into monsters and heal) → Skill 1 (AMUBE YATORO: mark) → Basic Attack (enhanced attack triggers the mark)
combos.description: RERA MUTSUBE's healing is lower when it hits non-hero units. The mark's damage to monsters is capped, but the cooldown reduction and Mana recovery still come back in full, so cycling in this order lets her reach the next camp without running out of Mana.

strengths: KAMUI MUTSUBE's speed boost and terrain hop let her gank from outside vision
The Eagle Eye Mark deals damage based on the target's Health, so her damage gets through high-Health targets
Enemies hit by KAMUI MUTSUBE's charge deal less damage for a while
RERA MUTSUBE deals extra damage to monsters and heals on hit, so clearing costs her little
weaknesses: Few ways to escape after diving in, so a failed engage is hard to get out of
Heavy Mana costs, and she runs dry quickly if she can't activate her marks
No way to remove or block crowd control, so hard crowd control often leads straight to her death
KAMUI MUTSUBE's speed boost fades over time, so ambushes work less well against enemies who are waiting for her

playstyle.style: Nakoruru is a jungle assassin who fights alongside her hawk, Mamahaha. Every skill hit enhances her next Basic Attack, and that attack summons Mamahaha to damage nearby enemies. The Eagle Eye Mark from AMUBE YATORO activates when she deals further damage, dealing damage based on the target's Health.
playstyle.suited: She suits players who can reliably carry out the two-step routine of applying the mark and then triggering it with other damage. Activating the mark shortens AMUBE YATORO's cooldown and restores Mana, so the better you keep to that routine, the longer her damage keeps flowing. She has few ways out after diving in with her ultimate, so judging which target to enter on and when is also essential.

synergy.reason: Lian Po's Tremor Smash launches enemies and holds them still, so Ukyo's tip-range damage finally connects.
Zhang Fei's Unbridled Outburst stuns enemies at the end of its wind, so Ukyo lands every Snowfall Slash and heals.

counters.reason: Arthur's silence cuts Ukyo's combo short, and the quick-draw slash's slow only adds to his passive healing.
Han Xin can chain his leaps back to back, so any distance Ukyo opens up closes again at once.

passive.description:
Ukyo Tachibana's next Basic Attack is enhanced to a quick-draw slash that has longer range, dealing 40 (40 + 35% extra physical attack) physical damage to enemies and slowing them by 15−30% (scales with hero level) for 2s. Enemies on the edge of the attack take 80 (80 + 70% extra physical attack) extra physical damage. Damage is halved against non-hero units. He recovers 125 (125 + 2% extra Health) Health.
The quick-draw slash has a cooldown of 4−5s (scales with hero level). Cooldown is shortened by 0.5s upon dealing skill damage.
passive.name: CONCEALED SABRE HAZY BLADE

skill1.description:
Ukyo Tachibana leaps backward and slashes enemies in his path, dealing 330 (330 + 150% extra physical attack) physical damage and activating the skill's second phase. If no enemy units are hit, the second phase will be activated after 2s.
If he returns near the start point of phase 1 after using phase 2, he enhances the second phase to slash enemies in a larger range, and his Ultimate's Cooldown is reduced by 1s for every enemy hero hit (halved for non-hero units). For every 2% Health lost by the target, this skill's damage is increased by 1%.
skill1.name: CONCEALED SABRE SWALLOW SWIPE

skill2.description:
Ukyo Tachibana slashes in the target direction, dealing 600 (600 + 200% extra physical attack) physical damage to enemies within range.
Enemies at the far end of the area are stunned for 0.75s.
skill2.name: CONCEALED SABRE HEAVENLY HACK

skill3.description:
Ukyo Tachibana quickly slashes 4 times in the target direction, with each slash dealing 240 (240 + 75% extra physical attack) physical damage to enemies within range. If an enemy hero is hit, each slash restores 300 (300 + 4.5% extra Health) Health to him.
The healing is halved if only non-hero units are hit.
skill3.name: CONCEALED SABRE SNOWFALL SLASH

strategy.earlyGame: Ukyo Tachibana clears the jungle while weaving the quick-draw slash between skills. Both the quick-draw slash and CONCEALED SABRE HEAVENLY HACK gain their extra effects at the tip of their reach, so train the tip distance into your hands while clearing. Once he learns CONCEALED SABRE SNOWFALL SLASH, healing whenever it hits an enemy hero makes trading easier to sustain.
strategy.midGame: From the mid game on, drawing enemies out in side lanes suits him. Push a wave, fight at tip range if one enemy comes, and leave with CONCEALED SABRE SWALLOW SWIPE's two-step leap if two do. Crowd control easily gets him killed, so while the enemy still has lockdown skills ready, watch from a step back. In fights over Tyrant or Overlord, don't walk in from the front; wait on the flank and go in with CONCEALED SABRE HEAVENLY HACK on a worn-down enemy the moment their formation breaks. The September 23 update raised the damage of HEAVENLY HACK and CONCEALED SABRE SNOWFALL SLASH.
strategy.teamfight: Even in the middle of a brawl, keep measuring the tip distance. Too close and the extra damage does not come out; too far and nothing lands. Leap back with CONCEALED SABRE SWALLOW SWIPE after seeing an enemy dash, then land the quick-draw slash with its tip as he touches down, and the chaser ends up taking the damage. CONCEALED SABRE SNOWFALL SLASH heals more when it catches an enemy hero and only half when it hits minions alone, so pick the direction you slash.

combos.title: Far-End Stun Into Four Slashes
combos.sequence: Skill 2 (CONCEALED SABRE HEAVENLY HACK: stun with the far end) → Skill 3 (CONCEALED SABRE SNOWFALL SLASH: four slashes that heal) → Basic Attack (quick-draw slash: extra damage at the tip)
combos.description: CONCEALED SABRE HEAVENLY HACK only stuns enemies caught at the far end of its area, so put the target at the edge before slashing. While they are stopped, pour in all four CONCEALED SABRE SNOWFALL SLASH hits and heal as you chip them down. Every bit of skill damage shortens the quick-draw slash's cooldown, so the finishing strike is ready in time.

combos.title: Swallow Swipe Round-Trip Trade
combos.sequence: Skill 1 (CONCEALED SABRE SWALLOW SWIPE: leap back and slash) → Basic Attack (quick-draw slash at the tip) → Skill 1 (second phase: return near the start for the enhanced slash)
combos.description: Hitting an enemy with CONCEALED SABRE SWALLOW SWIPE lets him use the second phase right away. Ending the second phase near where the first began enhances it, widening the slash, and hitting enemies with it shortens his Ultimate's cooldown. The more Health the target has lost, the more damage SWALLOW SWIPE deals.

strengths: Hitting with the tip adds the quick-draw slash's extra damage and CONCEALED SABRE HEAVENLY HACK's stun
CONCEALED SABRE SNOWFALL SLASH heals him when it hits an enemy hero, so he holds up in small brawls
CONCEALED SABRE SWALLOW SWIPE's two-step leap works for both engaging and escaping
Every bit of skill damage shortens the quick-draw slash's cooldown, keeping his attacks flowing
weaknesses: Misjudging range makes both his damage and his stun hard to land
Few defensive skills, so crowd control often gets him killed
CONCEALED SABRE SWALLOW SWIPE moves in an unusual way, and mistakes are common until you are used to it
In head-on teamfights full of crowd control, he struggles to keep his spacing

playstyle.style: Ukyo Tachibana is a swordsman jungler whose effects change depending on whether he hits with the tip of his reach. The quick-draw slash deals extra damage to enemies on the edge of the attack, and CONCEALED SABRE HEAVENLY HACK stuns only enemies at the far end of its area. CONCEALED SABRE SWALLOW SWIPE leaps him backward with a slash, and its second phase lets him reposition again.
playstyle.suited: He suits players who can measure the distance to their opponent one step at a time. Whether he hits with the tip changes both his damage and his stun, so standing too close or too far wastes his strength. CONCEALED SABRE SWALLOW SWIPE is a skill you press while thinking about where you leap and where you come back, so it takes practice.

synergy.reason: Luban No.7's bombs only fall on enemies standing inside the area, and Arthur's launch keeps them there.
Arke only crits from behind, and Arthur's launch freezes the target long enough for her to circle around.

counters.reason: Lu Bu always carries either true damage or physical pierce, so Arthur's bulk buys him nothing.
Mi Yue vanishes into Umbral Moon immune to everything, so Might of Excalibur lands on nothing.

passive.description: Arthur invokes the Holy Vanguard to recover 100 (100 + 2.5% extra Health) Health every 2s. If his Movement Speed is impaired, he recovers an extra 100 (100 + 2.5% extra Health) Health every 2s.
passive.name: Holy Vanguard

skill1.description:
Arthur gains 30% Movement Speed for 3s and enhances his next Basic Attack, where he dashes forward to deal 325 (325 + 100% extra physical attack) physical damage and silence the target for 1.25s.
The enhanced Basic Attack also marks the target enemy hero for 5s. His Basic Attacks and skills deal extra magical damage to marked enemies equal to 1% of their Health.
Allies near marked enemies gain 10% Movement Speed.
skill1.name: Valiant Charge

skill2.description: Arthur summons holy shields that orbit him for 5s, dealing 285 (145 +80% physical attack) physical damage every second to nearby enemies.
skill2.name: Whirling Strike

skill3.description:
Arthur raises Excalibur and leaps at the target enemy hero, dealing magical damage equal to 16% of their Health and leaving behind a holy seal. Enemies within range of the seal are launched for 0.5s.
The seal lasts 5s and deals 85 magical damage to enemies within range every second.
skill3.name: Might of Excalibur

strategy.earlyGame: Trades start with Valiant Charge's enhanced attack. Dash in to silence and mark the target, keep Whirling Strike spinning, and the opponent cannot answer with skills during the silence. Since the 30 July update, the enhanced attack can be fired in a direction even with no enemy nearby, moving him forward a set distance. That makes it a step toward someone out of reach, or a step away when you need to back off. Holy Vanguard keeps restoring Health after you get chipped, so you can keep cycling out and back in.
strategy.midGame: Ganks are where Might of Excalibur does its work. The leap targets an enemy hero, so it reaches whoever your jungler is attacking, and the silence from Valiant Charge can follow the launch. Allies near a marked enemy move faster, so the whole team can run down a fleeing target. Because the ultimate's damage scales with the target's Health, it works on back-liners and frontliners alike. Silenced enemies cannot use skills, so going after a mage with a big spell makes it easier to finish them without a skill coming back at you. If an attempt goes wrong, Holy Vanguard's regeneration lets him recover before heading to the next one.
strategy.teamfight: The plan is simple: leap onto your target with Might of Excalibur, stop the reply with Valiant Charge's silence, and keep swinging with Whirling Strike up. With so little to execute, target choice is where Arthur makes his difference. Default to the enemy backline, but if an enemy has dived your own carries, stopping that hero first keeps your team from collapsing. Whirling Strike keeps dealing damage while he moves, so spin it on the chase and on the retreat.

combos.title: An Engage That Cannot Whiff
combos.sequence: Skill 3 (Might of Excalibur: leap at the target and launch) → Skill 1 (Valiant Charge: enhance the next Basic Attack) → Basic Attack (enhanced: dash, silence and mark) → Skill 2 (Whirling Strike) → Basic Attack
combos.description: Might of Excalibur targets an enemy hero, so the opener cannot miss. Layer the enhanced attack's silence before the launch wears off and the target takes the hits without answering. Marked enemies take extra magical damage from his Basic Attacks and skills, which is why it pays to finish with Whirling Strike.

combos.title: Spin Before You Commit
combos.sequence: Skill 2 (Whirling Strike: start the shields first) → Skill 1 (Valiant Charge: speed boost) → Basic Attack (enhanced: dash and silence) → Basic Attack (extra damage on the mark)
combos.description: With the shields already spinning, every moment he stays attached after the dash is damage. The silence stops the target from fighting back with skills, so he can finish the exchange and step out. Holy Vanguard then restores his Health while he waits for the next trade.

strengths: Might of Excalibur targets an enemy hero, so it reaches the one you chose
Valiant Charge's silence opens a window where the target cannot answer with skills
Might of Excalibur scales with the target's Health, so it hits high-Health frontliners by the same share
Regular Health recovery, boosted while his Movement Speed is impaired
weaknesses: No shields or invulnerability; focus fire has to be survived on regeneration
His only gap closers are Valiant Charge and Might of Excalibur, and once both are spent he cannot close in again
Using Valiant Charge to engage leaves no speed boost for the retreat
Whirling Strike only hits around his own body

playstyle.style: Arthur is built around two tools: Might of Excalibur, which leaps onto the enemy hero he picks, and Valiant Charge, which silences. Holy Vanguard restores his Health at regular intervals, and more while his Movement Speed is impaired, so getting chipped rarely forces him off the front line.
playstyle.suited: Once you decide who gets Might of Excalibur, the rest of the sequence mostly follows. The real decisions are about target choice, which makes him comfortable for players who would rather read the fight than juggle a complex kit. He has no shields or invulnerability, so players who want plenty of ways out of focus fire may find him lacking.

synergy.reason: Kongming's Winning Strategy hits harder the more Health the target has lost, so Wukong's opening damage feeds it.
Heino's melee Scepter of Fate slows enemies, giving Wukong a clean run straight at them.

counters.reason: Agudo rolls straight through hard crowd control, so Wukong's Golden Cudgel launch simply vanishes.
Gao chips away nonstop while String Bender heals him on every hit, so a diving Wukong wears out first.

passive.description:
After using a skill, Wukong enhances his next Basic Attack, where he charges at the target to deal 648 (475 + 100% physical attack) physical damage. This damage is always a critical hit.
He has a base Critical Rate of 20%, but his base Critical Damage is only 150%.
passive.name: The Great Sage

skill1.description:
Wukong chants a protective spell that lets him resist the next enemy skill used on him. The spell lasts up to 1.5s. If a skill is successfully resisted, he becomes invincible for 0.2s and gains a shield that negates 859 (600 + 150% physical attack + 15% extra Health) damage for 4s.
He gains 40% Movement Speed for 1s when using this skill.
skill1.name: Protective Shroud

skill2.description:
Wukong dashes in the target direction. If he dashes into an enemy, he leaps into the air and gains 90% Movement Speed that diminishes over 1s. Using a Basic Attack or skill will interrupt this leap.
Monster Slayer: Dashing into monsters will deal 274 (240 + 20% physical attack) true damage to them. If the monster has less than 15% Health, it will take grievous damage. This does not affect Overlords or Tyrants.
skill2.name: Furious Advance

skill3.description:
Wukong rams his staff into the earth, dealing 250 (250 + 80% extra physical attack) physical damage to enemies within range and launching them for 1s.
He also places 3 marks on enemies within range. When his Basic Attacks hit a marked enemy, the target loses a mark and takes an extra 270 physical damage.
skill3.name: Golden Cudgel

strategy.earlyGame: Early on, Wukong spends most of his time clearing the jungle to build levels and items. Furious Advance deals true damage to monsters it touches, so dashing into a camp combines moving and attacking in one cast. His base Critical Damage is modest, and while his items are thin even the enhanced Basic Attacks do not reach their full weight. When he runs into the enemy jungler, whether Protective Shroud is ready decides whether to fight or back off.
strategy.midGame: With Eternity Blade and Shadow Ripper done, the crits on his enhanced Basic Attacks get heavier. Eternity Blade raises Critical Damage the higher his Critical Rate climbs, which pairs well with attacks that always crit. Gank by closing in with Furious Advance, then go from the enhanced Basic Attack into Golden Cudgel's launch. While Golden Cudgel's marks remain, every Basic Attack that lands deals extra damage. Don't spend Protective Shroud on movement; casting it as the opponent goes for their answer skill makes the brawl easier to win. Rapacious Bite stacks Physical Attack and Cooldown Reduction for every monster killed, so keep clearing camps between ganks.
strategy.teamfight: Wukong goes in once your front line has started the fight and the enemy back line is less protected. Dive with Furious Advance, then after the enhanced Basic Attack launch the enemies around the target with Golden Cudgel, and keep spending marks with Basic Attacks. If Protective Shroud is still up, it can resist one enemy answer skill, which tells you whether to go for a second target.

combos.title: Weave Skills Into Enhanced Attacks
combos.sequence: Skill 2 (Furious Advance: dash and speed up) → Basic Attack (enhanced) → Skill 3 (Golden Cudgel: launch and marks) → Basic Attack (enhanced, spends a mark) → Skill 1 (Protective Shroud) → Basic Attack (enhanced)
combos.description: Each skill enhances his next Basic Attack, so alternating skills and Basic Attacks fits in more of those always-critical hits. Each Basic Attack on a target marked by Golden Cudgel spends a mark for extra damage. The aim is to land as many enhanced attacks as possible while the target is in the air.

combos.title: Resist, Then Answer
combos.sequence: Skill 1 (Protective Shroud: resist one enemy skill) → Skill 2 (Furious Advance: close in) → Basic Attack (enhanced) → Skill 3 (Golden Cudgel: launch)
combos.description: Protective Shroud only lasts a moment after the chant starts, so cast it before the enemy skill is on its way. A successful resist grants brief invincibility and a shield, and he can close in with Furious Advance while carrying that shield. If nothing was resisted, wait for Protective Shroud to come back before the next engage.

strengths: Enhanced Basic Attacks after a skill always crit
Protective Shroud resists one enemy skill and grants invincibility and a shield
Golden Cudgel launches nearby enemies and marks them for extra Basic Attack damage
Protective Shroud and Furious Advance both boost his speed, for engaging or leaving
weaknesses: His base Critical Damage is modest, so his damage stays low until items come in
The Protective Shroud window is short, and a misread wastes it
Golden Cudgel's launch is his only way to stop an enemy
Using a Basic Attack or skill cuts Furious Advance's leap short

playstyle.style: Wukong's damage in the jungle comes from weaving skills and Basic Attacks together. Each skill enhances his next Basic Attack, a leap at the target that always lands as a critical hit. Resist one enemy skill with Protective Shroud and he gains brief invincibility and a shield, carrying him straight into the brawl.
playstyle.suited: Protective Shroud has to be up before the enemy skill arrives, so you need to read what the opponent will use and when. A correct read starts his counterattack; a wrong one leaves him one defensive tool short until the cooldown is back. His starting Critical Damage is modest, so another deciding factor is whether you can wait until items like Eternity Blade raise his crits.

synergy.reason: Huang Zhong cannot move in Turret Mode, and Lapulapu's fissures stall enemies closing in on the turret.
Diaochan needs enemies to stay in range to stack her floral marks, and Lapulapu's fissures slow them there.

counters.reason: Marco Polo blinks away on a short cooldown, slipping out of Raging Sea's line before the wind-up ends.
Lu Bu gains Physical Pierce with his halberd unenchanted, walking straight past Lapulapu's passive defense.

passive.description: Lapulapu gains 100 Physical and Magical Defense. When there are teammates within a range of 800, the teammate with the lowest Health also gains this bonus. When there are no teammates within range, Lapulapu gains an extra 50% Physical and Magical Defense.
passive.name: Sea Beast's Favor

skill1.description:
Tap: Lapulapu slashes with his blade, dealing 462 (300 + 100% physical attack) physical damage to enemies and slowing them by 30% for 1s. This skill's cooldown is then reduced by 50%. He recovers 100 (100 + 2% extra Health) Health for each enemy hit by the slash. Effect is halved against non-hero units.
Tap and hold: Lapulapu throws his weapon in the target direction, dealing 462 (300 + 100% physical attack) physical damage to enemies hit and slowing them by 15% for 1s. After his weapon drops to the ground, it continuously deals 69 (50 + 12% physical attack) physical damage. When Lapulapu retrieves his weapon, he slashes nearby enemies and knocks them back.
When this skill hits an enemy, it reduces their physical defense by 50 for 2s.
skill1.name: Torrential Blade

skill2.description: Lapulapu charges in the target direction, dealing 529 (400 + 80% physical attack) physical damage to enemies along the path and launching them for 0.75s. After they land, enemies are slowed immensely for 1s.
skill2.name: Island's Blessing

skill3.description:
Lapulapu briefly charges up, then cleaves the ground, dealing 650 (650 + 180% extra physical attack) physical damage to enemies within range, launching them for 1s, and interrupting their skill use.
The ground remains fractured for 5s, and enemies caught in the fissures take 80 (80 + 25% extra physical attack) physical damage per 0.5s, and are slowed by 30%.
skill3.name: Raging Sea

strategy.earlyGame: Lapulapu's first spot is beside his farm-lane marksman. His passive also raises the defense of the nearby teammate with the lowest Health, so simply standing next to a teammate does more than standing alone in a bush. Once he has Island's Blessing, start short trades the moment the opponent steps forward. Torrential Blade's tap cycles fast and heals on hit, so use it freely once a brawl starts.
strategy.midGame: Once he learns Raging Sea, he can interrupt enemy skill use. A charged cleave can stop a big ability mid-cast. Between roams, he can also drop his weapon ahead with Torrential Blade's hold to lower physical defense before his team engages. He is the one taking hits at the front of the group, so step forward in earnest once his defensive items are in place. The September 10 update lowered Torrential Blade's damage.
strategy.teamfight: Island's Blessing signals the start of the fight, chaining into Raging Sea and dragging the brawl onto the fissures. Keep landing Torrential Blade's tap during the brawl, and its healing and cooldown reduction keep him standing. Launch overextended mages or marksmen rather than enemy tanks. Timing Raging Sea to stop an enemy winding up a big skill is also an important part of his job.

combos.title: Double Launch to Hold Them
combos.sequence: Skill 2 (Island's Blessing: charge and launch) → Skill 3 (Raging Sea: charge and cleave, launch and fissures) → Skill 1 (Torrential Blade: tap to slash and heal)
combos.description: Spend the time enemies are airborne from the charge on Raging Sea's wind-up. Launch them again as they land, leaving fissures under their feet for a while. The closing Torrential Blade heals him for each enemy slashed, so he can stay and drag them into a brawl.

combos.title: Throw the Weapon to Shred Defense
combos.sequence: Skill 1 (Torrential Blade: hold to throw the weapon and lower physical defense) → retrieve the weapon (slash nearby enemies and knock them back) → Skill 2 (Island's Blessing: charge and launch)
combos.description: The thrown weapon keeps dealing damage where it lands and lowers the physical defense of enemies it hits for a while. Retrieving it slashes and knocks back nearby enemies, so going to pick it up doubles as peeling. The defense reduction is short, so make sure Island's Blessing's follow-up lands within it.

strengths: His passive raises the defenses of himself and a low-Health teammate at the same time
Raging Sea interrupts enemy skill use, stopping big abilities
Torrential Blade's tap heals on hit and halves its own cooldown, helping him last through long brawls
Chaining Island's Blessing into Raging Sea's double launch holds enemies for a long time
weaknesses: His own damage is low, so the time he holds enemies goes to waste without his team's follow-up
Raging Sea needs a charge and is easy to miss against fast enemies
Island's Blessing is his only dash, leaving no way out after he uses it
He has few ways to reach enemies who chip him from range

playstyle.style: Lapulapu is a support who stands at the front while raising the physical and magical defense of himself and the nearby teammate with the lowest Health. Island's Blessing's charge and Raging Sea's cleave launch enemies in succession, and Raging Sea also interrupts enemy skill use. Torrential Blade slashes enemies and heals him on a tap, or throws his weapon when held.
playstyle.suited: He suits players who value the quiet work of helping just by standing next to teammates. Raging Sea charges up before cleaving, so he needs to read the moment to stop an enemy's big skill as it goes off.

synergy.reason: Cai Yan keeps healing while Earworm stuns the enemies closing in, so Hou Yi can hold position and keep firing.
Zhang Fei's shield and knockback break up dives, so Hou Yi never has to stop attacking.

counters.reason: Cirrus ignores terrain when he dives in, and Hou Yi has no dash to break away.
Mulan is immune to crowd control during her heavy-sword skills, so Hou Yi's stun cannot stop her.

passive.description:
Hou Yi gains 1 stack of Chastising Shot every time he hits an enemy with his Basic Attack, for up to 3 stacks. Each stack increases his Attack Speed by 2–4% for 3s.
At max stacks, he becomes enhanced for 3s. While enhanced, his Basic Attacks shoot 3 arrows (counts as 1 Basic Attack), dealing a total of 120% of a normal Basic Attack's physical damage.
passive.name: Chastising Shot

skill1.description: Hou Yi enhances his Basic Attacks to deal 257 (125 + 80% physical attack) physical damage. While the Passive's enhancement is in effect, using Skill 1 will cause the 3 arrows to deal a total of 120% of a normal Basic Attack's physical damage plus 50% damage to 2 more enemies or structures in front of him within range (without on-hit effects). This effect lasts 4s.
skill1.name: Arrow Volley

skill2.description:
Hou Yi orders the Sun Tower to attack the target area, gaining vision of the area.
After a short delay, he deals 480 (480 + 110% extra physical attack) magical damage to enemies within range and reduces their Movement Speed by 25–50% for 2s. Damage and slow effects are halved against enemies on the edge of the skill's range.
skill2.name: Afterglow

skill3.description:
Hou Yi shoots a flaming arrow in the target direction, which explodes upon hitting an enemy hero. The explosion deals 800 (800 + 120% extra physical attack) physical damage to enemies within range.
The arrow stuns the first enemy hero hit for 0.75–3.5s (depending on how far it has flown), while slowing enemies in the explosion's range by 30% for 1s.
skill3.name: Burning Sun Arrow

strategy.earlyGame: The moment three basic attacks put Hou Yi into the enhanced state is the moment to trade. While it lasts each attack fires three arrows, so the laning rhythm is to step up and shoot during the enhancement and back off once it ends. Afterglow lands after a delay, so aim it for when your opponent stops to last-hit.
strategy.midGame: Once he learns his ultimate, Burning Sun Arrow, Hou Yi has a way to stop enemies at a distance. The stun lasts longer the further the arrow has flown, so distant targets stay stopped for longer. If it misses, Afterglow's slow is the only thing left to stop someone coming at him, so pick the moment to fire it. Arrow Volley used during the enhanced state spreads damage to other enemies or a tower in front of him. Keep the stacks up and cycle Arrow Volley when you are taking a tower to speed up the damage. Afterglow also reveals the area it targets, which makes it a way to check bushes for hidden enemies before Tyrant or Overlord. Stand behind your frontline.
strategy.teamfight: Hou Yi keeps landing basic attacks from the very back. If Burning Sun Arrow connects before the fight starts, your team gets the first shot at the stunned target.
