Once it turns into a brawl, keep attacking whoever is in range so the enhanced state never drops. Against divers, fire Afterglow into their path before they arrive to make up for its delay. When the slow lands, back off to reset the distance, and keep Flash for the moment you cannot escape otherwise.

combos.title: Stun, Then Into the Enhanced State
combos.sequence: Skill 3 (Burning Sun Arrow: longer stun the further it flies) → Skill 2 (Afterglow: at the stunned target's feet) → Basic Attack (three hits to enter the enhanced state)
combos.description: Afterglow lands after a delay, so a target that can move can step out before it hits. Fire it under someone Burning Sun Arrow has stunned and it becomes easier to keep them inside until it lands. Stack basic attacks in the meantime and the attacks that follow come out as three arrows each.

combos.title: Arrow Volley While Enhanced
combos.sequence: Basic Attack (three hits to enter the enhanced state) → Skill 1 (Arrow Volley: also reaches enemies or structures in front) → Basic Attack
combos.description: Cast during the enhanced state, Arrow Volley adds damage to other enemies or structures in front of him on top of the three arrows. Build the stacks first so the Arrow Volley bonus overlaps with the enhancement. The order is the same whether you are taking a tower or fighting a crowd.

strengths: In the enhanced state, each basic attack fires three arrows
Burning Sun Arrow stuns longer the further it has flown
Afterglow gives vision of a distant area without walking in
Arrow Volley in the enhanced state also damages other enemies or structures in front of him
weaknesses: No mobility skill, so once caught he struggles to get away
His damage comes from basic attacks and drops off when he cannot keep attacking
Afterglow lands after a delay, so moving targets are hard to hit
If Burning Sun Arrow misses, Afterglow's slow is all he has left to stop a diver

playstyle.style: Hou Yi is a marksman whose output grows the longer he keeps landing basic attacks. Three hits put him in an enhanced state where, for a short time, each attack fires three arrows. He has no mobility skill; instead he protects himself with the long flight of Burning Sun Arrow and the vision Afterglow gives over a distant area.
playstyle.suited: With no mobility skill, matches turn on where you stand more than on mechanics. If you can keep firing from the edge of your range while tracking the enemy jungler, his basic attack damage comes through in full. If your habit is to look for an exit only after someone reaches you, he will leave you in a lot of bad spots.

synergy.reason: Guiguzi's pull and stun hold enemies in place, so every shotgun shell lands and stacks Liu Bei's pierce.
Donghuang's suppression pins a hero in place, so Liu Bei keeps firing and feeds the damage back into his shield.

counters.reason: Lady Zhen's icicles wall heroes off and launch them, stopping Liu Bei before he can close.
Mai Shiranui's ultimate knocks Liu Bei back and strips the very physical attack Hearts and Minds just gave him.

passive.description:
Liu Bei's shotgun holds 4 shells. The two middle shells deal 87 (50% physical attack) physical damage to the enemy, while the other two shells on either side deal 52 (30% physical attack) physical damage. Every hit on an enemy hero grants him 1 stack of Combat Instinct, giving 5–10 Physical Pierce for 6s. Combat Instinct stacks up to 12 times.
Only the 2 middle shells from each shot can crit and trigger equipment effects. Structures are not affected by extra shells.
passive.name: Reinforced Shells

skill1.description: Liu Bei increases his Movement Speed by 40% for 1.5s. The next Basic Attack is a double shot, with each shell dealing 148 (110 + 22% physical attack) physical damage.
skill1.name: Dual Shot

skill2.description:
Liu Bei smashes into the enemy, knocking them back and dealing 300 (300 + 100% extra physical attack) physical damage before stopping.
Hitting an enemy hero reduces this skill's cooldown by 2s.
skill2.name: Leading the Charge

skill3.description:
Liu Bei cleanses himself of all crowd control effects and gains crowd control immunity for 3s.
He also gains 100 physical attack and a shield that negates 1,000 (1,000 + 15% extra Health) damage for 6s.
While the shield is active, 60% of the damage he deals to enemy heroes and 20% of the damage he deals to minions and monsters is added to the shield.
Shield points are capped at 150% of the initial value.
skill3.name: Hearts and Minds

strategy.earlyGame: Liu Bei clears the jungle while staying close to monsters so his shells land. When ganking, enter with Leading the Charge's dash from the side of the enemy's escape route and knock them back toward his team. Combat Instinct only stacks when shells hit enemy heroes, so in fights, getting close and emptying his shotgun makes the most of the Physical Pierce.
strategy.midGame: From the mid game on, he enters skirmishes with Hearts and Minds ready. Pressing it the moment enemy crowd control comes his way cleanses it and lets him carry a shield into the brawl. In fights over Tyrant or Overlord, keep in mind that Combat Instinct does not build up. What helps against the boss is the shield, and part of the damage he deals to monsters is added to it too. When he spots an isolated enemy, walk in to close the distance while keeping Leading the Charge for the chase.
strategy.teamfight: Liu Bei engages a little after the opening. After seeing the enemy spend skills and crowd control on his front line, close on a squishy target with Leading the Charge and finish them with Dual Shot's double shot and his shells. If enemies fire crowd control to stop him, cleanse it with Hearts and Minds and keep attacking. Once the effect ends he cannot block crowd control, so it also matters not to get greedy chasing after a kill.

combos.title: Push Them Out, Then Fire
combos.sequence: Skill 2 (Leading the Charge: dash and knock back) → Basic Attack (four shells) → Skill 1 (Dual Shot: speed up, next Basic Attack is a double shot) → Basic Attack
combos.description: The dash knocks the enemy back, and Liu Bei himself stops in place. Walk back in toward where he pushed them and fire his shells, all as one sequence. Hitting an enemy hero with the dash shortens Leading the Charge's cooldown, so it comes back sooner for the next chase.

combos.title: Push Through Crowd Control and Hit Back
combos.sequence: (The moment enemy crowd control lands) Skill 3 (Hearts and Minds: cleanse and immunity, shield) → Skill 2 (Leading the Charge: dash) → Basic Attack → Skill 1 (Dual Shot: double shot)
combos.description: Hearts and Minds removes the crowd control on him and blocks new crowd control for a short time. He gains physical attack and a shield at the same time, so spend that window counterattacking. While the shield lasts, part of the damage he deals to enemy heroes is added to it, building it past its initial value.

strengths: Landing several shells at close range deals high burst damage
Hearts and Minds cleanses crowd control and briefly grants immunity, letting him attack through enemy disruption
During Hearts and Minds, damage he deals is added to his shield, so he gets tougher the more he attacks
Every shell that hits an enemy hero raises his Physical Pierce, keeping his damage up against tough targets
weaknesses: At range the outer shells struggle to land, and his damage drops
Leading the Charge is his only movement skill, and missing it makes both chasing and escaping difficult
He is weak to crowd control right after Hearts and Minds ends
Only the two middle shells crit and trigger equipment effects, so his items work in an unusual way

playstyle.style: Liu Bei is a jungle fighter who advances while firing four shells from his shotgun. Each shell that hits an enemy hero adds a stack of Combat Instinct, raising his Physical Pierce. His ultimate, Hearts and Minds, cleanses crowd control and grants immunity to it for a short time, along with a shield and physical attack, and part of the damage he deals is added to the shield.
playstyle.suited: He suits players who enjoy closing the distance in trades on their own terms. Only the two middle shells can crit and trigger equipment effects, so he needs to position to land them head-on. His only movement skill is Leading the Charge's dash, so decide whether to chase or retreat before using it.

synergy.reason: Garo has no escape skill, so Zhang Fei can stand in front of her and knock divers away.
Lady Sun rolls right up to enemies, so Zhang Fei can leap to that same spot and shield her.

counters.reason: Diaochan cuts her blink's cooldown on every hit, so she slips out of Zhang Fei's knockback and gust alike.
Lu Bu is immune to crowd control during his dive, so Zhang Fei's knockback cannot protect the ally he is covering.

passive.name: Dark Potential
passive.description: Before transforming, Zhang Fei's Basic Attacks increase Madness by 3. After transforming, using skills will shake the ground and slow nearby enemies by 25% for 2s.

skill1.name: Forbidden Domain / Mad Slaughter

forms.description:
Zhang Fei swings his snake spear, dealing 600 (600 + 150% extra physical attack) physical damage to enemies within range and knocking back enemy heroes.
Hitting an enemy unit increases Madness by 3.
Zhang Fei smashes the ground, dealing 741 (600 + 150% extra physical attack + 4% Health) physical damage to enemies within range. Enemies in the center are launched for 0.5s.

skill1.description:
Zhang Fei swings his snake spear, dealing 600 (600 + 150% extra physical attack) physical damage to enemies within range and knocking back enemy heroes.
Hitting an enemy unit increases Madness by 3.

skill2.name: Leaping Savior / Stampede

forms.description:
Zhang Fei leaps to the target location and activates a mark, granting a shield that negates 650 (650 + 13% extra Health) damage to teammates within range.
He gains 3 Madness from using the skill and 1 extra Madness for each shield granted to teammates.
Zhang Fei leaps to the target location, trampling enemies within range and dealing 621 (480 + 120% extra physical attack + 4% Health) physical damage. Enemies in the center are launched for 0.5s.

skill2.description:
Zhang Fei leaps to the target location and activates a mark, granting a shield that negates 650 (650 + 13% extra Health) damage to teammates within range.
He gains 3 Madness from using the skill and 1 extra Madness for each shield granted to teammates.

skill3.name: Unbridled Outburst
skill3.description:
Zhang Fei roars in the target direction for 1.25s, generating a powerful gust of wind and gaining a shield that negates damage equal to 40% of his Health for 15s. While roaring, he gains crowd control immunity and invincibility. The wind knocks enemies back and deals 600 (600 + 150% extra physical attack) physical damage, and enemies at the end of its path are stunned for 1.5s. His Movement Speed increases by 50% while he is in the wind.
Ferali Form: While he is in Ferali Form, his Basic Attacks deal an extra 220 (220 + 100% extra physical attack) damage. When Ferali Form ends, Forbidden Domain is automatically triggered.

strategy.earlyGame: Zhang Fei's early game begins with auto-attacking next to his marksman. Basic attacks in normal form build Madness, and how fast he can transform is directly his strength. Leaping Savior shields everyone where he lands and gains Madness per teammate shielded. Layer it just as allies are about to take hits. In trades, cut off the enemy's follow-up with Forbidden Domain's sweep. Building full Madness before Tyrant lets him transform in the first skirmish.
strategy.midGame: How much he contributes depends on keeping Unbridled Outburst ready. He is invincible and immune to crowd control during the roar, so it suits countering the enemy's engage head-on. Before Tyrant or Overlord, keep the transformation ready and answer the moment the enemy moves. Choose the direction carefully; ideally, blow the enemy's key player toward your team. Forbidden Domain triggers automatically when Ferali Form ends, so he can count on that final push too.
strategy.teamfight: Zhang Fei's job follows a clear order. Shield teammates with Leaping Savior before the fight, answer the enemy's dive with the roar, and split their formation with the wind. Only then does he start hitting. The invincible window exists to make enemy ultimates miss, so spending it before he has been hit by anything wastes it. Blowing them away after seeing the enemy's ultimate animation can swing the whole fight at once. While transformed, every skill also slows nearby enemies, so he can handle chasing down a scattered enemy team himself.

combos.title: Take the Dive, Then Roar Back
combos.sequence: wait for the enemy to dive → Skill 3 (Unbridled Outburst: invincible roar, shield, stun at the far end) → chase inside the wind (faster movement)
combos.description: Crowd control does not land during the roar and he is invincible, so don't use it first; wait for the enemy to dive in, then answer. The wind blows enemies away, and only those touching its far end are stunned. Hit it from half a step back rather than point-blank.

combos.title: Hand Out Shields and Peel
combos.sequence: Skill 2 (Leaping Savior: leap in normal form and shield allies) → Skill 1 (Forbidden Domain: sweep in normal form to knock back) → Basic Attack
combos.description: Leap in the moment an ally is targeted, shielding teammates within range as he lands. The sweep from Forbidden Domain does the peeling, knocking back enemy heroes it hits. Shielding teammates and landing the sweep also build Madness, so he gets closer to transforming while protecting.

strengths: During Unbridled Outburst's roar he is immune to crowd control and invincible, and gains a large shield
Leaping Savior hands shields to every teammate where he lands
The wind blows enemies away and stuns those at the far end, breaking formations
In Ferali Form his basic attacks deal extra damage and each skill slows nearby enemies
weaknesses: Until Madness builds up, his damage is low and his only crowd control is knockback
Blowing enemies in the wrong direction lets them escape
He relies on Leaping Savior's leap for mobility and has few ways to protect himself
No long-range tools, so he can do little in poke-heavy fights

playstyle.style: Zhang Fei is a support who hands out shields and builds Madness in his normal form, then transforms with his ultimate, Unbridled Outburst, to blow enemies away. While roaring during the transformation he is immune to crowd control and invincible, and he gains a large shield based on his max Health. In Ferali Form, Forbidden Domain / Mad Slaughter and Leaping Savior / Stampede become attacks that launch enemies, and every skill slows enemies around him.
playstyle.suited: He suits players who want to play both a protector and a brawler in the same match. Early on he hands out shields while building Madness; after transforming he blows the enemy away as a group. Sending the roar's wind in the wrong direction lets enemies escape, so choosing where to blow them is the key decision.

synergy.reason: Zhang Fei shields her and knocks divers away, so Chicha's Basic Attacks never have to stop.
Guiguzi pulls enemies into one spot, so Chicha's Overkill Form arrows lock onto the whole group.

counters.reason: Dun chains a slow into a launch, stalling Chicha's attacks until her Fighting Spirit falls off.
Lam dashes right back in after every knockback, healing himself as he closes the gap again.

passive.name: Forge Inheritor
passive.description:
Chicha cycles through her five ancestral weapons (polearm, spear, dagger-axe, halberd, and bow). Each Basic Attack restores 20 (20 + 0.3% extra Health) Health and switches to the next weapon with increased range. Each Basic Attack or skill hit grants 1 stack of Fighting Spirit (lasts 4s, up to 8 stacks), with each stack granting 4% Attack Speed (can exceed the Attack Speed cap).
Holding a polearm or spear puts her in Defense Form, dagger-axe or halberd puts her in Offense Form, and bow puts her in Overkill Form.
Each form grants different Skill 1 and Skill 2 effects. Entering Overkill Form instantly reduces the Cooldown of Skill 1 and Skill 2 by 50%.

skill1.name: Peak-Crushing Polearm / Hell-Binding Dagger-Axe / Sky-Shattering Bow

forms.description: Chicha swings her weapon and leaps forward in the target direction, dealing 225 (225 + 70% extra physical attack) physical damage to enemies in the path and carrying them to the landing point. After landing, thrusts forward, dealing 225 (225 + 70% extra physical attack) physical damage and launching enemies for 0.75s.

Chicha hurls her weapon toward the target direction and propels forward, dealing 250 (250 + 80% extra physical attack) physical damage to enemies in her path and pushing them to the skill's endpoint. After landing, she smashes the ground, dealing 250 (250 + 80% extra physical attack) physical damage and launching enemies for 0.75s.

Chicha launches a flying kick in the target direction, firing a piercing arrow that deals 275 (275 + 90% extra physical attack) physical damage and knocking back enemies for 0.75s. If enemies hit a wall, they are restricted to a fixed area for 2s and take 275 (275 + 90% extra physical attack) physical damage.

skill1.skill_name: Peak-Crushing Polearm / Hell-Binding Dagger-Axe / Sky-Shattering Bow
skill1.description: Defense Form: Chicha swings her weapon and leaps forward in the target direction, dealing 225 (225 + 70% extra physical attack) physical damage to enemies in the path and carrying them to the landing point. After landing, thrusts forward, dealing 225 (225 + 70% extra physical attack) physical damage and launching enemies for 0.75s.

skill2.name: World-Splitting Spear / Realm-Sweeping Halberd / Star-Felling Arrow

forms.description: Chicha thrusts forward in the target direction, dealing 450 (450 + 150% extra physical attack) physical damage and knocking back enemies (without applying crowd control). For each target hit, she recovers 180 (180 + 3% extra Health) Health (halved for non-hero units).

Chicha sweeps in the target direction, dealing 475 (475 + 160% extra physical attack) physical damage and knocking back enemies (without applying crowd control). For each target hit, she recovers 180 (180 + 3% extra Health) Health (halved for non-hero units).

Chicha aims in the target direction, locking onto all enemies in range (up to five, prioritizing heroes). After aiming, she shoots arrows at all locked-on targets, dealing 500 (500 + 170% extra physical attack) physical damage, plus true damage equal to 10% of the Health the target has lost, and knocking back enemies (without crowd control). For each target hit, she recovers 180 (180 + 3% extra Health) Health (halved for non-hero units).
While using this skill, Chicha gains crowd control immunity and 15% damage reduction.

skill2.skill_name: World-Splitting Spear / Realm-Sweeping Halberd / Star-Felling Arrow
skill2.description: Defense Form: Chicha thrusts forward in the target direction, dealing 450 (450 + 150% extra physical attack) physical damage and knocking back enemies (without applying crowd control). For each target hit, she recovers 180 (180 + 3% extra Health) Health (halved for non-hero units).

skill3.name: Return of the Armsmaster
skill3.description:
Chicha unleashes all five weapons, gaining a Movement Speed boost for 2s and 35% Attack Speed, and breaking the Fighting Spirit stack limit for 6s.
During this time, she commands all five weapons to attack, with each Basic Attack dealing an extra 40 (40 + 13% extra physical attack) physical damage.
While using this skill, she can use her Basic Attack while moving. Overkill Form will remain active once entered.

strategy.earlyGame: Landing Basic Attacks is how Chicha both heals and moves on to her next weapon. Fighting Spirit fades once her attacks stop, so once you commit to a trade, keep swinging to hold the Attack Speed. Defense Form's polearm and spear are short-ranged and struggle to reach distant targets. Starting trades when the bow is close is the low-risk way to lane.
strategy.midGame: Once she learns Return of the Armsmaster, she gets a window where she can attack while moving. Right after the cast her Movement Speed and Attack Speed jump and the Fighting Spirit limit is lifted for a while, so her damage keeps flowing whether she is chasing or backing off. Enter Overkill Form during the skill and it stays active. Her Skill 2 forms heal her for every target hit, but minions and monsters only give half. When she needs a lot of Health back, hitting enemy heroes heals her more. Where walls are close, pushing enemies toward them while in Overkill Form makes Sky-Shattering Bow's trap easier to set up.
strategy.teamfight: The key is picking the moment for Overkill Form's Star-Felling Arrow. It locks onto enemies in range with heroes first and adds true damage based on missing Health, so it hits harder after your team has worn them down. She gains crowd control immunity and damage reduction while firing. If the fight starts before she reaches the bow, use Return of the Armsmaster to keep attacking on the move and advance her weapon to Overkill Form. Every Basic Attack restores Health, so not letting up inside the enemy team is what keeps her standing.

combos.title: Use Offense Skills, Then Reach the Bow
combos.sequence: Skill 1 (Hell-Binding Dagger-Axe: launch) → Skill 2 (Realm-Sweeping Halberd: sweep and heal) → Basic Attack (advance to the bow for Overkill Form) → Skill 1 (Sky-Shattering Bow)
combos.description: Spending both skills while holding the dagger-axe and halberd means they come back sooner once the bow arrives. Landing the halberd sweep while the target is still in the air from the dagger-axe also wins back some Health.

combos.title: Trap Them Against the Wall
combos.sequence: Skill 3 (Return of the Armsmaster: attack while moving) → Basic Attack (advance to the bow for Overkill Form) → Skill 1 (Sky-Shattering Bow: knock into a wall to trap) → Skill 2 (Star-Felling Arrow: lock on and fire)
combos.description: A target knocked into a wall by Sky-Shattering Bow gets trapped and takes extra damage. Wear them down during the trap before firing Star-Felling Arrow, and its true damage hits harder. Return of the Armsmaster goes first because Overkill Form stays active once she enters it during the skill.

strengths: Every Basic Attack restores Health, so long brawls suit her
Stacked Fighting Spirit pushes her Attack Speed past the normal cap
During Return of the Armsmaster she attacks on the move and keeps Overkill Form once entered
Enemies knocked into a wall by Sky-Shattering Bow are trapped in place for a while
weaknesses: Weapons advance in a set order, so she cannot pick the form she wants on demand
Once her attacks stop, Fighting Spirit fades and the bonus Attack Speed goes with it
The polearm and spear of Defense Form are short-ranged and struggle to reach distant targets
Skill 1 is her only way to stop an enemy in place

playstyle.style: Chicha swaps weapons with every Basic Attack, and the weapon in hand changes what her skills do. The polearm and spear put her in Defense Form, the dagger-axe and halberd in Offense Form, and the bow in Overkill Form. Entering Overkill Form cuts the cooldowns of Skill 1 and Skill 2 on the spot, so the time she holds the bow is her best window to attack.
playstyle.suited: Her weapons only advance in a fixed order, so you fight while reading what she will be holding a few attacks from now. If counting weapons in the middle of a brawl sounds fun, one set of skill buttons gives you three ways to play. Fighting Spirit fades once her attacks stop, so players who like to hold back and wait for an opening will find her a poor fit.

synergy.reason: Liu Shan's stun pins enemies in place, letting Fang land Bladestorm's double-damage center right on them.
Zhang Fei's shield lets Fang hold his ground under fire and finish stacking Dark Marks.

counters.reason: Dun chains a launch into a stun, leaving Fang no window to shoot back.
Di Renjie's Legal Immunity gives him a brief window where nothing lands, so Fang's burst whiffs on him.

passive.description:
Fang's big ears allow him to sense nearby movement and pick up the trail of enemy heroes, gaining their vision for 1s. This skill works on the same hero once every 6s.
He can also identify monster weak spots, letting him deal 7.5-15% extra physical damage to monsters.
passive.name: Going Undercover

skill1.description:
Fang marks an enemy with a Dark Mark that explodes after 4s, dealing 230 (230 + 75% extra physical attack) physical damage to enemies within range. His Basic Attacks place 1 stack of Dark Mark, for up to 4 stacks, with each stack dealing an extra 230 (230 + 75% extra physical attack) physical damage. The Dark Marks detonate immediately upon reaching 4 stacks.
He also gains 35% Attack Speed and 75 Attack Range for 4s when using this skill.
skill1.name: Target Sighted

skill2.description: Fang launches his blade in the target direction and catches it on the other end with uncanny speed. He is untargetable while using this skill. The blade deals 260 (260 + 80% extra physical attack) physical damage to enemies in its path and slows them by 15% for 2s. He also leaves a burning trail behind him for 2.9s, which deals 110 (110 + 30% extra physical attack) physical damage every 0.25s to enemies treading on it and slows them by 15%.
skill2.name: Wheel Away

skill3.description:
Fang throws his blade to the target location, dealing 320 (320 + 100% extra physical attack) physical damage to enemies within range. After reaching its destination, it spins for 5.4s, dealing 140 (140 + 40% extra physical attack) physical damage to enemies within range every 0.5s while slowing them by 50%.
The blade deals double damage to enemies at the center and places Dark Marks on them.
skill3.name: Bladestorm

strategy.earlyGame: Fang's early trades depend on how many Basic Attacks you land after casting Target Sighted. Marks burst as soon as they reach max stacks, and the blast spreads, so it can catch other enemies standing nearby. Going Undercover briefly grants vision of enemy heroes nearby, which sometimes reveals someone waiting in a bush. Keep Wheel Away as your exit, and trade with Target Sighted and Basic Attacks alone.
strategy.midGame: When a teammate catches someone, drop Bladestorm on that enemy's escape route to slow them down. Enemies at the center take far more damage and pick up Dark Marks, so layering Target Sighted makes the escape much harder. Going Undercover also adds damage against monsters, which makes him useful when the team is taking Tyrant or Overlord. In sieges, mark detonations spread onto enemies clustered under their tower, so push forward together with your front line. Right after Wheel Away he has no escape left. Keep any time spent alone away from the team short.
strategy.teamfight: Bladestorm is the first thing to place. Drop it where the enemy backline will retreat or where your front line is pushing them, and they have to move around the center, which tends to break their formation. Then raise your attack speed with Target Sighted and start stacking marks with Basic Attacks on enemies caught in the storm. Detonations spread, so the tighter they clump, the more you hit at once. When an assassin dives, slip through with Wheel Away, leave the burning trail behind, and reset behind your front line.

combos.title: Max Stacks, Instant Blast
combos.sequence: Skill 1 (Target Sighted: more Attack Speed and Attack Range) → Basic Attack (stack marks; they burst at max)
combos.description: Target Sighted raises attack speed and range for a short while, so that is where the stacking starts. Reaching max stacks detonates the marks at once, and even short of that they explode after a moment, so there is no need to chase someone who is walking away. The extra range helps the last attack reach a target who is starting to back off.

combos.title: Killing Inside the Storm
combos.sequence: Skill 3 (Bladestorm: slows the area, more damage at the center) → Skill 1 (Target Sighted) → Basic Attack (stack marks)
combos.description: Bladestorm keeps spinning and slowing, which buys time to land Basic Attacks on a target who can barely move. Enemies at the center also receive Dark Marks, so with your attacks the stacks max out quickly. Place it on the escape route and make them walk over the middle.

combos.title: Untargetable Sidestep
combos.sequence: Skill 2 (Wheel Away: untargetable in transit, leaves a burning trail) → Skill 1 (Target Sighted) → Basic Attack
combos.description: Fang cannot be targeted while he follows the blade, so a diving assassin's skill can miss outright. The trail keeps burning for a while, damaging and slowing anyone who steps on it. It is his only escape, so turn it into offense only when you expect to finish the chase.

strengths: Mark detonations deal area damage, chipping clumped enemies and minions together
Wheel Away makes him untargetable in transit, so diving skills can miss
Bladestorm heavily slows enemies in its area and deals much more damage at the center
Going Undercover briefly reveals nearby enemy heroes, which helps spot ambushes
weaknesses: Wheel Away is his only movement skill; once it's used, he has no way out
Much of his damage comes from mark detonations, which take time to build
Enemies who stay out of Bladestorm's center take much less damage
Target Sighted's attack speed and range last only a few seconds, so the attacks have to land inside that window

playstyle.style: Fang is a marksman who stacks Dark Marks with his Basic Attacks and detonates them together. Marks go off on their own after a short time and burst immediately at max stacks, catching other enemies standing nearby. His one movement skill, Wheel Away, makes him untargetable in transit, so it serves both as an escape and as a way to reposition.
playstyle.suited: Fang wants you to cast Target Sighted and then count your Basic Attacks as the marks build. Wheel Away is his only movement skill, so every time you have to choose between spending it to attack and saving it to escape. He fits players who can make that call calmly in the middle of a trade.

synergy.reason: Lapulapu's launch and slowing fissures freeze enemies in place, so Consort Yu's charged bolt pierces the group.
Donghuang's suppression pins an enemy completely still, giving Consort Yu a free target for her charged bolt.

counters.reason: Erin's skill damage is magical, so it ignores Consort Yu's physical immunity, and Forest Whisper shrugs off the slows.
Diaochan blinks straight in, and her magical and true damage ignores Consort Yu's physical immunity entirely.

passive.description: Basic Attacks have a 25% chance of shooting an extra bolt, which deals 110 (90 + 12% physical attack) physical damage and places 1 stack of slow on the enemy, for up to 2 stacks. Each stack slows enemies by 10−20% for 2s.
passive.name: Blessing of the Dryads

skill1.description:
After charging up, Consort Yu shoots a powerful bolt in the target direction, dealing damage to enemies in its path. The bolt deals 740 (740 + 230% extra physical attack) physical damage to the first enemy it hits. Damage is reduced by 15% for every subsequent enemy hit, down to 40% of the initial damage.
When her Attack Speed is increased by 0%/40%/80%/120%/160%/200%, her charging is accelerated by 0%/20%/40%/60%/80%/100%.
skill1.name: Oak Bolt

skill2.description:
Consort Yu enhances herself for 2s. While enhanced, her Movement Speed is increased by 20%, Attack Speed is increased by 12.5%, and she becomes immune to physical attacks.
When using Skill 2, she briefly gains crowd control immunity, removing all slow effects from herself and enhancing her next Basic Attack within 5s to trigger the Blessing of the Dryads.
Passive: She increases her Attack Speed by 12.5%.
skill2.name: Protecting Winds

skill3.description:
Consort Yu gains crowd control immunity and jumps on the target enemy, stunning them for 0.5s and slowing them immensely for 2s.
She then flips backward to her original location while shooting 1 bolt at the same enemy. The bolt deals 340 (340 + 100% extra physical attack) physical damage. Upon landing, she gains 20% Attack Speed for 4s.
When her Attack Speed is increased by 0%/40%/80%/120%/160%/200%, she shoots 1/2/3/4/5/6 bolt(s). The second bolt that hits the same target deals 60% damage, while subsequent bolts deal 20% damage.
skill3.name: Vaulting Shot

strategy.earlyGame: How far forward she can stand in trades depends on whether Protecting Winds is ready. Oak Bolt deals its full damage to the first enemy it hits and less to each one after. An enemy standing in the way cuts what reaches your target, so look for an angle where they stand in front of the line before you fire. With low Attack Speed the charge is slow as well, so start it from a range their skills cannot reach.
strategy.midGame: Vaulting Shot leaps onto the target, stuns them, slows them heavily, and then flips her back to her original spot. That means she can catch an enemy who walked too far forward without ending up inside their team. Landing raises her Attack Speed, so charging Oak Bolt right away makes it easier to hit the target while the slow lasts. When pushing a tower or holding a standoff before an objective, keep Protecting Winds until the fight actually starts. It does nothing against magic damage, so stay out of reach of enemies who fight with magic.
strategy.teamfight: Consort Yu fights while holding Protecting Winds, watching for the moment the enemy's physical damage dealers commit. When one dives in, make their attacks whiff with Protecting Winds and shoot back, using the enhanced Basic Attack and the extra bolt to slow them down. Using Vaulting Shot after the enemy shows its plan, rather than at the very start of the brawl, makes it easier for your team to focus whoever she stops. Fire Oak Bolt down a line of enemies and it still reaches the ones at the back, even though the damage drops along the way.

combos.title: Make Them Whiff, Then Shoot Back
combos.sequence: Skill 2 (Protecting Winds: physical immunity, slows removed) → Basic Attack (enhanced, triggers Blessing of the Dryads) → Skill 1 (Oak Bolt)
combos.description: Protecting Winds answers an attack that is already coming, so it goes first. The enhanced Basic Attack fires an extra bolt that slows the target, so Oak Bolt becomes easier to land as they try to leave.

combos.title: Vault In, Shoot on the Way Out
combos.sequence: Skill 3 (Vaulting Shot: pounce and stun, then flip back) → Skill 1 (Oak Bolt) → Basic Attack
combos.description: Vaulting Shot stuns the target and then flips her back to where she started, leaving them heavily slowed at a distance. Start charging Oak Bolt while the landing Attack Speed bonus is active and it finishes quickly enough to hit the slowed target. The number of bolts grows with Attack Speed, but from the second bolt on, each one deals less to the same target.

strengths: During Protecting Winds she ignores physical attacks and clears any slows on her
More Attack Speed means faster Oak Bolt charges and more bolts from Vaulting Shot
Vaulting Shot returns her to where she started, so a catch does not leave her stuck among enemies
Basic Attacks sometimes fire an extra bolt that stacks a slow on the target
weaknesses: Protecting Winds only blocks physical attacks; magic damage still lands
With little Attack Speed, Oak Bolt takes a long time to charge
If Oak Bolt hits someone in front first, it deals less to the enemies behind
After Protecting Winds is used, she has nothing to block physical attacks until it returns

playstyle.style: Consort Yu's trades are built around the short window in which Protecting Winds makes her immune to physical attacks. Time it to the moment a physical attacker commits, and their hits whiff while her enhanced Basic Attack shoots back. More Attack Speed charges Oak Bolt faster and adds bolts to Vaulting Shot, so her output keeps climbing as her items come together.
playstyle.suited: Protecting Winds is pressed after the enemy starts attacking, not before. Use it early and it blocks nothing before going on cooldown, so if you like waiting for the opponent and answering second, one skill can flip a whole trade. Against drafts with a lot of magic damage, there is much less for Protecting Winds to block.

synergy.reason: Huang Zhong cannot move in Turret Mode, and Join Me drags enemies to Kui, who stands in front of the turret.
Lady Sun's Ultimate Shell needs a target that stays put, and Into the Void stuns marked enemies through the whole channel.

counters.reason: Fatih cleanses his own crowd control with Sacred Tree Blessing, so Kui's Into the Void stun falls off him.
Kaizer turns durable under Invincible Warrior, so Join Me just hauls that buffed form into Kui's own lap.

passive.description:
Kui detonates an explosion when taking damage that exceeds 10% of his current Health in a single hit, dealing 166 (60 +60% magical attack +3% Health) magical damage to nearby enemies. This effect has a 2s Cooldown.
3s after he's defeated, he explodes, dealing 664 (240 +240% magical attack +12% Health) magical damage to nearby enemies.
passive.name: Ethereal Outburst

skill1.description: Kui hammers the ground, dealing 320 (320 + 32% magical attack) magical damage to enemies within range and slowing them by 15% for 1.5s. Enemies next to him take 250% magical damage, are slowed by 15% for 1.5s, and are marked with Into the Void.
skill1.name: Mortals!

skill2.description:
Kui throws his chain hook in the target direction, marking the first enemy hit with Into the Void and pulling them to him, dealing 550 (550 + 60% magical attack) magical damage.
Passive: Defeats and assists grant 1 stack of Void Devour, increasing his Health by 180, for up to 20 stacks.
skill2.name: Join Me

skill3.description:
Kui opens up the portal to the void and devours enemies up to 16 times, dealing a total of 1,920 (1,920 + 288% magical attack) magical damage and continuously stunning targets marked by Into the Void.
He also gains a shield that negates 46 (46 + 1% extra Health) damage with each devour.
skill3.name: Into the Void

strategy.earlyGame: Early on, Kui spends more time waiting than throwing. The chain pulls the first enemy it touches, so any other enemy standing between you and your target gets pulled instead. Wait for a moment when nothing stands between you and your target, then throw. Until he has his ultimate, the only thing that keeps a pulled enemy in place is the slow from Mortals!, so throw only when your laner is close enough to hit the target straight away. Kills and assists keep adding to his max HP, so every early fight he joins turns into bulk later.
strategy.midGame: Once Into the Void is learned, one chain becomes the start of a kill. The pulled enemy already carries the mark, so opening the portal right after leaves them unable to move until it closes. That makes the choice of target matter. Pulling a tank gives your damage dealers little to work with; a fragile back-liner is far more likely to die. Standoffs before Tyrant or Overlord are the best time to land one from outside vision. A successful pull forces the enemy either to fight a player down or to abandon the teammate you dragged away. The reverse also holds: if Kui is spotted first, his lack of mobility makes him an easy target. Stand in a bush a little behind your front line, and after a miss stay back until the chain is ready again.
strategy.teamfight: The fight takes its shape from the chain thrown before it starts. Pull one back-liner out and you are fighting the other four. Once it turns into a brawl, his job is to mark enemies next to him with Mortals! and hold every marked target with Into the Void. Marking with Mortals! means getting right next to enemies, so stepping into the enemy team cannot be avoided. Whether he survives there depends on the max HP he has built up and the shields Into the Void stacks. Even after he falls, a large explosion goes off around him a moment later, so going down inside their formation is not wasted. If the chain misses and no fight opens, don't force your way in; fall back behind your team.

combos.title: Chain Them, Then Hold Them
combos.sequence: Skill 2 (Join Me: Into the Void mark and pull) → Skill 3 (Into the Void: keeps the marked target stunned) → Skill 1 (Mortals!)
combos.description: A target hit by the chain carries Into the Void, so opening Into the Void right after keeps them stunned. The chain is his only way to mark someone far away. Each devour also stacks a shield, so enemies rushing in to help will not drop him at once.

combos.title: The Answer After a Missed Chain
combos.sequence: Skill 1 (Mortals!: marks enemies right next to him) → Skill 3 (Into the Void)
combos.description: The mark does not have to come from the chain. Mortals! marks enemies standing right next to Kui and hits them harder too. Its cooldown is far shorter than the chain's, which makes it the fallback when someone walks up to him just after a miss.

strengths: A landed chain pulls one enemy in front of your team before the fight starts
An enemy marked with Into the Void stays stunned for the whole of Into the Void
Every kill and assist raises his max HP, so he gets sturdier as the game goes on
Big hits and even his own death still leave damage on the enemies around him
weaknesses: No mobility skill; once caught, he cannot get away on his own
After a missed chain he has no way to mark a distant enemy until the next one
Marking with Mortals! means standing right next to enemies
If the team cannot finish the pulled target, he is left fighting with an enemy right in front of him

playstyle.style: A support who hooks one enemy with Join Me and drags them to where his team can hit them. The pulled target is marked with Into the Void, and a marked enemy cannot move while his ultimate, also called Into the Void, is open, so a single landed chain is where a kill starts.
playstyle.suited: The chain has a long cooldown, and after a miss he has no way to pull anyone for a while. What decides whether Kui suits you is picking your own moments and not minding the wait. Players who like helping the team through sheer volume of actions will find that wait long.

synergy.reason: Bai Qi's Shadow Power amplifies healing, so Melody of Peace restores far more Health on him.
Sun Bin's Time Lapse field detonates on a delay, and Tragic Beauty's slow holds enemies inside it until then.

counters.reason: Han Xin has crowd control immunity during The Unrivaled Spear, so Yuhuan's stun cannot stop him.
Shouyue's Wild Wind carves out a share of max Health, so stacking Health does nothing to soften it.

passive.description:
Yuhuan changes the melody to produce different skill effects.
War: Skills deal 90 (90 + 15% magical attack) extra magical damage to enemy units within a range of 800.
Peace: Skills restore 35 (35 + 6% magical attack) Health to allies, while also restoring (+ 6% extra Health) Health to herself.
passive.name: Poignant Melodies

skill1.description:
Yuhuan releases up to 4 sound waves, dealing 275 (275 + 45% magical attack) magical damage to enemies and slowing them by 25% for 1s. Sound waves deal 300 (300 + 30% magical attack) extra magical damage to minions and 100% of this amount to monsters.
After using the skill, the next Basic Attack will deal 175 (175 + 25% magical attack) extra magical damage.
skill1.name: Tragic Beauty

skill2.description: Yuhuan plucks the strings, gaining 50% Movement Speed that diminishes over time. After 1.5s, she deals 275 (275 + 55% magical attack) magical damage to all enemies within a range of 600−800 and stuns them for 0.75s.
skill2.name: Mournful Tempo

skill3.description: Yuhuan rises into the air and plays a melody, becoming untargetable while airborne and removing all crowd control effects. When finished playing, she recovers 960 (800 + 120% magical attack + 5% Health) Health, restores 50% of this amount to allies within a range of 500, and deals 500 (500 + 75% magical attack) magical damage to enemies within range.
skill3.name: Unending Sorrow

skill4.description:
Yuhuan changes the melody to Melody of Peace, in which skills provide area healing.
War: Skills deal 90 (90 + 15% magical attack) extra magical damage to enemy units within a range of 800.
Peace: Skills restore 35 (35 + 6% magical attack) Health to allies, while also restoring (+ 6% extra Health) Health to herself.
skill4.name: Melody of Peace

strategy.earlyGame: The first thing Yuhuan learns in mid lane is switching melodies. Clearing waves in War speeds up her damage, and switching to Peace to heal after taking hits keeps her in lane longer. Tragic Beauty deals extra damage to minions and the enhanced basic attack that follows chips further, so until she has her ultimate, repeating sound waves and enhanced attacks is her basic pattern. Even if the enemy jungler closes in, she can turn them back with Mournful Tempo's speed and delayed stun.
strategy.midGame: Once she learns Unending Sorrow, the key decision is whether to use it for healing or dodging. She cannot be targeted and sheds crowd control while playing, so timing it to the enemy's burst makes big abilities miss. Rising into the air after seeing an enemy assassin's ultimate animation is a good way to waste it. In fights over Tyrant or Overlord, her job is staying put while restoring worn-down allies with Peace and the post-melody area healing. She lacks the burst to delete enemies, so in standoffs she chips with Tragic Beauty and turns aside dives with Mournful Tempo followed by Unending Sorrow. Steer the game into a war of attrition that favors her the longer it goes.
strategy.teamfight: Yuhuan's place is half a step behind the front line. Once the fight starts, switch to War for the extra area damage and keep cycling Tragic Beauty's sound waves and enhanced attacks. When an enemy dive turns toward her, drop Mournful Tempo, back away with its speed, and turn to stun them when it goes off. Rising with Unending Sorrow the moment enemy burst stacks up wastes their damage and still delivers her area healing. Leave finishing to her team and focus on throwing off the enemy's plans.

combos.title: Follow Through to the Enhanced Attack
combos.sequence: Skill 1 (Tragic Beauty: sound waves slow) → Basic Attack (enhanced attack deals extra damage) → Skill 1 (Tragic Beauty)
combos.description: Casting Tragic Beauty enhances her next basic attack with extra magical damage. The sound waves' slow is short, so follow up with the basic attack right away. In War, every skill also deals extra damage to enemies around her.

combos.title: Switch to Peace and Support
combos.sequence: Skill 4 (Melody of Peace: switch the melody) → Skill 1 (Tragic Beauty) → Skill 2 (Mournful Tempo: delayed stun)
combos.description: In Peace, every skill restores Health to nearby allies and herself. She can support without stopping her attacks, so she keeps firing from behind a worn-down front line. When it is time to push back, switch to War for the extra damage on each skill.

combos.title: A Melody That Makes Ultimates Miss
combos.sequence: time it to the enemy's big ability → Skill 3 (Unending Sorrow: untargetable, remove crowd control) → Skill 2 (Mournful Tempo) → Skill 1 (Tragic Beauty)
combos.description: While airborne she cannot be targeted and her crowd control effects are removed. Casting it too early dodges nothing, so the condition is to time it after seeing the enemy's big ability. When the melody ends, she and nearby allies heal and enemies in range take damage.

strengths: Switching melodies lets her both chip and heal on her own
Unending Sorrow makes her untargetable and removes crowd control, so she can make enemy ultimates miss
She chains Tragic Beauty into its enhanced basic attack, keeping her damage flowing
Area healing gives her staying power in long teamfights
weaknesses: Low burst, so finishing enemies alone is hard
Mournful Tempo's stun comes after a delay, so enemies who read it can avoid it
While Unending Sorrow is down, she has few ways to protect herself and is vulnerable to dives
She has little power to swing games herself and often relies on her team's damage

playstyle.style: Yuhuan is a mage who switches between two melodies, the offensive War and the healing Peace. In War, every skill deals extra damage to nearby enemies; in Peace, every skill restores Health to her allies and herself. Her ultimate, Unending Sorrow, lifts her into the air where she cannot be targeted and sheds crowd control, then heals her and nearby allies and damages enemies when the melody ends.
playstyle.suited: She suits players who want to decide, based on the fight, whether to lean into damage or healing. Choosing when to switch melodies and when to dodge an enemy ultimate with Unending Sorrow are where her skill shows. Her own finishing power is modest, so she often plays a supporting role for her team's damage.

synergy.reason: Zhang Fei's gust blows enemies back, so they land right where Chano's traps are already waiting.
Lapulapu launches enemies and slows them on landing, so they sit still for Chano's traps and wolf spirits.

counters.reason: Gao Changgong closes in from stealth, so the spacing Chano takes from the brush counts for nothing.
Musashi knocks projectiles out of the air with Illuminating Slash, so Chano's airborne shot dies in flight.

passive.description:
While in the brush, Chano gains 10-20% increased Movement Speed and accumulates Concealment, which reaches its maximum after 1s. When leaving the brush, he consumes Concealment to perform a leap, with the distance increasing based on the amount accumulated.
Entering the brush also enhances his next Basic Attack into a double shot (counts as 1 Basic Attack), with each arrow dealing 175 (70 + 60% physical attack) physical damage. The double shot has a 4s cooldown.
He deals 25% more damage to monsters while in the brush.
passive.name: Hunting

skill1.description:
Chano leaps into the air, gaining a Movement Speed boost and the ability to traverse terrain. While airborne, his Basic Attack becomes a powerful long-range arrow, dealing 580 (300 + 160% physical attack) physical damage and knocking back enemies (without applying crowd control), while also extending his air time.
Each 1% Attack Speed increases the arrow's damage by 2.
If he doesn't use the enhanced Basic Attack while airborne, he stores one with normal Attack Range for 3s upon landing.
If he uses the enhanced Basic Attack while moving the movement wheel away from the target, he dashes for a short distance in that direction.
skill1.name: Soaring Signal

skill2.description:
Chano throws a wolf spirit trap at the target location, exposing the enemy that triggers it and dealing 400 (400 + 100% extra physical attack) physical damage. A wolf spirit is also summoned at the trap's location to attack the enemy that triggered it.
Traps become invisible 2s after deploying. Up to 4 traps can be deployed simultaneously.
The wolf spirits inherit 25% of Chano's base stats and half of his Critical Damage, and each attack slows the target by 5-10% for 1s, for up to 5 stacks.
skill2.name: Lupine Trap

skill3.description:
Chano activates his Leader Stance, summoning (2 + Skill 2 charges) wolf spirits to charge in a designated direction, consuming stored charges of Skill 2 and activating all nearby traps.
He gains the Mounted Archery ability, allowing him to move while attacking and increasing his Movement Speed by 10%, Physical Attack by 50, and Attack Speed by 20% for 8s.
Each Basic Attack activates nearby targetless wolf spirits to join the attack.
skill3.name: Leader Stance

strategy.earlyGame: The first habit to build is simple: touch a bush before you shoot. In lane, move between the bushes on your side and along the river, landing the double shot and leaping back out again. Lupine Trap reveals whoever triggers it, so placing traps in bushes or river paths the enemy jungler is likely to use gives early warning of ganks.
strategy.midGame: Trap management becomes the core of his job once he starts moving away from lane. Several traps can be out at once and they turn invisible after a moment, so seeding them around Tyrant or Overlord in advance gives you vision and damage on anyone approaching. When someone closes in, leap with Soaring Signal and cross terrain to get away. The airborne arrow pushes the chaser back, and pushing away from the target as it fires moves him further back afterward. Attack Speed also raises the arrow's damage, so the more attack speed items he finishes, the heavier that parting shot becomes. The knockback applies no crowd control, though, so remember the chaser can act again right away.
strategy.teamfight: Chano enters teamfights from a side bush, not the front. Wait near the ground you've trapped, and when enemies walk onto it, use Leader Stance to set off every nearby trap and send the wolf pack charging. Mounted Archery lets him attack on the move, so he can keep dealing damage while backing away from their front line. Wolf spirit attacks slow their target with every hit, which also makes it easier to keep chasers at a distance. If you get pressed, cross terrain with Soaring Signal to make space, then return to a bush to ready the next double shot.

combos.title: Brush In, Brush Out
combos.sequence: Enter the brush (next Basic Attack becomes a double shot) → Basic Attack (double shot) → Leave the brush (leap scaled to Concealment)
combos.description: Concealment fills after a short stay, so wait a moment before leaving if you want the longer leap.

combos.title: Trap Field Detonation
combos.sequence: Skill 2 (Lupine Trap: place several ahead of time) → Skill 3 (Leader Stance: trigger all nearby traps, wolf spirits charge) → Basic Attack (Mounted Archery, firing on the move)
combos.description: Traps turn invisible shortly after landing, and several can be out at once. Leader Stance sets off every nearby trap and sends in extra wolf spirits for each Lupine Trap charge you kept in reserve, so neither the placed traps nor the saved charges go to waste. During Mounted Archery, each Basic Attack brings an idle wolf spirit into the fight, so keep firing as you back away.

combos.title: Aerial Shot and Slide
combos.sequence: Skill 1 (Soaring Signal: leap up and cross terrain) → Basic Attack (airborne arrow with knockback) → Input away from the target (move after the arrow)
combos.description: The airborne arrow knocks enemies back but applies no crowd control. Push the movement wheel away from the target as you fire and Chano moves in that direction afterward, which widens the gap to whoever is chasing. If he lands without firing, an enhanced Basic Attack at normal range stays stored for a short time.

strengths: Every trip into a bush readies a double shot, and leaving it gives him a leap for distance
Lupine Trap handles vision, damage and a wolf-spirit chaser in one placement
Leader Stance's Mounted Archery lets him keep attacking while he moves
Soaring Signal crosses terrain, and the airborne arrow pushes chasers back
weaknesses: Away from bushes, the speed boost and the leap are not available
The airborne arrow's knockback applies no crowd control, so the target can act right away
If a fight starts before traps are down, neither the wolf spirits nor Leader Stance's mass trigger has anything to work with
Many inputs to manage, such as steering away from the target as the arrow fires

playstyle.style: A marksman whose next move gets stronger every time he goes in or out of the brush. Entering a bush turns his next Basic Attack into a double shot, and leaving one lets him leap as far as his stored Concealment allows. He can keep several Lupine Traps out at once, so setting the field before the shooting starts is part of Chano's job too.
playstyle.suited: His strength depends on where the bushes are and where his traps sit, so he suits players who read the terrain before a fight. His inputs are on the busy side too, such as pushing the movement wheel away from the target as the airborne arrow fires to slide back. If the game keeps turning into straight-up shootouts on open ground, his brush-based strengths go unused.

synergy.reason: Erin builds damage the more Basic Attacks she lands, and Yang Jian holding the front line buys her that time.
Huang Zhong cannot move in Turret Mode, so Yang Jian stopping divers in front keeps him firing.

counters.reason: Diaochan's blink keeps shortening its own cooldown, so chasing her down seldom works for Yang Jian.
Luna's dash resets its cooldown on every marked target, so she keeps diving Yang Jian without pause.

passive.description:
Heaven-Earth Form: Yang Jian gains Resistance (up to 60-90%, scaling with Ultimate level) when his Basic Attacks and skills deal damage. Upon reaching max Resistance, he enters Heaven-Earth Form, gaining crowd control immunity. Attacking a hero in this state knocks back nearby enemies, enhances his skills and Attack Range, and grants 600 Max Health.
Heavenly Eye: Hits with his skills grant 1 stack of Energy (up to 3 stacks). When enemies move away from Yang Jian, the Heavenly Eye fires light beams, dealing 80 (+25% extra physical attack) physical damage and recovering 60 (+1% extra Health) (halved against non-hero units).
Outside Heaven-Earth Form, Yang Jian's Resistance is capped at 25%.
passive.name: Mind Games

skill1.description:
Yang Jian summons the Heaven Hound to charge forward, dealing 200 (200 + 60% extra physical attack) physical damage, marking the hit enemy, and granting vision of them (lasts 5s). While the mark is active, he can use the skill again to dash to the enemy, dealing 300 (300 + 90% extra physical attack) physical damage, as well as additional physical damage equal to 15% of the target's lost Health.
If the skill misses, Heaven Hound will remain at the endpoint, searching for targets. When Yang Jian approaches, Heaven Hound returns to its master, reducing this skill's remaining cooldown by 25%-50%.
If an enemy dies while marked, this skill's cooldown is reset.
skill1.name: Unleash the Hound

skill2.description:
Yang Jian sweeps with his spear, dealing 350 (350 + 100% extra physical attack) physical damage to enemies in range, slowing them by 15% for (2s) and stunning them for (1/2s, doubled if the target's remaining Health percentage is higher than Yang Jian's).
After hitting an enemy with this skill, Yang Jian's Basic Attacks deal an additional 125 (125 + 36% extra physical attack) true damage (lasts 5s).
skill2.name: Vain Disillusionment

skill3.description:
Yang Jian uses Heavenly Eye to fire 3 light beams, dealing 340 (340 + 110% extra physical attack) physical damage to enemies in their path, while recovering 300 (300 + 4.5% extra Health) Health (halved for non-hero units).
If multiple light beams hit the same target, subsequent light beams deal only 30% damage and recover 50% Health.
skill3.name: Sight of Origin

strategy.earlyGame: Yang Jian first builds Resistance through damage from Basic Attacks and skills. Until Heaven-Earth Form his Resistance is capped, so instead of forcing long brawls, build a lead gradually with Unleash the Hound's chip damage and Vain Disillusionment's true damage. When the opponent moves away, the Heavenly Eye fires beams that deal damage and heal him.
strategy.midGame: From the mid game on, things really start once he fills his Resistance and enters Heaven-Earth Form. In that form he is immune to crowd control and can attack with enhanced skills while knocking back enemies around him when fighting heroes. If a marked enemy dies, Unleash the Hound's cooldown resets, so pounce on wounded enemies one after another.
strategy.teamfight: Mark his target with Unleash the Hound, pounce, then stop them with Vain Disillusionment. In Heaven-Earth Form he cannot be stopped by crowd control, so fire Sight of Origin in the middle of the brawl to chip while healing. Diving first without his Resistance built up tends to lose trades, so go in together with his front line.

combos.title: Mark, Then Pounce
combos.sequence: Skill 1 (Unleash the Hound: mark with the Heaven Hound) → Skill 1 (recast to pounce) → Skill 2 (Vain Disillusionment: sweep and stun) → Basic Attack (true damage)
combos.description: An enemy hit by the Heaven Hound is marked, and he gains vision of them for a while. Recasting during the mark pounces on them, adding damage based on their lost Health. Vain Disillusionment stuns longer when the target's Health percentage is higher than his, so landing it early in a trade holds them longer.

combos.title: Chip and Heal With Sight of Origin
combos.sequence: Skill 3 (Sight of Origin: fire three beams) → Skill 2 (Vain Disillusionment) → Basic Attack
combos.description: Sight of Origin fires three beams, restoring his Health on each hit. Several beams hitting the same target at once deal less damage and heal less, so firing them through several enemies wastes less.

combos.title: Retrieve a Missed Hound
combos.sequence: Skill 1 (Unleash the Hound: on a miss, the hound stays at the endpoint) → approach to retrieve it (cooldown shortened) → Skill 1 (Unleash the Hound: mark) → Skill 1 (recast to pounce)
combos.description: A Heaven Hound that misses keeps searching for targets at its endpoint. Walking close brings it back and shortens the remaining cooldown. It also works as a scout thrown into a bush to check for danger, so missing costs little.

strengths: Heaven-Earth Form grants crowd control immunity and strengthens his skills and range
Unleash the Hound's pounce deals damage based on lost Health, making wounded enemies easy to finish
Basic Attacks after Vain Disillusionment add true damage, getting through tough targets
Sight of Origin's light beams chip distant enemies while restoring his Health
weaknesses: He struggles before entering Heaven-Earth Form and tends to lose short trades
Missing Unleash the Hound leaves him with few ways to close in
Sight of Origin deals less damage and healing when several beams hit the same target

playstyle.style: Yang Jian is a fighter whose Resistance rises as his Basic Attacks and skills deal damage, and who fights in Heaven-Earth Form once it maxes out. In Heaven-Earth Form he is immune to crowd control, his skills and range are enhanced, and his max Health rises. An enemy marked by the Heaven Hound from Unleash the Hound can be pounced on with a recast, taking damage based on their lost Health.
playstyle.suited: He suits players who enjoy building up their own enhancement by staying in a brawl. Outside Heaven-Earth Form his Resistance has a low cap, so he needs the patience to fill it through repeated short trades.

synergy.reason: Zhang Fei's slows bog enemies down, so Nuwa's ground-laid matrix explosions land on them.
Mozi's barrier stuns enemies where they stand, so Nuwa can box them in with her matrices.

counters.reason: Han Xin leaps in over the ground, so Nuwa's matrices never stand between him and her.
Gao Changgong chains a heavy slow into a stun, and Nuwa has only one escape to answer with.

passive.description: Nuwa gains 10-20% vision, Basic Attack range, and skill range (increases with hero level).
passive.name: Divine Consciousness

skill1.description:
Nuwa unleashes energy in the target direction, dealing 225 (225 + 42% magical attack) magical damage to enemies in its path and knocking them back. After hitting an enemy, the energy gradually stops and expands in a cross shape, forming a matrix. This deals 225 (225 + 42% magical attack) magical damage to enemies hit.
The cross deals an extra 50% damage to enemies at its center, and sets off explosions if it touches matrices.
skill1.name: Divine Glow - Creation

skill2.description:
Nuwa creates a matrix that only she can traverse and enemy heroes cannot pass through. Each matrix lasts 3.5s.
Whenever a matrix is hit by one of Nuwa's other skills, it sets off an explosion that deals 210 (210 + 40% magical attack) magical damage to nearby enemies.
When matrices fuse, they deal 180 (180 + 35% magical attack) magical damage (+50% extra damage in the center) on collision and knock back enemies for 0.5s. Collisions gain up to 30% extra range based on the initial distance between matrices. Up to 3 matrices can be stocked. When multiple matrices explode simultaneously, they only deal damage to the same target once.
skill2.name: Divine Glow - Coalescence

skill3.description: Nuwa teleports to the target location while gaining 30% Movement Speed and a shield that negates 600 (600 + 9% extra Health) damage for 2s. She also deals 300 (300 + 57% magical attack) magical damage to enemies within the target area and slows them by 25-50% for 0.5s. Enemies take less damage the farther away they are from her, down to 50% of the initial damage.
skill3.name: Divine Glow - Emergence

skill4.description: Nuwa releases pure energy, dealing 600 (600 + 115% magical attack) magical damage to enemies in its path. The pure energy will set off an explosion if it touches a matrix.
skill4.name: Divine Glow - Annihilation

strategy.earlyGame: Nuwa's passive extends the reach of her basic attacks and skills, so in mid lane she can clear the wave from a step further back than her opponent. Divine Glow - Creation hits and knocks back enemies in its path, so sending it where minions and the opponent overlap clears and pokes in one cast. Before using matrices to attack, place one on the path the enemy jungler is likely to take; enemy heroes cannot pass through it and have to go around. Keep Divine Glow - Emergence, with its teleport and shield, in hand until the threat of a gank is gone.
strategy.midGame: Once she leaves lane, more of her time goes into placing matrices on the narrow paths leading to objectives. Enemy heroes cannot pass through the walls, so the right placement can block both the way in and the way out. In standoffs before Tyrant or Overlord, place two walls and then send Divine Glow - Creation through; the cross touches the walls, explodes, and takes HP off the enemy before the fight starts. Matrices can be stocked, so refill them before your team commits and you will have more walls to place. Do not spend Divine Glow - Emergence on offense; keep it to get away from a diving assassin. Put a wall down where you land as well, and whoever is chasing cannot get through.
strategy.teamfight: How a teamfight goes depends on where her walls were placed before it started. Read the route the enemy will take, lay matrices across it, and send Divine Glow - Creation and Divine Glow - Annihilation into the group to stack explosions. Once the fight is on, choose between placing a wall in front of fleeing enemies to cut off their retreat, or between your back line and the enemy assassin to keep them away. Stand at the very back and hold Divine Glow - Emergence as your last way out.

combos.title: Stack Explosions With the Cross and Walls
combos.sequence: Skill 2 (Divine Glow - Coalescence: place a matrix) → Skill 1 (Divine Glow - Creation: spreads into a cross where it hits) → Skill 4 (Divine Glow - Annihilation: send the pure energy through)
combos.description: With a matrix already in place, an explosion goes off where Divine Glow - Creation's cross touches it. Enemies at the center of the cross take extra damage, and enemies near the wall are also hit by the explosion. Divine Glow - Annihilation also sets off an explosion if a matrix is in its path.

combos.title: Get Away, Then Close the Path
combos.sequence: Skill 3 (Divine Glow - Emergence: teleport and shield) → Skill 2 (place a matrix) → Skill 2 (place a second one so they fuse) → Skill 1 (Divine Glow - Creation)
combos.description: After teleporting away with Divine Glow - Emergence, place a matrix between you and the chaser; enemy heroes cannot pass through it. A second matrix makes the two fuse and knock back enemies where they collide, which stops the chase. Hit the stalled enemy with Divine Glow - Creation and open the gap further.

strengths: Her passive extends range and vision, so she can fire from further away than her opponent
Enemy heroes cannot pass through matrices, so she can close off paths
Hitting a matrix with another skill sets off an explosion that damages an area
Divine Glow - Emergence's teleport and shield let her get away at least once when someone reaches her
weaknesses: Walls need setting up before she fires, which makes sudden scrambles hard
Divine Glow - Emergence is her only escape, and once it is used she struggles if someone closes in
Matrices do not last long, so she keeps having to place them again
Divine Glow - Annihilation only hits enemies in its path

playstyle.style: Nuwa is a mage who uses her passive's extra range and vision to wear enemies down from afar. The matrices she places with Divine Glow - Coalescence are walls that only she can move through quickly and that enemy heroes cannot cross, and they explode when her other skills hit them. Placing walls first and firing second is what drives both her damage and her safety.
playstyle.suited: Every exchange starts with deciding where to put a wall. If you like taking time to set up and opening fights on your own terms, you will enjoy how a well-placed wall turns straight into damage. Players who are at their best reacting in sudden scrambles may find the setup time frustrating.

synergy.reason: Sun Bin's Time Flux gives the diving Nezha the speed to stay on a target and then get out.
Zhang Fei's Leaping Savior shields teammates around his landing spot, so a Nezha diving in with him holds the line longer.

counters.reason: Donghuang's Forsaken Contract makes the two share damage, so Nezha's own team ends up hitting him.
Diaochan heals each time her floral marks trigger and burns Nezha with true damage for staying close.

passive.description:
Nezha receives a shield that negates 75 (75 + 1.5% extra Health) true damage for every enemy hero he damages with a skill, for up to 800 (800 + 20% extra Health) true damage in total. This also triggers Wind-Fire Wheels 1 time, increasing Movement Speed by 5% for 3s, for up to 5 stacks.
The true damage shield can be recovered at the spawn point.
When he deals damage using Basic Attacks or Scorching Ember, or deals damage to a non-hero unit, he only gets a shield negating 20 (20 + 0.5% extra Health) true damage.
Each target can trigger Wind-Fire Wheels up to 1 time.
passive.name: Scorching Ember

skill1.description:
Nezha deals 330 (330 + 100% extra physical attack) physical damage to nearby enemies and places Scorching Ember on them, dealing 42 (42 + 17% extra physical attack) true damage to the enemy every second for 5s, for up to 3 stacks. Damage increases by 50% with each stack. Scorching Ember also reduces the target's Health recovery by 15%.
The duration of Scorching Ember is refreshed when Nezha deals damage to the target.
skill1.name: Fire-tipped Spear - Sweep

skill2.description:
Flips behind the target to deal 150 (150 + 65% extra physical attack) physical damage. He also gains a shield that negates 24 (24 + 0.5% extra Health) true damage, halved for non-hero units.
This skill cannot be used on the same target again for 3s.
skill2.name: Red Armillary Sash - Bind

skill3.description:
Nezha selects an enemy hero and flies to their location, dealing 450 (450 + 160% extra physical attack) physical damage and knocking them back.
After landing, Nezha gains 10% damage reduction and 20% Resistance for 4s.
This skill enters a 50%-100% Cooldown based on flight distance. If the target is untargetable upon arrival, Nezha waits until the untargetable state ends and then immediately knocks the target back (can wait up to 0.5s).
skill3.name: Universe Ring - Skyfall

skill4.description:
Nezha unleashes the universe ring, dealing 140 (140 + 45% extra physical attack) physical damage to all enemy heroes across the entire map and gaining vision. Enhances the range of Universe Ring - Skyfall to cover the entire map for 5s.
Heroes revealed by this effect cannot use recall.
skill4.name: Universe Ring

strategy.earlyGame: Before learning Universe Ring - Skyfall, Nezha doesn't force a win; he chips with Scorching Ember from Fire-tipped Spear - Sweep. Each skill hit on an enemy hero adds to his shield, so many short trades suit him. Red Armillary Sash - Bind flips him behind the opponent, but it cannot be used on the same target again right away.
strategy.midGame: Once he learns Universe Ring - Skyfall, how he plays the map changes. When the minimap shows a wounded enemy or an isolated back-liner, fly to them, break their position with the landing knockback and sandwich them with your team. Skyfall's cooldown depends on flight distance, so the closer the target, the sooner it comes back. When the fight over Tyrant stalls, pressuring the opposite lane without showing himself makes it easier to force the enemy to split up. Limit your targets to enemies your team can reach right away. Flying in the moment the enemy marksman steps forward lets the knockback pull them out of formation, and Scorching Ember follows straight after. Scorching Ember's healing reduction also slows the support's attempts to restore them. The November 5 update lowered the damage of Fire-tipped Spear - Sweep and Skyfall.
strategy.teamfight: Decide in advance whether Nezha flies first or last. If your team has another engager, flying onto the remaining damage dealer after the enemy has used their crowd control is the steadier option. After landing, stack Scorching Ember with Fire-tipped Spear - Sweep and keep flipping behind the target with Red Armillary Sash - Bind to burn them down with true damage. He struggles when the enemy spreads out and fires from range, so aim to start fights in tight terrain.

combos.title: Ambush From Map-Wide Vision
combos.sequence: Skill 4 (Universe Ring: damage and vision on every enemy hero) → Skill 3 (Universe Ring - Skyfall: fly in and knock back) → Skill 1 (Fire-tipped Spear - Sweep: Scorching Ember) → Skill 2 (Red Armillary Sash - Bind: flip behind)
combos.description: Pick a target whose recall is blocked by Universe Ring's vision and fly to them with Universe Ring - Skyfall. Landing grants damage reduction and Resistance, so keep chipping with Fire-tipped Spear - Sweep and Red Armillary Sash - Bind and hold on until your team arrives.

combos.title: Keep Scorching Ember Burning
combos.sequence: Skill 1 (Fire-tipped Spear - Sweep: apply Scorching Ember) → Skill 2 (Red Armillary Sash - Bind: flip behind and gain a shield) → Skill 1 (Fire-tipped Spear - Sweep: add stacks)
combos.description: Scorching Ember keeps dealing true damage for a while and grows with each stack. Dealing damage also refreshes its duration, so weave in Red Armillary Sash - Bind flips and keep it burning. Red Armillary Sash cannot be used on the same target again right away, so fill the gaps with Fire-tipped Spear - Sweep and Basic Attacks.

strengths: Universe Ring - Skyfall flies him to a distant enemy hero, and Universe Ring extends it to the whole map
Scorching Ember's true damage and healing reduction get through enemies who rely on healing
His shield stacks every time a skill lands, so he is hard to kill in brawls
After Universe Ring - Skyfall lands, he takes less damage and gains Resistance
weaknesses: Universe Ring - Skyfall only flies him to the target, so he is easily isolated if his team does not follow
His burst is modest, so targets sometimes escape before he finishes them
His shield only stacks when skills land, so a string of misses leaves him unprotected
Until he learns Universe Ring - Skyfall, Red Armillary Sash - Bind's flip is his only way to close in

playstyle.style: Nezha is a fighter who stacks a shield against true damage every time his skills hit an enemy hero, and drops from the sky onto a chosen enemy hero with Universe Ring - Skyfall. Casting Universe Ring briefly lets Skyfall reach every enemy hero on the map, and enemies it reveals cannot recall. Scorching Ember, applied by Fire-tipped Spear - Sweep, keeps dealing true damage and reduces the target's Health recovery.
playstyle.suited: He suits players who want to go catch a chosen target themselves. Universe Ring - Skyfall leaves him isolated if his team does not follow, so he needs the composure to check the minimap for teammates before flying. Whether you can hold Universe Ring until the turning point of the match also decides how he plays.

synergy.reason: Guiguzi's pull bunches enemies into one spot and stuns them, so every flying sword lands at once.
Dolia's Celestial Melody refunds Freshly Forged, so Gan & Mo get another full set of flying sword charges.

counters.reason: Mai Shiranui strips magical defense, then dashes in and launches Gan & Mo, who cannot answer while airborne.
Sun Ce keeps super armor while piloting his ship, so the knockback on Guard Her Grave cannot stop him.

passive.description:
Whenever Gan uses a flying sword skill at a target location, Mo unleashes an equal number of swords to the same location at the same time to deal equal damage. Flying sword skills share usage caps.
Flying swords place 1 stack of Sword Energy on enemies hit. If a flying sword hits a marked target, each stack deals 75 (75 + 12% magical attack) magical damage.
If multiple flying swords hit a marked target at the same time, subsequent hits only deal 50% of this damage.
Gan & Mo's Basic Attacks deal 300 (300 + 25% magical attack) magical damage.
passive.name: Forever Entwined

skill1.description:
Gan unleashes Splitting Swords in the target direction, dealing 300 (300 + 50% magical attack) magical damage twice to enemies within range and knocking them back, while also retreating in the opposite direction. Reduces hit enemies' Magical Defense by 150 for 3s.
Passive: Each defeat or assist grants Gan & Mo 1 Splitting Sword, increasing their magical attack by 15, for up to 20 stacks.
skill1.name: Guard Her Grave

skill2.description:
Unleash flying swords in the target direction, dealing 325 (325 + 45% magical attack) magical damage to enemies in their path, and an extra 75 (75 + 12% magical attack) magical damage to enemies with Sword Energy.
Flying sword skills share a usage cap, with one charge restored every 5-6s (cooldown reduces with skill level). When the same Sword Energy is triggered multiple times, the second time onwards only deals 50% damage.
skill2.name: Coupled Blades - Short

skill3.description:
Unleash flying swords in the target direction, dealing 325 (325 + 45% magical attack) magical damage to enemies in their path, and an extra 75 (75 + 12% magical attack) magical damage to enemies with Sword Energy.
Flying sword skills share a usage cap, with one charge restored every 5-6s (cooldown reduces with skill level). When the same Sword Energy is triggered multiple times, the second time onwards only deals 50% damage.
skill3.name: Coupled Blades - Long

skill4.description:
Immediately gains 2 uses of flying sword skills and enhances the next flying sword skill to unleash more swords.
Passive: Increases field of vision by 15% and increases the usage cap of flying sword skills by 1. Each time a flying sword hits an enemy, this skill's cooldown is reduced by 1s.
skill4.name: Freshly Forged

strategy.earlyGame: Gan & Mo outrange their mid-lane opponent from the start. First, get a feel for overlapping the short and long swords on one spot against standing minions. Flying swords take time to come back, so don't step forward right after spending them.
strategy.midGame: From the mid game on, drop swords from max range on enemies entering the pit before Tyrant or Overlord. The enemy then has to start the fight already worn down.
