When his Basic Attacks and skills hit enemy heroes, he gains Fury, increasing his Physical and Magical Pierce by up to 40% and damage reduction by up to 20%. Upon reaching max Fury, he recovers 168 (80 + 50% physical attack) Health, with a cooldown of 8s.
The lower his current Health, the more Health he recovers, for up to 3 times the base recovery.
His Physical Lifesteal takes 75% effect and applies to magical and true damage. His Basic Attacks only carry 60% of on-hit effects.
passive.name: Howling Blade

skill1.description:
Allain swipes upward, dealing 177 (110 + 38% physical attack) magical damage, 177 (110 + 38% physical attack) physical damage twice, and launching targets directly in front of him for 0.75s. After the initial strikes of this skill, he performs different follow-up strikes depending on how many marks he has stacked.
1 Mark: Strikes twice more, the first strike dealing 177 (110 + 38% physical attack) magical damage and the second strike dealing 177 (110 + 38% physical attack) physical damage.
2 Marks: Increases the launch range and strikes another 2 times, the first strike dealing 177 (110 + 38% physical attack) magical damage and the second strike dealing 177 (110 + 38% physical attack) physical damage. He can move slowly while performing the strikes.
3 Marks: Increases the launch range and strikes another 2 times, the first strike dealing 177 (110 + 38% physical attack) true damage and the second strike dealing 312 (180 + 75% physical attack) true damage. He can move slowly and gains crowd control immunity while performing the strikes.
He gains stacks when his Ultimate and Basic Attacks hit enemies. Skill 1 can trigger 50% of the Basic Attack's on-hit effects, and can grant lifesteal and deal critical damage.
skill1.name: Meteor Kill

skill2.description:
Allain dashes in the target direction, dealing 144 (100 + 25% physical attack) physical damage and 144 (100 + 25% physical attack) magical damage to enemies in his path and reducing their Movement Speed by 15% for 1.5s. He also gains 10% Movement Speed for 3s, and his next 3 Basic Attacks gain 40% extra Attack Speed.
He stocks 1 charge of this skill every 10s (affected by Cooldown Reduction), for up to 2 charges.
skill2.name: Moonlight Flash

skill3.description:
Allain selects a target hero and leaps into the air for 1.5s, during which he can move and is untargetable. He then smashes into the ground, dealing 254 (175 + 45% physical attack) physical damage and 254 (175 + 45% physical attack) magical damage to enemy heroes. The closer the heroes are to him, the more damage they take, for up to 100% extra damage. He gains marks and Fury for every enemy hero hit.
This skill produces different effects depending on whether the targeted hero is an enemy or a teammate. When he lands, he grants himself or the targeted teammate a shield that negates 627 (450 + 100% physical attack) damage. For every extra enemy hero hit, the shield's strength is increased by 1/3.
skill3.name: Death at Sunset

strategy.earlyGame: Not committing before his marks are built is Allain's basic rule in the clash lane. Build marks through Basic Attack trades, and after casting Meteor Kill, back off instead of chasing, repeating short trades. Healing at max Fury grows the lower his Health, so he can hold up in brawls even after taking some damage.
strategy.midGame: From the mid game on, push a side lane to draw an opponent out, then chase them with Moonlight Flash's dash for a one-on-one. Thanks to his passive, lifesteal from items works at reduced strength but also applies to magical and true damage. His Basic Attacks deal physical and magical damage at once, so lifesteal items readily turn into healing. Join teamfights late from a side bush, and time Death at Sunset's untargetable window to make enemy big skills miss. His damage and durability drop when marks and Fury run out, so go into fights with them built up.
strategy.teamfight: First decide which enemy you most want to take down and stick to them. Moonlight Flash holds two charges, so use the first to close in and the second to cut off their escape. Fury raises his pierce and damage reduction as it builds, so surviving the first clash matters most.

combos.title: Three-Mark Meteor Kill
combos.sequence: Basic Attack (three hits to build marks) → Skill 1 (Meteor Kill: cast at three marks)
combos.description: Meteor Kill with three marks widens its launch and adds two follow-up strikes of true damage. He can move slowly while swinging and is immune to crowd control, so minor interruptions do not stop him. Without marks, it ends after the opening strikes and the launch.

combos.title: Speed Up and Go All In
combos.sequence: Skill 2 (Moonlight Flash: dash and speed up the next three Basic Attacks) → Basic Attack (three hits for marks) → Skill 1 (Meteor Kill: three marks) → Skill 3 (Death at Sunset: target an enemy hero and slam down)
combos.description: The three sped-up Basic Attacks after Moonlight Flash become the three marks. Death at Sunset deals more damage to enemies closer to where he lands, and every enemy hero hit returns marks and Fury, so landing in the middle of the brawl speeds up his next cycle.

combos.title: Escape by Targeting a Teammate
combos.sequence: Skill 3 (Death at Sunset: target a teammate and leap) → land (shield for himself and the teammate) → Skill 2 (Moonlight Flash: get out)
combos.description: Leaping to a teammate the moment he is focused makes him untargetable while airborne, and he can still move. The more enemy heroes the landing damages, the thicker the shield, so it works not only as an escape but as a way to hand out shields and turn back into the fight.

strengths: He mixes physical, magical and true damage, so stacking only one kind of defense does not stop him
His lifesteal also applies to magical and true damage
Meteor Kill at three marks launches an area while he is immune to crowd control
Death at Sunset alone covers chasing, dodging and shielding a teammate
weaknesses: Until marks and Fury build up, his damage is lower than it should be
Enemies who stack slows and kite him make marks hard to build
Only part of item on-hit effects apply to his Basic Attacks, so item choices need care
Moonlight Flash is his main way to close in, and once it is spent, chasing and escaping are both hard

playstyle.style: Allain is a fighter whose dual-sword Basic Attacks deal physical and magical damage at the same time, with true damage added on every third attack. The more marks he builds with Basic Attacks and Death at Sunset, the more follow-up strikes Meteor Kill gets, and at three marks it also grants crowd control immunity. His ultimate, Death at Sunset, can target an enemy or a teammate, and he cannot be targeted while airborne.
playstyle.suited: He suits players who enjoy holding back until marks are built, then attacking all at once. He needs to decide on the spot whether to use Death at Sunset for a chase or to target a teammate and escape while handing out shields.

synergy.reason: Sun Bin's slow clumps enemies, so Augran can mark them with Death's Precipice and link Soul Resonance to several.

counters.reason: Arli blinks away and speeds up without her parasol, so Augran's Soul Resonance never stays connected.

passive.description:
Augran's Basic Attacks vibrate his dagger-axe to resonate with an enemy's soul for 3s. The soul resonance deals 88 (50% physical attack) physical damage upon connection and will continue to deal damage with increasing frequency unless it is broken. When it ends, it deals a further 211 (70 + 80% physical attack) magical damage.
The soul resonance's initial and final damage carry 100% of the on-hit effect, while the rest carries 50%.
passive.name: Soul Resonance

skill1.description:
Augran carves a path to the afterlife, dealing 280 (280 + 95% extra physical attack) magical damage to targets it hits.
The path accelerates after hitting walls or the Life-Death Border, then deals an additional 150 (150 + 60% extra physical attack) magical damage to enemies hit. While on the path, Augran ignores terrain and gains 50% Movement Speed. The first time the path hits a wall, it creates an afterlife bridge. When Augran traverses the bridge, he gains a burst of Movement Speed, while nearby enemies are slowed by 15%.
Augran can use this skill again to recall his dagger-axe, entering the Seer State for 4s. If his Basic Attacks target an enemy with less than 10% Health (750-1,500 for monsters depending on hero level), Augran will instantly execute them.
This skill deals full contact damage to non-hero units. The dagger-axe will automatically be summoned back when the skill's cooldown ends.
skill1.name: Path of Passing

skill2.description:
Augran swings his dagger-axe, dealing 200 (200 + 60% extra physical attack) physical damage to enemies in front and slowing them by 25% for 1s. He then leaves behind a Life-Death Border, marking enemies who touch it. Enemies who touch the dead branches on the border also take 140 (140 + 45% extra physical attack) magical damage and are slowed by 25% for 1s.
Augran enhances his next Basic Attack, dealing 50% extra damage to the target and recovering 80 (80 + 1.5% extra Health) Health for himself. If there are marked enemies within range, the resonance applies the same extra damage and recovery effect for each marked target.
This skill also knocks back non-hero units. The resonance can link to up to 3 targets. When resonating with non-hero units, the recovery effect is only 50% effective.
skill2.name: Death's Precipice

skill3.description:
Augran channels his divine power and descends from the sky, dealing 380 (380 + 150% extra physical attack) physical damage to nearby enemies and knocking them back for 0.5s. If he hits an enemy hero, he recovers 750 (750 + 12% extra Health) Health and conjures their spirit counterparts to assist him for 8s.
After descending, he enters the Seer State for 8s. If his Basic Attacks hit a target with less than 10% Health (750-1,500 for monsters depending on hero level), they will deal a fatal blow instantly.
Every enemy hero hit increases recovery by 50%, up to a max increase of 100%. The conjured spirits inherit 30% of Augran's physical attack. They can only use Basic Attacks, but have higher Movement Speed and Attack Speed.
skill3.name: Conductor of Souls

strategy.earlyGame: Augran clears the jungle by keeping the soul resonance connected with Basic Attacks and weaving Death's Precipice in between. Healing from monsters is halved, but marking several monsters means more targets feeding it. Path of Passing deals full contact damage to monsters, and the Seer State's execute works on them too. When you head out to gank, the path lets him ignore terrain and approach from the far side of a wall.
strategy.midGame: Path of Passing speeds up when it touches a wall or a Life-Death Border, and enemies it hits afterwards take extra damage. The first wall it touches becomes an afterlife bridge; crossing it gives Augran a burst of Movement Speed and slows nearby enemies. When chasing, mark the target with the border, close in along the path, then recall the dagger-axe to enter the Seer State once they are hurt. After he learns his Ultimate, Conductor of Souls also puts him in the Seer State after landing, giving him a longer window to execute.
strategy.teamfight: Augran is looking for a Conductor of Souls landing on a group of enemy heroes. The more enemy heroes the descent hits, the more he heals, and he also conjures spirits shaped like them. The descent knocks enemies away, so after landing, re-mark them with Death's Precipice's border and draw healing from every marked target with the enhanced Basic Attack. Soul resonance hits more often the longer it stays connected, so he needs to stay close to enemies after landing as well. When enemies drop low during the Seer State, finish them with Basic Attacks.

combos.title: Run the Path Through the Border
combos.sequence: Skill 2 (Death's Precipice: place a Life-Death Border) → Skill 1 (Path of Passing: drive it into the border) → Basic Attack (enhanced, heals) → Skill 1 (recast for the Seer State)
combos.description: Path of Passing gets stronger after touching a wall or the border, so instead of relying on terrain, create the surface yourself and send the path through it. Enemies who touch the border are marked, and the enhanced Basic Attack's extra damage and healing reach every marked target. Recalling the dagger-axe at the end opens a window to execute weakened enemies with Basic Attacks.

combos.title: Descend, Then Spread the Marks
combos.sequence: Skill 3 (Conductor of Souls: descend and conjure spirits) → Skill 2 (Death's Precipice: mark with the border) → Basic Attack (enhanced) → Basic Attack (execute in the Seer State)
combos.description: Healing from the descent grows with each enemy hero hit, so land where they are bunched up. Once the knockback pushes them apart, mark them again with the border, then finish weakened enemies during the Seer State that follows the landing.

strengths: The more enemies Death's Precipice marks, the further his enhanced Basic Attack's extra damage and healing spread
On the path he ignores terrain and can approach from behind walls
In the Seer State, his Basic Attacks execute enemies and monsters that are low on Health
Conductor of Souls heals more for each enemy hero it hits and conjures spirits shaped like them
weaknesses: Soul resonance gets stronger the longer it stays connected, so it falls short in quick trades
Both his healing and his executes need him in Basic Attack range
Conductor of Souls knocks enemies away on landing instead of holding them in place
Recasting the path and placing the border mean many decisions in every fight

playstyle.style: Path of Passing speeds up when it hits a wall, and Augran can make it accelerate by driving it into a Life-Death Border he placed himself. The soul resonance his Basic Attacks create deals damage more and more often the longer it stays connected. Enemies left with very little Health can be executed with Basic Attacks once he enters the Seer State.
playstyle.suited: His strengths show when he can stand next to enemies and keep landing Basic Attacks. Each fight asks a lot of decisions, such as when to recast Path of Passing and where to place the border, so he suits players who like building a fight step by step. In short exchanges the soul resonance never fully ramps up, so you also need the patience to drag fights out.

synergy.reason: Zhang Fei's shield and knockback hold the front line, letting Ao'yin attack through all of True Dragon Sword.

counters.reason: Arli blinks off with the speed she gains from dropping her parasol, then shoves Ao'yin back out of range.
Consort Yu can go immune to physical attacks, and nearly everything Ao'yin deals is physical.

passive.description:
The elemental Dragon Souls from Ao'yin's last 2 skill attacks will be attached to his primary and secondary swords. He deals 165 (100% physical attack) physical damage with his primary sword, and if there are other enemies nearby he will also attack them with his secondary sword to deal 57 (35% physical attack -70% physical attack) physical damage.
When using skills, he gains 1 Dragon Soul mark (up to 3 marks) and 1 enhanced Basic Attack. Using the enhanced Basic Attack expends all marks, unleashing Dragon Souls that attack the target (Each mark grants 1 extra attack, with subsequent hits dealing half damage). Effects vary depending on the type of Dragon Soul attached to his primary sword.
When switching between elements, Dragon Souls of the same element is prioritized.
passive.name: Hidden Dragon

skill1.description:
Ao'yin unleashes a wave of sword energy, gaining 1 extra Dragon Soul mark and dealing 270 (270 + 70% extra physical attack) physical damage and 70 (70 + 16% extra physical attack) true damage (and 50% splash damage behind the target) to up to 3 targets within range.
Use of Flaming Palm attaches 1 Fire Dragon Soul to his sword, allowing him to deal an extra 15 physical damage during Basic Attacks. If a Fire Dragon Soul is attached to both swords, he deals 50% more damage. If a Fire Dragon Soul is attached to his primary sword, the first strike of his enhanced Basic Attack will deal 97 (48 + 30% physical attack) true damage while the subsequent two strikes will deal an equal amount of physical damage.
Skill use speed scales with Attack Speed.
skill1.name: Flaming Palm

skill2.description:
Ao'yin unleashes sword energy, dealing 180 (180 + 45% extra physical attack) physical damage to up to 3 targets within range (dealing 50% splash damage behind the targets), and recovering 150 (150 + 2.5% extra Health) Health upon hit.
Use of Downpour attaches 1 Water Dragon Soul to his sword, allowing him to recover 18 Health and 0.5% Mana from Basic Attacks. If a Water Dragon Soul is attached to both swords, he recovers 50% more. If a Water Dragon Soul is attached to his primary sword, his enhanced Basic Attacks will deal 97 (48 + 30% physical attack) physical damage each strike, for a total of 3 strikes. Landing a hit on the enemy recovers 150 (150 + 2.5% extra Health) Health.
Recovery effects are halved against non-hero units. Skill use speed scales with Attack Speed.
skill2.name: Downpour

skill3.description:
Ao'yin unleashes a wave of sword energy, gaining 30% Movement Speed (diminishes over time). He also deals 180 (180 + 45% extra physical attack) physical damage (with 50% splash damage) to up to 3 targets within range and knocks them back.
Use of Riding the Wind attaches 1 Wind Dragon Soul to his sword, granting him 16 Movement Speed. If a Wind Dragon Soul is attached to both swords, he gains an extra 50% Movement Speed. If a Wind Dragon Soul is attached to his primary sword, he will deal 97 (48 + 30% physical attack) physical damage and knock back the enemy with every strike of his enhanced Basic Attack, for a total of 3 strikes.
Skill use speed scales with Attack Speed.
skill3.name: Riding the Wind

skill4.description:
Ao'yin reveals his true white dragon form and soars into the sky for up to 4.5s, then dives forward. During this time, he is untargetable and ignores terrain, but cannot attack. He deals 400 (400 + 80% extra physical attack) physical damage to enemies in his path and slows them by 15%.
Upon landing, he deals the same amount of physical damage and applies Dread to nearby enemies for 1s. Targets afflicted with Dread will involuntarily move away from Ao'yin.
Ao'yin then unsheathes his True Dragon Sword, gaining 20% Attack Speed and 25 Attack Range, and the ability to attack up to two additional targets for 10s.
Ao'yin can switch his swords' elemental Dragon Souls while in flight.
Flight speed increases with his Ultimate's level.
skill4.name: Infinite Vastness

strategy.earlyGame: How trades go depends on who Downpour hits. Downpour restores Health on hit, but the healing is halved against non-hero units. Cast it from a spot where it also catches the enemy laner, and you can win back the damage you took. When clearing waves, cast skills to bank marks before the enhanced Basic Attack, which packs more strikes into a single swing. His skill damage scales with extra physical attack and his cast speed with Attack Speed, so while items are thin, don't force trades and put CS first.
strategy.midGame: From the mid game on, pick which Dragon Soul to carry for each situation. When you want to win a trade, cast Flaming Palm repeatedly and fight with the fire soul's true damage. When Health runs low, switch to Downpour and heal through the water soul, and when someone closes in, shove them off with Riding the Wind. Souls of the same element are prioritized when switching, and matching both swords to one element strengthens its effect. Once he learns it, Infinite Vastness flies over terrain, so it also works for circling behind a wall or escaping across one. He can switch souls in flight, so decide in the air what you want after landing.
strategy.teamfight: Ao'yin's job is to keep the damage flowing from behind the frontline. His secondary sword also strikes another nearby enemy, so with two enemies close together each Basic Attack hits both. Answer anyone who jumps on you with Riding the Wind and use the knockback to open space. Infinite Vastness gets more out of its post-landing window when cast after the enemy's dives have settled. The landing Dread only drives enemies away from him; it does not hold them in place. After landing, use the True Dragon Sword's extra range and targets to wear down whoever is in reach.

combos.title: Bank Marks, Then Swing
combos.sequence: Skill 3 (Riding the Wind: speed and knockback) → Skill 1 (Flaming Palm: grants an extra mark) → Basic Attack (enhanced, spending the marks)
combos.description: Flaming Palm grants one more mark than usual, so casting it after Riding the Wind lets him start the enhanced Basic Attack with his marks topped up. More marks mean more extra strikes, so the swing comes after both skills.

combos.title: Land, Then Cut With the Sword
combos.sequence: Skill 4 (Infinite Vastness: fly and dive) → Basic Attack (True Dragon Sword hits several enemies) → Skill 1 (Flaming Palm: rebuild marks)
combos.description: He cannot attack in the air but can switch his Dragon Souls, so set the elements you want before touching down. The landing Dread drives enemies away from him, but once the True Dragon Sword is out, his longer range and extra targets keep his attacks reaching them.

combos.title: Recover When Someone Sticks to You
combos.sequence: Skill 2 (Downpour: heals on hit) → Basic Attack (enhanced) → Skill 3 (Riding the Wind: knock them back)
combos.description: None of these skills move him, so this is a way to hold on through healing and pushing back rather than escaping. With a Water Dragon Soul on his primary sword, every hit of the enhanced Basic Attack restores Health as well. Riding the Wind ends it by shoving the enemy back, and the speed boost helps him reset the distance.

strengths: Downpour and the Water Dragon Soul let him restore Health from skills and Basic Attacks
His secondary sword also strikes another nearby enemy, so a second enemy standing close takes a hit too
Flaming Palm includes true damage, which gets through even on targets who stack defense
During Infinite Vastness he is untargetable and can move across terrain
weaknesses: Cast order changes what his enhanced Basic Attack does, and the wrong order leaves him without the effect he needs
No dash; his self-defense is limited to Riding the Wind's speed and knockback and Infinite Vastness
The Dread on landing pushes enemies away from him rather than holding them in place
His skill damage and cast speed scale with extra physical attack and Attack Speed, so his output is low before items

playstyle.style: The last two skills Ao'yin used decide which elemental Dragon Souls sit on his two swords. Depending on the soul on his primary sword, his enhanced Basic Attack gains true damage (fire), healing (water) or knockback (wind), so the order you cast in becomes the content of your next hit. While Infinite Vastness carries him into the sky he cannot attack, but he is untargetable and ignores terrain.
playstyle.suited: Every cast changes his swords' elements and his marks, so he suits players who like planning their cast order around what they want next. He can heal himself through the farm lane, but his skill damage and cast speed grow with items. Whether you can wait for those items while collecting CS also decides how well he fits you.

synergy.reason: Guiguzi pulls enemies in and holds them still, so Haya's Crescent Wave and Wayward Rays both land.
Nakoruru's charge slows the enemies it hits, so a hero Haya links to cannot walk out of Moonscape Mirage.

counters.reason: Arli blinks away and snaps back to her parasol, breaking Haya's Moonscape Mirage link.
Donghuang's suppression locks Haya out of Moonscape Mirage and her shield, leaving her no way out.

passive.description: Haya carries up to 3 moon crystals. Using Crescent Wave or Wayward Rays consumes 1 moon crystal. Once all are used, the skills enter full cooldown, and she gains an enhanced Basic Attack that fires 3 extra orbs, each dealing 50 (50 + 10% magical attack) magical damage. Targets hit by Crescent Wave or Wayward Rays will be marked, and hitting them again will trigger different effects.
passive.name: Moon's Farewell

skill1.description:
Haya unleashes a beam of moonlight forward, dealing 350 (350 + 75% magical attack) magical damage.
If the beam triggers a mark, the target also takes 100 (100 + 22% magical attack) true damage.
skill1.name: Crescent Wave

skill2.description: Haya unleashes 3 glazed orbs, the first dealing 120 (120 + 22% magical attack) magical damage, and the next 2 dealing 60 (60 + 11% magical attack) magical damage. She also gains a shield that negates 250 (250 + 40% magical attack) damage for 3s and gradually gains Movement Speed over the next 2s, maxing out at a 30% increase. If she hits marked enemies, they will be stunned for 0.5s. Subsequent hits will only inflict 50% of the stun effect.
skill2.name: Wayward Rays

skill3.description:
Haya links to a hero for 1.5s, gaining 50% damage reduction. The link breaks if they move too far apart, refunding 75% of Moonscape Mirage's cooldown. If the link remains unbroken after 1.5s, both enter the mirage, granting her a shield that negates 300 (300 + 70% magical attack) damage.
While inside the mirage, her skill cooldowns are reduced by 50%. If she uses Moonscape Mirage again while inside the mirage, she moves 700 units away from the target.
skill3.name: Moonscape Mirage

strategy.earlyGame: Her main poke is landing Crescent Wave's beam from as far away as it reaches, then hitting the marked target again to add true damage. While crystals remain she can chain Crescent Wave and Wayward Rays, but once they are used up both go on full cooldown. Wayward Rays comes with a shield and a speed boost, so keep one cast in reserve for escaping when the enemy jungler might be near. Until she has her ultimate, don't overextend; fight by turning back opponents who walk up to her with the marked stun.
strategy.midGame: Once she learns Moonscape Mirage, she can cut a chosen target off from their team. Move with your jungler and link enemies who come to take vision or a mid laner left alone. If the link holds, you both enter the mirage, and the shortened cooldowns let her pour Wayward Rays' stuns and Crescent Wave's true damage onto them. The link breaks with distance, so targets who have just used a movement skill are easier to keep tethered. Linking a sturdy frontliner can leave her unable to finish them inside, so choose carefully.
strategy.teamfight: Don't walk in from the front; stay behind your front line, hand out marks, and keep Wayward Rays' shield in reserve. When an enemy assassin dives your back line, link them with Moonscape Mirage and take them into the mirage, away from your allies. Recasting it inside moves her away from them so she can reset. On offense, stop an enemy who stepped too far forward with the marked stun from Crescent Wave and Wayward Rays, and finish them with your team. Her area damage is weak, so she does more by focusing one target than by firing into a crowd.

combos.title: Marked Stun Into the Enhanced Attack
combos.sequence: Skill 1 (Crescent Wave: apply the mark) → Skill 2 (Wayward Rays: stun the marked target) → Skill 1 (Crescent Wave: true damage) → Basic Attack (enhanced attack orbs)
combos.description: A mark only appears once Crescent Wave or Wayward Rays hits. Wayward Rays then stuns the marked target and Crescent Wave adds true damage. Those three casts use up the crystals, so the closing basic attack becomes the enhanced attack that fires orbs.

combos.title: Force a One-on-One in the Mirage
combos.sequence: Skill 3 (Moonscape Mirage: link) → enter the mirage → Skill 2 (Wayward Rays: apply the mark) → Skill 1 (Crescent Wave: true damage) → Skill 2 (Wayward Rays: stun)
combos.description: If the link holds, she and the target enter a mirage of their own. Skill cooldowns are shorter inside, so she can recast Crescent Wave and Wayward Rays quickly even after the crystals are gone. If the target breaks the link by moving away, most of Moonscape Mirage's cooldown comes back.

combos.title: Peel an Enemy Off an Ally
combos.sequence: Skill 3 (link to the enemy on your ally) → enter the mirage → Skill 3 (recast to move away from them)
combos.description: Linking Moonscape Mirage to an enemy who dove your back line reduces the damage she takes while linked, so she can take the hits instead. Once inside the mirage, that enemy is gone from around your allies, and recasting Moonscape Mirage moves her away from them to reset.

strengths: Marked targets take true damage from Crescent Wave and are stunned by Wayward Rays
Moonscape Mirage pulls one enemy into the mirage, cutting them off from their team
Wayward Rays grants a shield and a speed boost, so she can protect herself
Her skill cooldowns are shorter inside the mirage
weaknesses: Without a first hit to apply the mark, there is no true damage and no stun
Moonscape Mirage's link breaks if the target gets far enough away
Few skills hit an area, so wearing down a grouped enemy team is hard
Once the crystals are spent, Crescent Wave and Wayward Rays go on full cooldown

playstyle.style: Haya is a mage who spends three moon crystals to chain Crescent Wave and Wayward Rays, stacking true damage and stuns on marked targets. Once the crystals are used up, both skills go on full cooldown and her next basic attack becomes an enhanced attack that fires orbs. Her ultimate, Moonscape Mirage, pulls her and a linked target into a mirage of their own, where her skills come back faster.
playstyle.suited: You build each sequence while tracking how many crystals remain and who carries a mark. If you enjoy learning the routine of marking and picking off one target at a time, the speed at which she wears down a chosen target is rewarding. You also need to plan where to spend the wait after the crystals run out, so there is a fair amount to learn.

synergy.reason: Guiguzi pulls enemies together and stuns them, so Yao's Starlight Slice catches the whole group at once.
Sun Bin's speed boost lets Yao close the gap without spending Star Rush, keeping that dash in reserve.

counters.reason: Liang's suppression locks out Return to Dust, so the Star Reduction Yao has banked eats straight through his Health.
Donghuang's suppression shuts down Yao's casts, which also cuts off the passive healing those skills would bring.

passive.name: Gift of the Stars
passive.description: Yao recovers 70 (70 + 2% extra Health) Health when his skills hit an enemy unit, or half if they miss. Skill uses grant stacks of Star Power. At max stacks, enhances his next skill for 3s. Using the enhanced skill then enhances his next Basic Attack, letting him dash at the target and deal 100 (100 + 30% extra physical attack) physical damage.

skill1.name: Starlight Slice / Brilliance: Starlight Slice

forms.description: Yao spins quickly with his blade, dealing 425 (425 + 125% extra physical attack) physical damage to nearby enemies.

Yao spins quickly with his blade, dealing 425 (425 + 125% extra physical attack) physical damage to nearby enemies and enhancing his next Basic Attack.
Star Power mimics this skill, increasing his Attack Speed by 40% when both he and the stars hit a unit.

skill1.description: Yao spins quickly with his blade, dealing 425 (425 + 125% extra physical attack) physical damage to nearby enemies.

skill2.name: Star Rush / Brilliance: Star Rush

forms.description: Yao moves quickly to the left, dealing 180 (180 + 70% extra physical attack) physical damage to enemies in his path and slowing them by 25% for 1-2s.

Yao moves quickly to the right, dealing 180 (180 + 70% extra physical attack) physical damage to enemies in his path, slowing them by 25% for 1-2s, and enhancing his next Basic Attack.
Star Power will use this skill again from the left, launching units hit by both him and the stars for 0.75s.

skill2.description: Yao moves quickly to the left, dealing 180 (180 + 70% extra physical attack) physical damage to enemies in his path and slowing them by 25% for 1-2s.

skill3.name: Return to Dust / Brilliance: Return to Dust

forms.description:
Yao returns to his location 2s ago (up to 600 units), removes all Star Reduction, and deals 420 (420 + 140% extra physical attack) magical damage to enemies in his path and at the end point.
Passive: 40% of damage taken is converted into Star Reduction, only taking effect after 2s.

forms.skill_name: Enhanced Ultimate: Brilliance: Return to Dust
forms.description:
Yao returns to his location 2s ago (up to 600 units), removes all Star Reduction, deals 420 (420 + 140% extra physical attack) magical damage to enemies in his path and at the end point, and enhances his next Basic Attack.
Star Power mimics this skill, slowing units hit by both him and the stars by 25% for 2s.
Passive: 40% of damage taken is converted into Star Reduction, only taking effect after 2s.

skill3.skill_name: Return to Dust / Brilliance: Return to Dust
skill3.description:
Yao returns to his location 2s ago (up to 600 units), removes all Star Reduction, and deals 420 (420 + 140% extra physical attack) magical damage to enemies in his path and at the end point.
Passive: 40% of damage taken is converted into Star Reduction, only taking effect after 2s.

strategy.earlyGame: Yao fights through repeated short contacts in the jungle, using his passive that heals him whenever a skill hits. Touch the enemy with Star Rush's dash, land Starlight Slice's spin, then leave right away. Repeating this makes his Health drop more slowly than the enemy's. Keep an eye on Star Power: his skills are only enhanced for a short time at max stacks, so don't engage once the enhancement has run out. Once he learns Return to Dust, he can carry delayed damage and then remove it by returning to where he was a moment ago.
strategy.midGame: From the mid game on, he pushes side waves and picks up small fights by moving in and out. Starting from the enhanced Star Rush's launch sets up combos that take down fragile enemies. Return to Dust takes him back to where he stood a moment ago, so stepping on a safe spot before engaging is important. With a return point secured, even if the enemy jungler and support surround him, he can remove the delayed damage with Return to Dust and retreat. At the start of teamfights, hold his skills and go in with Star Rush only after seeing the enemy's targeted crowd control used on someone. Entering at max Star Power lets him press hard with enhanced skills and his dashing enhanced basic attack. Return to Dust is pointless if it lands him in the middle of the enemy team, so plan the path in as his way back.
strategy.teamfight: Ideally, keep moving in and out while staying healthy through skill-hit healing. Leave the front to his team's tank, enter from the enemy's flank with Star Rush and Starlight Slice, stack enhanced skills, then leave. Repeat this round trip again and again. If hard crowd control stops him, his delayed damage piles up and he is easily killed, so watch out for enemy stuns until the end. Using Return to Dust to attack leaves him unable to cancel the next round of damage, so take a breath before deciding when to use it.

combos.title: Pin Them Between the Stars
combos.sequence: Reach max Star Power → Skill 2 (Star Rush: enhanced, he and the stars rush from both sides) → Basic Attack (enhanced attack dashes at the enemy) → Skill 1 (Starlight Slice)
combos.description: The enhanced Star Rush sends Yao to the right while the stars rush from the left. Only enemies hit by both are launched, so engage near walls or in corridors where they cannot step sideways. The basic attack after an enhanced skill dashes at the enemy and leads straight into Starlight Slice's spin.

combos.title: Cancel Damage With Return to Dust
combos.sequence: Step on a safe spot → Skill 2 (Star Rush: dash and slow) → Skill 1 (Starlight Slice) → Skill 3 (Return to Dust: return to where he was and remove Star Reduction)
combos.description: Part of the damage he takes becomes Star Reduction and hits his Health later. Stepping on a safe spot before diving lets Return to Dust remove that damage as he returns. The return distance is limited, so diving too deep leaves him unable to get back to safety.

strengths: He heals every time a skill hits, so repeated short trades wear him down slowly
At max Star Power, enhanced skills and his dashing enhanced Basic Attack let him press hard
Returning with Return to Dust removes damage that would have hit his Health later
Star Rush's dash gives him mobility for both chasing and escaping
weaknesses: Each skill on its own hits modestly, so he needs to finish his combo to deal damage
Return to Dust always returns him to where he was a moment ago, so diving in without thinking can send him back into the enemy
When stopped by hard crowd control, he is easily killed before he can remove his delayed damage

playstyle.style: Yao is a jungler who heals on skill hits while building Star Power, then presses the attack with enhanced skills. Every skill use builds Star Power, and at max stacks his skills are enhanced for a short time, with Star Power repeating the same skill. His ultimate, Return to Dust, takes him back to where he was a moment ago and removes damage that would otherwise have hit his Health later.
playstyle.suited: He suits players who can think about where they will return to before engaging. Return to Dust only takes him back to where he stood a moment ago, so he needs to step on a safe spot before diving in. Enhanced skills are only available for a short time at max Star Power, so what decides it is whether you can engage without missing that window.

synergy.reason: Guiguzi camouflages the whole team, letting Shi open with Silk Imprint from the long range her passive rewards.
Huang Zhong cannot move in Turret Mode, so Shi drags enemies into the center where his shots hit hardest.

counters.reason: Zhuangzi's passive cleanses crowd control and grants immunity, so the hold from Shi's Silk Imprint does not last.
Sima Yi's silence cuts off the second tap of Silk Imprint, so Shi never completes the pull.

passive.description: Shi's skills deal more damage as the distance between herself and the enemy increases. For every 100 distance, the damage is increased by 5%, for up to 40%.
passive.name: Maiden's Trick

skill1.description:
Shi throws an artifact to the target location, dealing 120 (120 + 24% magical attack) magical damage to enemies in the area. Enemies are pulled toward the artifact, and 1 enemy is wrapped in Silk Imprint. The skill can be used again within 5s to pull that enemy a short distance while interrupting the enemy's skill use.
If the enemy is too far from Shi, they will not be affected. Silk Imprint deals double damage to non-hero units.
skill1.name: Silk Imprint

skill2.description:
Shi releases an energy orb that stops if it hits a monster. The energy orb attacks nearby enemies every 0.5s, dealing 160 (160 + 50% magical attack) magical damage. The first hit slows enemies by 15% for 1.5s. Subsequent hits on the same target only deal 25% damage.
The orb explodes after 2s, dealing 160 (160 + 33% magical attack) magical damage, and double damage to enemies at the center of the blast. The orb will move toward the target wrapped in Silk Imprint.
skill2.name: Silky Beauty

skill3.description: Shi enhances herself for 8s, gaining a greater field of vision and resetting Skill 2's cooldown. While enhanced, hitting an enemy with Skill 1 lets her manipulate their movements twice, and Skill 2's cooldown is reduced by 50%. She gains 50% Movement Speed for 0.5s when using this skill.
skill3.name: Sole Focus

strategy.earlyGame: Shi clears mid waves with Silk Imprint while looking to chip from long range. Silk Imprint deals heavy damage to non-hero units, so using it on minions is never wasted. Firing from the edge of her range makes her passive hit harder. She has few ways to protect herself up close, so avoid stepping too far forward.
strategy.midGame: While Sole Focus is active, her vision widens and an enemy hit by Silk Imprint can be moved twice. Casting it also resets Silky Beauty's cooldown and halves it while enhanced, so she can go from the catch to stacking orbs on her own. In standoffs before Tyrant or Overlord, her job is landing Silk Imprint from a river bush and dragging the enemy toward her team. Pull them diagonally back toward where your team's damage reaches, not straight toward herself. Pulling them straight in can leave her the first one they hit. Silk Imprint does not work on enemies who are too far away, so switch between the range for pulling and the long range where her passive grows. From behind the front line, she can also interrupt enemies winding up long skills with Silk Imprint.
strategy.teamfight: How much Shi contributes depends on whether she catches someone before the fight starts. Ideally, she catches a poorly positioned enemy with Silk Imprint and drags them into her team before the fight begins. Once it turns into a brawl, pull frontliners who dove your marksman away from them. Placing Silky Beauty where she drags them deals heavy damage to enemies at the center of the blast. Keep to the outer edge, far from the enemy group.

combos.title: Throw the Orb First, Then Catch
combos.sequence: Skill 2 (Silky Beauty: throw the energy orb first) → Skill 1 (Silk Imprint: pull and wrap one enemy) → Skill 1 (use again to drag them in a chosen direction)
combos.description: Throw the orb first, and once she catches someone it drifts to them and keeps dealing damage. Dragging the target to the center of the blast makes the explosion deal double damage to them.

combos.title: Move Them Twice With Sole Focus
combos.sequence: Skill 3 (Sole Focus: reset Silky Beauty's cooldown) → Skill 1 (land Silk Imprint) → Skill 1 (use again to move them, twice while enhanced) → Skill 2 (Silky Beauty)
combos.description: Sole Focus resets Silky Beauty's cooldown, and an enemy hit by Silk Imprint while she is enhanced can be moved twice. Use the first move to pull them out of formation and the second to carry them into your team's damage. While enhanced, Silky Beauty's cooldown is also halved, so her follow-up arrives in time.

strengths: Silk Imprint's pull can drag enemies out of their formation
Her skills deal more damage the farther away the enemy is, so she can chip from a distance
Silk Imprint can interrupt the enemy's skill use
Silk Imprint deals heavy damage to non-hero units, so she clears waves quickly
weaknesses: If Silk Imprint misses, she has no way to catch anyone until it is back
She has few ways to protect herself, and her passive does nothing once enemies are close
Enemies who are too far away are not affected by the pull, so managing range is hard

playstyle.style: Shi is a mage whose skills deal more damage the farther she is from the enemy. Silk Imprint pulls enemies toward her artifact and wraps one of them, and using it again drags that enemy a short distance in the direction she chooses. Silky Beauty's energy orb moves toward the target wrapped in Silk Imprint.
playstyle.suited: She suits players who enjoy keeping a long range while trying to peel one enemy away from their team. Silk Imprint does not affect enemies who are too far from her, so she has to find a position between the range where her passive grows and the range where she can still pull. The patience not to step forward after missing Silk Imprint is also essential.

synergy.reason: Menki brawls deep in the enemy line, so Missile Mayhem keeps finding fresh targets to mark.
Agudo's Furball stuns enemies in place, giving Meng Ya a still target to strafe down.

counters.reason: Mai Shiranui's dash launch interrupts Meng Ya mid-strafe, so his long channel never gets to finish.
Pei closes in with a dash and a shield, so Meng Ya loses the straight trade at close range.

passive.description:
For every 5% increase in Attack Speed, gains 1% Cooldown Reduction. Gains 5 Anger upon Basic Attack and skill hits (10 upon critical hits). At max Anger, enters the Excited state.
Excited: Enhances all skills and reduces the cooldowns of Awesome Barrage and Heavy Shot by 25%−50% while recovering (0−3 + 1% physical attack) Health for every 1 surplus Anger.
When not gaining any Anger for 3s, Anger will begin to diminish over time.
passive.name: Fiery Temper

skill1.description:
Uses the Apocalyptor to strafe continuously for 5s. Each bullet deals 87 (35 + 32% physical attack) physical damage. While strafing, he is slowed by 50. Enters cooldown after use.
Excited: Bullets have a piercing effect, dealing 50% damage to subsequent enemies. Firing speed is increased by 1% for every 2% Attack Speed, up to 100%.
Tap and hold to use. Damage can deal critical hits. Strafing can be paused temporarily to use other skills. Hits grant 5 Anger, while critical hits grant 10 Anger.
Every 2% Attack Speed increases skill casting speed by 1%.
skill1.name: Awesome Barrage

skill2.description:
Shoots a heavy round in the target direction, dealing 200 (200 + 50% extra physical attack) physical damage to all enemies hit and slowing them by 25% for 2s. When the round hits an enemy or wall, or reaches its maximum range, it explodes and splits into 5 splinters that can ricochet off walls and deal 410 (410 + 100% extra physical attack) physical damage to the first enemy they hit.
Excited: The number of splinters increases from 5 to 9.
Gains 5 Anger every time rounds or splinters hit an enemy. If multiple splinters hit the same target within 1s, subsequent hits only deal 25% damage.
skill2.name: Heavy Shot

skill3.description:
Meng Ya scans the vicinity and marks the locations of enemies within range when they take damage from his teammates (up to 5 locations can be marked). When the scan is complete, he fires missiles that deal 450 (450 + 120% extra physical attack) physical damage. Subsequent hits on the same target deal 75% less damage and grant 10 Anger. He continues to fire up to 1 missile every second for 8s after the scan. 50% of the skill's cooldown is refunded if the skill is canceled or interrupted.
Excited: The minimum interval between subsequent missiles is reduced from 1s to 0.5s.
The skill button can be held down for up to 3s to expand the scan range. He gains 50% Movement Speed while scanning.
skill3.name: Missile Mayhem

strategy.earlyGame: Meng Ya starts by building Anger with Basic Attacks and skills. In lane, bouncing Heavy Shot off a wall and chipping the opponent with the ricocheting splinters is the safe way to poke. With no movement skill, stay away from river-side bushes while you don't know where the enemy jungler is. Don't go into fights with an empty Anger gauge; start trades at full Anger.
strategy.midGame: As his attack speed items come together, his cooldowns shrink and his skills cycle faster. In fights over Tyrant and skirmishes, layer Missile Mayhem from the back. Enemies his teammates hit get marked and missiles keep falling, so he can join fights without stepping forward. Strafe with Awesome Barrage from behind and stay in the fight with the Excited state's healing. The August 13 update lowered Awesome Barrage's damage.
strategy.teamfight: Start by casting Missile Mayhem as the fight opens. Hold it to widen the scan and rain missiles on every enemy his teammates touch. After that, strafe with Awesome Barrage from the very back and keep his distance by landing Heavy Shot's slow on anyone who closes in. Excited Awesome Barrage bullets pierce, so he can chip enemies lined up in a row. He can pause strafing to use other skills, so slip Heavy Shot in right away when someone closes in.

combos.title: Ricochet Splinters Off a Wall
combos.sequence: Skill 2 (Heavy Shot: hit a wall to split into splinters, slow) → Skill 1 (Awesome Barrage: strafe)
combos.description: Heavy Shot explodes when it hits an enemy or a wall or reaches max range, splitting into splinters. The splinters ricochet off walls and each damages the first enemy it hits. Splinters landing on the same target within a short time deal less damage, so spreading them across several enemies does more than putting all of them into one.

combos.title: Turn Teammates' Attacks Into Damage
combos.sequence: Skill 3 (Missile Mayhem: hold to widen the scan) → teammates attack enemies in range to place marks → Skill 2 (Heavy Shot) → Skill 1 (Awesome Barrage)
combos.description: Missile Mayhem uses his teammates' attacks, not his own, as its trigger. When teammates attack enemies in range, those positions get marked, and after the scan, missiles keep falling for a while. He moves faster while holding the button, so he can set it up while backing off.

strengths: While Excited all his skills are enhanced, and surplus Anger restores Health
Attack speed turns into cooldown reduction and faster strafing, so attack speed items pay off directly
Missile Mayhem lets him support his team's fights from a distance
Heavy Shot's splinters ricochet off walls and reach several enemies in tight spaces
weaknesses: No movement skill, so he struggles to escape once enemies get close
His skills weaken without Anger built up, so he needs preparation before fights
He slows down while strafing with Awesome Barrage, making enemy skills harder to dodge
Missile Mayhem depends on his teammates' attacks and is hard to use alone

playstyle.style: Meng Ya is a marksman who builds Anger by landing hits, and when he enters the Excited state, all his skills are enhanced. The more attack speed he has, the shorter his cooldowns and the faster Awesome Barrage fires. While Excited, every point of surplus Anger also restores Health.
playstyle.suited: He suits players who enjoy stacking attack speed through items and watching their skills cycle faster. He has no movement skill at all, so he needs the care to settle his position before firing. Building Anger before engaging, so that he starts fights Excited, is also essential.

synergy.reason: Liang's suppression locks a hero in place, so Lam's Death From Below cannot be dodged at all.
Liu Shan's stun holds enemies still, letting Lam land Space Split and heal off the follow-up hits.

counters.reason: Arthur's silence shuts off both the submerge and the dash Lam lives on, and slowing Arthur only makes him heal faster.
Mozi stacks shields that soak Lam's opening burst, and his barrier stuns anything that tries to close in.

passive.description: When the enemy's Health drops below 30%, Lam will mark them as Prey. Lam's skills and Basic Attacks deal an extra 7.5-15% true damage to Prey.
passive.name: Hunter

skill1.description:
Lam submerges himself for 3s and gains 40 Movement Speed for 3s. After the duration expires, he returns to normal and 50% of the Cooldown is returned.
If he uses this skill again while submerged, he will burst out of the water and dash in the target direction, dealing 300 (300 + 120% extra physical attack) physical damage to enemies in his path and slowing them by 25% for 1.5s.
skill1.name: Wavebreaker

skill2.description:
Lam attacks nearby enemies and slices open their wounds, dealing 2 strikes of 235 (235 + 50% extra physical attack) physical damage and recovering 100 (100 + 1.5% extra Health) Health for every enemy hero hit (recovery is halved for non-hero units). He gains 1 mark when using the skill, and gains 1 additional mark every time a different enemy is hit, for up to 3 stacks.
While he has a mark, his Basic Attack is enhanced, consuming 1 mark to dash and deal 197 (70 + 75% physical attack) physical damage while recovering 100 (100 + 1.5% extra Health) Health. Each follow-up attack reduces the cooldown of this skill by 10%-20%.
When using this skill while submerged, he will dash in the target direction and reduce Skill 1's Cooldown by 25%.
skill2.name: Space Split

skill3.description:
Lam throws his dagger in the target direction, slowing enemies in its path immensely for 0.5s. After a short delay Lam dashes toward the dagger, dealing 520 (520 + 180% extra physical attack) physical damage and dragging enemies in his path along with him.
When using this skill while submerged, he will drag enemies to the dash destination, and Skill 1's Cooldown will be reduced by 50%.
skill3.name: Death From Below

strategy.earlyGame: Early on, Lam clears the jungle leaning on the healing from Space Split. It heals off monsters too, though healing from anything other than enemy heroes is halved. Wavebreaker's submerge raises his Movement Speed and gives back part of its cooldown when it ends, so it doubles as a way to travel between camps. When you go to gank, pick an enemy who has already lost Health in lane.
strategy.midGame: As skirmishes pick up, Lam is after two kinds of targets: enemies low on Health and enemies away from their team. Death From Below dashes him to the dagger, so throwing it deep into the enemy leaves Lam stranded among them. Keep the throw within a range where he can get back to his team after the dash. In standoffs before Tyrant or Overlord, wait for an enemy back-liner to step forward. After a kill, submerge and back off, then go in again once Space Split and Death From Below are ready, so he does not die right after.
strategy.teamfight: Lam does not need to be the first one in. After the enemy's crowd control goes onto your frontline, circle around the outside while submerged and drag one back-liner out with Death From Below. From there, build marks with Space Split and weave in the enhanced Basic Attack's dash and healing, taking down enemies marked as Prey first. The longer the fight runs and the lower everyone's Health falls, the more targets become Prey, so simply surviving the opening is what gives him damage later. If he is about to be surrounded one against three, slip out with the submerge and Space Split's dash and wait for the next target.

combos.title: Drag Them from Underwater
combos.sequence: Skill 1 (Wavebreaker: submerge) → Skill 3 (Death From Below: while submerged, drags enemies to the dash destination) → Skill 2 (Space Split: marks and healing) → Basic Attack (enhanced dash)
combos.description: Cast while submerged, Death From Below carries enemies in its path to the dash destination, so ending it near your team delivers the target right in front of them. It also shortens Wavebreaker's cooldown, so his way out comes back soon after the pull. Build marks on the target with Space Split and follow up with the enhanced Basic Attack's dash.

combos.title: Keep the Marks Turning
combos.sequence: Skill 2 (Space Split: build marks) → Basic Attack (enhanced: dash and heal) → Basic Attack (enhanced) → Skill 2 (Space Split)
combos.description: Space Split grants a mark just for casting it, and more when it hits different enemies. Each Basic Attack spends one mark and turns into a follow-up with a dash and healing. Every follow-up shortens Space Split's cooldown, so by the time the marks run out the next cast is close.

combos.title: Dive Out
combos.sequence: Skill 1 (Wavebreaker: submerge for speed) → Skill 2 (Space Split: dash in the target direction while submerged)
combos.description: When chased, submerge with Wavebreaker for Movement Speed, then cast Space Split while submerged to dash in the target direction. That dash shortens Wavebreaker's cooldown, and so does the submerge ending, so the next dive is not far off.

strengths: Enemies marked as Prey after losing Health take extra true damage from him
Space Split hits and enhanced Basic Attacks restore Health, so he holds up in brawls
Cast while submerged, Death From Below drags enemies in its path to the dash destination
Chaining the submerge and Space Split's dash lets him keep moving in the direction he wants
weaknesses: Death From Below dashes him to the dagger, so a bad throw leaves him alone inside the enemy team
He has to manage the submerge, marks and enhanced Basic Attacks all at once
Healthy enemies are not marked as Prey, so the extra true damage does not apply to them

playstyle.style: A jungler who closes out fights: the lower an enemy's Health, the easier Lam finishes them. Enemies who drop below a Health threshold are marked as Prey, and his Basic Attacks and skills deal extra true damage to them. He closes in submerged with Wavebreaker, drags targets with the dagger from Death From Below, and takes out wounded enemies one after another.
playstyle.suited: What decides it is whether you can read health bars and dive only onto targets that will become Prey. Submerging, Space Split's marks and his enhanced Basic Attacks all need tracking, and letting one lapse breaks the chain of dashes. If you would rather wait to come in behind a fight and pick off wounded enemies than trade blows head-on, he plays to that.

synergy.reason: Lady Zhen's launch and icicles pin enemies down, so Jing lands both her marks and shatters them.
Mai Shiranui's HISHOU RYUUENJIN launches the enemy, opening the window Jing needs to dive in with Reflective Assault.

counters.reason: Ata is immune to crowd control during Wavewalking, and he heals back much of what Jing chips off.
Daji stuns Jing in place while Captivate stacks strip Magical Defense, so the burst that follows lands clean.

passive.description:
Jing and her mirror image apply 2 different types of marks on enemies when they deal damage. If an enemy has both types of mark at the same time, the marks shatter, dealing physical damage equal to 4% of their lost Health and refreshing the Cooldown of Reflective Assault and Shattered Illusions. This effect has a cooldown of 5s (2s during the Ultimate).
The damage dealt and recovery provided by the mirror image is only 30% of her real body. The farther the image is from her real body, the greater the damage and recovery, up to 80% of the real body. The image only deals 10% of the real body's damage to towers.
passive.name: Lethal Reflections

skill1.description:
Jing dashes in the target direction, dealing 200 (200 + 100% extra physical attack) physical damage to enemies in her path and slowing them by 15% for 1.5s.
Her next Basic Attack is enhanced to deal an extra strike of 50 (50 + 15% physical attack) physical damage.
If no mirror image is present on the battlefield, one will be created for 2s, which dashes with her and replicates all of her actions except the Ultimate.
skill1.name: Reflective Assault

skill2.description:
Jing deals 160 (160 + 85% extra physical attack) physical damage to nearby enemies and gains a 50% Movement Speed boost that diminishes over 1s. Recovers 150 (150 + 2% extra Health) Health for the first enemy hit, and 25% of that value for each additional target hit.
If no mirror image is present on the battlefield, one will be created for 2s, which attacks with her and replicates all of her actions except the Ultimate.
—A skill practiced with Yao since they were children.
skill2.name: Shattered Illusions

skill3.description: Jing and her mirror image switch locations. Stocks 1 charge every 10s, up to 4 charges.
skill3.name: Dimensional Shift

skill4.description:
Jing flies forward, pulling enemies along her path with her. When she stops, she opens a Mirror Vortex and immobilizes the enemies at its center for 1s. She and her mirror image then move to either side of the vortex's central axis. While the vortex is present, she recovers 17 (10 + 4% physical attack) Health for every 0.05s spent dashing with Dimensional Shift. She gains 1 charge of shift if she deals damage to an enemy. The Mirror Vortex lasts 10s, during which Jing gains 10% damage reduction, but it will disappear if she leaves before then.
When the vortex is formed, 8 mirror fragments are generated along its border. When Jing or her mirror image deal damage to an enemy, the nearest mirror fragment will fly at the enemy, dealing 30 + 2% of the target's lost Health physical damage.
skill4.name: Mirror Domain

strategy.earlyGame: Jing starts by getting used to how her image works. While clearing, train the rhythm of matching marks with Reflective Assault and Shattered Illusions to reset cooldowns. Early ganks can chip a target down just by stopping them with Reflective Assault's dash and slow and stacking the image's attacks to match marks. Practice making the resets happen before forcing invades.
strategy.midGame: From the mid game on, her targets are isolated enemies in the enemy jungle or side lanes. Finish the cycle of matching marks and resetting cooldowns before they can hit back. Shattered Illusions heals the most from the first enemy hit, so swinging it only after getting all the way in lets her take the damage and healing and ride the speed boost out. Keep one Dimensional Shift charge for the way back so she can get out even after diving deep. Before Tyrant or Shadow Tyrant, going after the enemy support who comes to ward first frees up her team.
strategy.teamfight: Wait on the edge until her tank draws out the enemy's crowd control, then go in the moment their back line is open. Once the marks match and her cooldowns reset, swap with her image using Dimensional Shift to make the enemy's counterattack miss, then chase with the returned Reflective Assault. Mark shatters deal damage based on lost Health, so the later the brawl and the more wounded enemies there are, the faster she takes them down. Spend little time on full-Health tanks and keep targeting fragile enemies.

combos.title: Double Marks to Recast
combos.sequence: Skill 1 (Reflective Assault: dash and create an image) → Basic Attack (enhanced) → Skill 2 (Shattered Illusions: hit around her, speed up, heal on hit) → Skill 1 (Reflective Assault, cooldown reset)
combos.description: Jing and her image apply different marks, and when both are on the same enemy they shatter, resetting Reflective Assault and Shattered Illusions. Use the returned dash to keep chasing. Shatters have a minimum interval, which gets shorter while her ultimate, Mirror Domain, is active.

combos.title: Trap Them in the Mirror Vortex
combos.sequence: Skill 4 (Mirror Domain: fly forward dragging enemies and immobilize those at the center) → Skill 1 (Reflective Assault) → Skill 2 (Shattered Illusions) → Skill 3 (Dimensional Shift: swap with the image)
combos.description: Mirror Domain flies forward dragging enemies along and opens a Mirror Vortex where it stops, immobilizing those at the center. Each time Jing or her image deals damage, one of the mirror fragments along the edge flies at the enemy. Dealing damage inside the vortex also returns Dimensional Shift charges, but the vortex vanishes the moment she leaves it.

strengths: Matching both marks resets Reflective Assault and Shattered Illusions, adding more casts
Mark shatters and mirror fragments deal damage based on lost Health, making wounded enemies easy to finish
Dimensional Shift's swap lets her choose to keep attacking or get out in a single move
Shattered Illusions heals her from enemies hit, so she can hold her own in brawls
weaknesses: Without both marks, her cooldowns do not reset and her damage drops
The image deals less damage than her real body and only grows when kept at a distance
She is fragile, and crowd control after a predictable swap often kills her
Managing the image adds a lot of input, so she takes time to learn

playstyle.style: Jing is a jungle assassin who attacks with both her real body and her mirror image, matching two types of marks to reset her skill cooldowns as she fights. If no image is present when she uses Reflective Assault or Shattered Illusions, one appears briefly and copies every action except her Ultimate. Dimensional Shift swaps the positions of Jing and her image.
playstyle.suited: She suits players who enjoy a high-input style that includes thinking about where to put the image. The farther the image is from her, the more damage it deals, but if enemies read where she will swap to, she gets caught by crowd control, so varying the distance of her swaps each time matters too.

synergy.reason: Dr Bian's poison pool slows whoever stands in it, so Agudo's Tumble, Furball! is much harder to dodge.
Zhang Fei's shield covers Agudo, so she can stay on the front line and keep landing Basic Attacks.

counters.reason: Han Xin still holds a second leap once Agudo has spent her only roll, leaving her no way out.
Lam's Death From Below drags Agudo in, and once she is low the Prey mark adds true damage.

passive.description:
Agudo has an affinity with the monsters of the Gorge. When she's near a monster, Recovery will be replaced with Release (grants buffs).
Upon hitting enemies, Agudo's Basic Attacks will drop Seed Mines and absorb nearby mines: She can pick up mines to gain 3% Attack Speed and Movement Speed for 2.5s, for up to 6 stacks.
Enemies that come into contact with a mine will take 30 (30 + 10% extra physical attack) physical damage.
passive.name: Mountain Encounter

skill1.description:
Agudo sows a field in the target area, creating an animal wonderland that provides Agudo and her animal companions with 15% Attack Speed and Movement Speed, while granting 40 (40 + 0.6% extra Health) Health. Her animal companions will come to the field and fight alongside Agudo. Animal companions' stats scale with Agudo's hero level, while the chance of summoning more companions scales with skill level.
Animal companions gain additional Attack, Attack Speed, and Critical Rate based on 50% of Agudo's stats.
skill1.name: Wild Growth

skill2.description:
Tumble, Furball!: Agudo rolls forward with Furball, gaining 40 Block and immunity to 1 hard crowd control while rolling. Also deals 240 (240 + 80% extra physical attack) physical damage to any enemies she hits and stuns them for (1/2s). If they hit a wall before the end of the roll, they'll ricochet up to 3 times, resetting the rolling distance while increasing the skill's effect by 25%. Agudo also enhances her next Basic Attack to shoot 3 Seed Mines and deal 65 (65 + 21% extra physical attack) physical damage.
Tumble, Agudo!: Agudo rolls forward and enhances her next Basic Attack to shoot 3 Seed Mines and deal 65 (65 + 21% extra physical attack) physical damage.
skill2.name: Tumble, Furball!

skill3.description:
While riding Furball: Agudo commands Furball to leap to the target location, dealing 460 (460 + 150% extra physical attack) physical damage to enemies and stunning them for 2/3s. After that, Furball will battle independently while inheriting 50% of Agudo's stats and 100% of her on-hit effects.
While not riding Furball: When Furball is defeated, it will enter recovery mode. It can rejoin the battle after its Health is fully restored.
She can call Furball back before the skill duration ends.
skill3.name: Gorge Mobilization

strategy.earlyGame: Agudo clears while picking up the Seed Mines her Basic Attacks drop, keeping her attack speed and movement speed raised. Tumble, Furball! is immune to one hard crowd control, so even if she runs into the enemy jungler, she can make one escape. Her one-on-one strength is limited before the wonderland and companions arrive, so if an invasion seems likely, call your team instead of forcing it. When ganking, choosing a lane with walls to bounce the roll off makes the stun easier to land.
strategy.midGame: In fights over Tyrant or Overlord from the mid game on, lay the Wild Growth wonderland first, then fight alongside the companions it calls. In skirmishes too, start by placing the wonderland. Sending Furball with Gorge Mobilization lands an area stun from a distance, but only open fights with it when your front line is in place. If Furball is defeated it cannot fight until its Health is full again, so stay near your team and keep shooting rather than pushing a far lane alone. The August 27 update shortened Furball's Basic Attack interval and made it speed up with Agudo's attack speed.
strategy.teamfight: Lay the Wild Growth wonderland in advance where the fight is likely to happen. Only Agudo and her companions benefit from it; allied heroes get nothing. Even so, the companions it gathers stand in front of the enemy, so the extra bodies turn directly into pressure. When the enemy engages, reposition with Tumble, Furball!, and save Furball from Gorge Mobilization as the finishing move to throw in the moment an enemy back-liner is isolated.

combos.title: Bounce Off a Wall
combos.sequence: Skill 2 (Tumble, Furball!: charge with immunity to one hard crowd control, stun on hit) → bounce off a wall → Basic Attack (enhanced: three Seed Mines)
combos.description: Rolling while riding Furball moves her forward with immunity to one hard crowd control. Hitting a wall bounces them back, resetting the roll distance and strengthening the skill, so targeting enemies near walls lands more hits. The enhanced Basic Attack that follows fires three Seed Mines, and enemies take damage just by touching the mines she scatters.

combos.title: Lay the Wonderland, Then Send Furball
combos.sequence: Skill 1 (Wild Growth: create the wonderland and call companions) → Skill 3 (Gorge Mobilization: send Furball to leap and stun) → Basic Attack (scatter Seed Mines) → Skill 3 (cast again to call Furball back)
combos.description: Laying the wonderland first raises the attack speed and movement speed of Agudo and her companions and restores Health. Sending Furball at the enemy with Gorge Mobilization then deals damage and stuns on landing, after which Furball fights on its own. If things turn dangerous, cast it again to call Furball back.

strengths: Wild Growth calls animal companions, letting her fight with more bodies
Tumble, Furball! charges in immune to one hard crowd control and stuns the enemies it hits
Sending Furball with Gorge Mobilization lands an area stun from a distance
Picking up Seed Mines raises her attack speed and movement speed, speeding up her clears
weaknesses: While separated from Furball, her roll has no stun or crowd control immunity, so she struggles to protect herself
If Furball is defeated, it cannot rejoin until its Health is fully restored
Before her wonderland and companions are in place, her one-on-one pressure is modest

playstyle.style: Agudo is a jungle marksman who fights alongside the monsters she befriends. Animal companions gather in the wonderland she creates with Wild Growth and fight with her, and she can either roll in while riding Furball or send Furball leaping at enemies with her ultimate to fight on its own. Her Basic Attacks drop Seed Mines when they hit, and picking them up raises her attack speed and movement speed.
playstyle.suited: She suits players who want to choose on the spot between fighting while riding Furball and sending it off to fight separately. Agudo herself is less protected after Furball leaves, so she needs the habit of checking the walls and teammates she can retreat to before sending it. The fine control of picking up Seed Mines while moving also affects how many attacks she gets out.

synergy.reason: Luban No.7's scattershot only hits enemies caught in a straight line, and Sakeer's launch pins them in place.
Bai Qi amplifies the healing he receives, and Sakeer's fireflies always chase the lowest-Health ally, usually him.

counters.reason: Liang's circles hold vision over the brushes, so Sakeer's next hop is read before he takes it.
Wukong's Protective Shroud simply absorbs Mulberry Power, the one cast Sakeer's setup depends on.

passive.description:
Sakeer's Basic Attack deals melee damage and summons a firefly that deals 100 (100 + 20% magical attack + 3% extra Health) magical damage to enemies and exposes them for 3s. Sakeer also periodically restores 50 (50 + 10% magical attack + 1.5% extra Health) Health to the nearby teammate with the lowest Health.
When there are no enemies nearby, charging his Basic Attack recovers 50 (50 + 10% magical attack + 1.5% extra Health) Health. He will stop restoring Health to teammates while charging.
passive.name: Firefly Protection

skill1.description:
Sakeer channels Luminescence to the target area, dealing 500 (500 + 10% magical attack) magical damage to enemies and launching them for 1s. Luminescence is consumed on hit, dealing 100 (100 + 20% magical attack + 3% extra Health) magical damage per stack. If there are teammates nearby, Luminescence instead heals the teammate with the lowest Health, restoring 50 (50 + 10% magical attack + 1.5% extra Health) Health per stack.
Luminescence: He gains 1 stack every 1.5s, for up to 9 stacks. The skill's range increases with the number of stacks.
skill1.name: Mulberry Power

skill2.description:
Sakeer flies to the target brush, gaining 1 stack of Luminescence and releasing a number of fireflies depending on how far he flies. After 1s, the fireflies fly to the nearby hero with the lowest Health. If the hero is an enemy, the fireflies deal 100 (100 + 20% magical attack + 3% extra Health) magical damage and expose them for 3s. If the hero is a teammate, they restore 50 (50 + 10% magical attack + 1.5% extra Health) Health.
This skill stocks up to 3 charges. Tap it to fly to a brush in front of him without aiming.
skill2.name: Ride the Wind

skill3.description:
Sakeer summons an Illuminating Brush at the target location. He can use this skill again within 6s to fly to the brush and gain a stack of Luminescence.
Illuminating Brush: 1s after the brush has been summoned, it releases fireflies at up to 5 nearby heroes every second. Every firefly deals 100 (100 + 20% magical attack + 3% extra Health) magical damage to enemies, or restores 50 (50 + 10% magical attack + 1.5% extra Health) Health to teammates.
Enemies that step into this brush will have their location revealed. After a while, the Illuminating Brush will stop releasing fireflies and turn into a regular brush that lasts for 30s.
skill3.name: Firefly Fields

strategy.earlyGame: Sakeer's first job is guarding his marksman and scouting bushes at the same time. His passive healing and fireflies work on their own, so standing in the right place is itself his support. Ride the Wind holds up to three charges, so deciding in advance which are for river scouting, escaping and joining ganks keeps him from hesitating.
strategy.midGame: Once he learns Firefly Fields, place the Illuminating Brush at the entrance to the fight before contests over Tyrant or skirmishes. Fighting around it makes things easier for his team thanks to the fireflies and vision. To join a gank, fly ahead with Ride the Wind to a brush on the enemy's escape route and place Mulberry Power's launch on their way out. The August 13 update lowered his passive's healing.
strategy.teamfight: Before the fight, place the Illuminating Brush, then fly with Ride the Wind to a brush near his back line and build Luminescence while waiting for the fight to start. Meet enemy dives with Mulberry Power's launch, and keep his team's Health up with firefly healing through the brawl. His own damage is low, so there is no need to chase or push forward. Staying alive turns directly into healing, so move between bushes the enemy cannot reach.

combos.title: Build Up, Then Meet Them
combos.sequence: Skill 2 (Ride the Wind: fly to a brush and gain Luminescence) → Skill 1 (Mulberry Power: launch enemies in the area)
combos.description: Mulberry Power launches enemies in the area and deals extra damage for each stack of Luminescence. If a teammate is nearby, the same stacks heal the teammate with the lowest Health instead. More stacks also widen the area, so slip in a Ride the Wind flight just before to extend its reach.

combos.title: Block the Path With the Illuminating Brush
combos.sequence: Skill 3 (Firefly Fields: grow the Illuminating Brush) → Skill 3 (cast again to fly to it and gain Luminescence) → Skill 1 (Mulberry Power: launch)
combos.description: A moment after it grows, the Illuminating Brush sends fireflies at nearby heroes every second, damaging enemies and healing teammates. Enemies who step into it are revealed. For a short time he can cast again to fly there himself, then hold Mulberry Power ready to launch anyone who comes in.

strengths: He covers healing, a launch, vision and exposing stealth on his own
Ride the Wind and Firefly Fields let him hop from brush to brush
The Illuminating Brush lets him hold and scout the area in front of objectives
Fireflies fly to the lowest-Health teammate automatically, keeping the healing going
weaknesses: Until Luminescence builds up, Mulberry Power's range and damage are small
In open areas with few brushes, he has fewer places to fly to
His own damage is low, and he has few answers to repeated hard crowd control
Away from teammates his healing goes to waste, so he is not suited to moving alone

playstyle.style: Sakeer is a support who moves from brush to brush sending out fireflies, scouting enemies and healing teammates. The fireflies from his Basic Attacks damage enemies and expose them, and his passive periodically heals the nearby teammate with the lowest Health. His ultimate, Firefly Fields, grows an Illuminating Brush at the target location that keeps releasing fireflies.
playstyle.suited: He suits players who want to support fights through vision and positioning. Fireflies hand out the healing automatically, so his main decisions are which brush to stand in and when to fire Mulberry Power's launch. Luminescence builds over time, so he also needs the patience to wait until just before casting.

synergy.reason: Mai Shiranui's launch freezes enemies in place, letting Charlotte's enhanced Basic Attack land in full.
Guiguzi pulls enemies into one stunned clump, so Charlotte's Power Gradation catches several of them at once.

counters.reason: Arthur's silence breaks the Follow-Up chain Charlotte relies on, and her own slow only speeds his healing.
Arli's Autumn Storm knocks Charlotte away, cutting short the close-range pressure Charlotte needs to build.

passive.name: SPLASH GRADATION
passive.description:
All of Charlotte's skills are considered Initial Skills. When any of her skills hit, the next different skill she uses will be enhanced to a Follow-Up Skill and she will gain 1 mark for 4s, for up to 5 stacks.
Upon reaching 3 stacks, her next Basic Attack is enhanced into the Follow-Up Skill SPLASH GRADATION, where she dashes toward the target and strikes 7 times, each strike dealing 121 (80 + 25% physical attack) physical damage while also slowing the enemy by 10%. The final strike deals extra physical damage equal to 12% of the target's lost Health. While launching an enhanced Basic Attack, she gains 21%-35% damage reduction.
Follow-Up Skills place 1 stack of Maim on enemies hit, reducing the enemy's Attack Speed by 10%-20% for 4s, for up to 2 stacks. Enemies lose 1 stack of Maim every time they use a Basic Attack.

skill1.name: TRI-SLASH

forms.description: Initial Skill: Charlotte unleashes TRI-SLASH in the target direction, and after a short delay, deals 366 (200 + 100% physical attack) physical damage to enemies in her path. If TRI-SLASH hits an enemy, she gains a 80% Movement Speed boost that diminishes over 2s.

Follow-up Skill: Charlotte quickly unleashes TRI-SLASH in the target direction, and after a delay that's shorter than that of the Initial Skill, deals 475 (260 + 130% physical attack) physical damage to enemies in her path. If TRI-SLASH hits an enemy, she gains a 80% Movement Speed boost that diminishes over 2s.

skill1.description: Initial Skill: Charlotte unleashes TRI-SLASH in the target direction, and after a short delay, deals 366 (200 + 100% physical attack) physical damage to enemies in her path. If TRI-SLASH hits an enemy, she gains a 80% Movement Speed boost that diminishes over 2s.

skill2.name: SPLASH FOUNT
